“the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will, and setteth up over it the basest of men.” It does not matter who you vote for; he puts whoever he wants. Donald Trump is one of the basest of men, a caricature and TV personality from The Apprentice, just as Ronald Reagan was an actor. His orange skin is telling you what he is about: he is Esau, the red man. The Most High puts these men over us so we can see: you wanted the other nations to rule over you besides me, and this is what happens.

Deuteronomy 17:14 shows that desire in our people: “When thou art come unto the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, and shalt possess it, and shalt dwell therein, and shalt say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me”. We are not satisfied with the King of kings and Lord of lords, Christ, being over us. We always want to be like the other nations. That is why we dye our hair blonde, put in the contacts, put on the suit and tie, go to their universities and get their education, and assimilate to their way of life.

But the law says “Thou shalt in any wise set him king over thee, whom the Lord thy God shall choose: one from among thy brethren shalt thou set king over thee: thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother.” We have to have a king of our own people, who is for our people, not a base man out for the interest of corporations that rob and steal our resources. We are not supposed to vote for other nations to be over us. Thus saith the Lord.

The same goes for our people in Latin America. In Mexico and in Argentina, where an Italian was set up, what are they doing for you? Nothing, not a damn thing. You cannot set up people of other nations over you. That is why the Most High sets the basest of men over Israel: to show us what it means to choose a stranger over the king he chose.

Deuteronomy 28:37 says Israel would become “an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations”: called by names outside of our God-given name. God gave us a name. Israel means prince of the power with God, and there is no mightier name on the face of the earth. Why would you want to call yourself a Latinized negro, a Latino? That is a racist term. You have to do the history and get the knowledge; you have to find yourself so you don't lose yourself.

Isaiah 65:15 says the same: “And ye shall leave your name for a curse unto my chosen.” We left the name Israel for a curse, for racist terms like Latino, Hispanic, and names like Cuban, Colombian, Venezuelan, Dominican. Yet it is “unto my chosen”: we are God's chosen people. You have to see the greatness in who you are. We have fallen so far that we think we can't come out of it, but we are coming out, because there is a God.

“for the Lord God shall slay thee”. For wanting a king of another nation over us, for wanting to assimilate, the Most High slew us and caused the basest of men to rule over us. “and call his servants by another name”: now we are called Latino, blacks, spics, wetbacks, illegal aliens. That is why we do not know who we are, a confusion of faces. We are searching, but we are not searching the scriptures.

So-called Latinos, you are the Israelites. Latino is not your given name; your name is Israel, the twelve tribes of Israel. You think this is a black movement, a negro movement, but the twelve tribes of Israel are mainly so-called Latinos. We have to get back to our history and our true nationality.

Moses blessed the tribes “before his death”, and of Asher he said “Let Asher be blessed with children; let him be acceptable to his brethren, and let him dip his foot in oil.” Asher is Venezuela, Colombia, Peru, Brazil, from Colombia down to Uruguay. When the conquistadors came to conquer, rob and pillage, many fled into the jungles of the Amazon and grew up without fathers, so they must be made acceptable to their brethren, and we have to go there and save our people in the jungles. And the oil: a brother in Venezuela, asked how Venezuelans and Colombians can benefit from their precious resource, stood right on the oil. The oil is the precious commodity the red man covets so earnestly.

Then verse 25: “Thy shoes shall be iron and brass.” Look up the name Brazil: it is associated with the Hebrew word barzel, meaning iron. It is not a coincidence that the name Brazil means iron in Hebrew; these people know where our people are. Brazil is full of iron, Colombia is full of iron, Venezuela is full of iron, Ecuador is full of iron. Mexico has iron too, but not the same abundance as South America.

“and as thy days, so shall thy strength be.” That is the inheritance of our people in these lands. It is not a coincidence, the names these countries get, for those who do not believe that the northern kingdom is the northern kingdom.

The elders in the 60s and 70s deciphered this without Google or the internet; all they had were the scriptures and history books. Now, in the information age, it is so much plainer. Asher's blessing, children, oil, iron and brass, sits right where the Bible said it would.

Esau has to be revealed. The devil has to be revealed, and the scriptures reveal him by his attributes. “And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.” Red is a warning: when you see the red man coming, destruction and death are coming, so flee. He is red and hairy, so much that they shave nearly the whole body to normalize their appearance. Jacob is not even described, because he looked like his parents. “Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people”: we are not the same, and no matter how hard we try we cannot be like them. “Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field”, a predator who loves to kill and prey; “Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents”, simple, living off the land and doing our sacrifices to God.

Then Esau begged, “Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father.” His blessing: “thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above; And by thy sword shalt thou live”. How would he get the fatness of the earth? By the sword: by armies, killing, destroying and preying on other nations. That is what we see on the news.

Then, “and shalt serve thy brother”: he was meant to serve Israel, Jacob’s sons. But “and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck”. He broke the yoke and is over us now, because we wanted to be like the other nations and wanted a king; God is a jealous God, and he cursed us with the basest of men over us.

His dominion is the pale horse: “his name that sat on him was Death, and Hell followed with him. And power was given unto them over the fourth part of the earth, to kill with sword, and with hunger, and with death, and with the beasts of the earth.” Hell follows him to Libya, Iraq, Iran, Venezuela, Cuba and Panama. The fourth part of the world is America, as their own book on the birth of America calls it, which is why they call this hemisphere theirs, the Monroe Doctrine become the Donroe Doctrine. With hunger: Cuba starved out by cut-off oil and sanctions. With the beasts of the earth: zoonosis, mixing animal DNA. He is the Chaldeans’ daughter, “that bitter and hasty nation, which shall march through the breadth of the land, to possess the dwellingplaces that are not theirs”, with some 850 military bases in other people’s lands. If Esau is not the devil, if they're not the wicked, then who is? The Arabs don't have military bases on every land.

Daniel says, “through his policy also he shall cause craft to prosper in his hand”: economic warfare and the witchcraft of a dollar with no gold behind it, which is why he went after Gaddafi’s African gold and Venezuela trading outside the dollar. And “by peace shall destroy many”, with peace summits led by the biggest warmongers on earth. Yet Daniel says, “but he shall be broken without hand”. Christ “shall destroy them without labour by the law”, which is why keeping and teaching God’s laws matters: the foolishness of preaching is destroying this kingdom from within. And no amount of money can hide the man of sin; he is being revealed, “that he might be revealed in his time.” The devil must be revealed in his time, through the words of the prophets and through us teaching his laws.

“in their affliction they will seek me early.” Why do we have to get deported? So that we seek God early. A lot of our people think this is the American dream, this is what life is about: get a house, get a car, barbecue on the weekend, watch sports, send your kids to college. No, that is Esau's way of life. This is death, this is oppression, and the Most High has to afflict us to remind us that this is not our rest.

Micah says it: “Arise ye, and depart”. Separate yourself from these heathen nations, these strangers, the real aliens. “for this is not your rest”. You were not brought here on slave ships to be comfortable, to assimilate, or to be friends with these heathen nations. You see the betrayal time and time again when you make a league with the strangers. “Our necks are under persecution: we labour, and have no rest”: we work and we have to watch our backs for ICE agents who come to our places of business and our homes, arrest us and kidnap our children.

“because it is polluted”: wicked, evil, deceptive. Witchcraft is in this place, so bad that it has you bleaching your skin, blonding your hair, putting in contacts, starving yourself. “it shall destroy you”: it destroyed Sammy Sosa, Serena Williams, Lil' Kim. Those are the celebrities Esau upholds so our people look up to them and want to be like them. It is witchcraft to make a black man hate himself so much that he destroys his own face.

“even with a sore destruction.” Destruction is coming to this place; this kingdom is not going to last forever. We are in the last days, so we have to get our minds right and our spirits right. There is much work to be done, especially for you so-called Latinos: Judah has shown us the way, and now it is our turn. When you see a head of state like Nicolás Maduro kidnapped and his country's resources stolen, that is for you to wake up. Seek his face, and see in the scriptures that he looks just like us.

“Remember, O Lord, what is come upon us: consider, and behold our reproach”: see the curses that fell upon us for our sins. “Our inheritance is turned to strangers, our houses to aliens.” The Chicago mayor was offended by the term alien, but the term is in the scriptures. The aliens are the strangers, the other nations. We are not the aliens; we are the natives of these lands. Esau has taken our lands, our resources, our inheritance.

“We are orphans and fatherless.” Why are we orphans? Deuteronomy 28:32: “Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people.” We see it all throughout history, and even now our northern kingdom children are separated from their parents. They killed our fathers, our leaders, the caciques and kings like Atahualpa, and burned them at the stake for not accepting the Christian religion. That is why the Asher in the Amazon grew up orphans and fatherless.

“and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day long”. You will look to the white Jesus, but he can't save you. Donald Trump is not going to save you. The US government is not going to save you. No matter how much you perfect your English, the accent is going to slip out and they are going to catch you.

“and there shall be no might in thine hand” to save our children. We saw ICE agents, grown men with weapons and body armor, surrounding a five-year-old autistic girl and holding her hostage: a nation of fierce countenance. How much plainer can it be?

So-called Latinos, you have to see yourselves in the scriptures. You are no different from your black brothers, from Haitians, Jamaicans and African Americans; we are the same people, oppressed together. All these curses have to afflict you so that you can see this is your book, and what is happening to you for turning your back on the black Messiah, Jesus Christ. We have to return to our true nationality.

We gave the hand to the Egyptians “to be satisfied with bread”: if I work hard, if I send my children to their school, if I learn English, I can assimilate; if I work hard for the white man, I've made it. No. Lamentations 4:17: “As for us”, as for Israel, “our eyes as yet failed for our vain help”. Our lying help. Esau is not here to help us; they have deceived us.

“in our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save us.” They don't want no parts of us, and they can't save us, no matter how hard we try. Look at the Latinos who stand with Trump: look how Donald Trump looks at him like he is a dumbass, and the other one is not even looking at him, because he is a clown. They despise you. They just use you to deceive your people and to betray your people.

Just because they let one get through, one Diddy, one Jay-Z, and give him millions, that is chump change compared to the destruction caused when our people are led astray into thinking this is the way of life, that this is our kingdom, that we can assimilate.

There is none that doth deliver us out of their hand. Hugo Chavez couldn't do it, Fidel Castro couldn't do it, Maduro couldn't do it, even with Russian helicopters and Chinese spyware; his Cuban guards went back to Cuba in little boxes. No man can save us. Our job, brothers and sisters, is to keep God's commandments and the faith of Christ. That is our power. When we do that, the Most High and his angels will fight for us, and we must see ourselves in these scriptures, no longer as blacks or Latinos but as one people, one nation.

“We have given the hand to the Egyptians, and to the Assyrians”: the Egyptians and the Assyrians represent the oppressor. Who is our oppressor today? Our main oppressor is Esau. How do we know? “Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom, that dwellest in the land of Uz”. Edom is the so-called white man; that is his biblical name.

“the cup also shall pass through unto thee”: that cup of affliction, that cup of oppression, is going to pass unto them. “thou shalt be drunken, and shalt make thyself naked.” His evil is being revealed. This is the beginning of that; we have not seen nothing yet.

Read on: “The punishment of thine iniquity is accomplished, O daughter of Zion; he will no more carry thee away into captivity”. Our punishment is coming to an end. We are not going into slavery anymore; this one here in America is our last and final captivity. Now it is time for us to wake up and rise up like God's army that we are.

“he will visit thine iniquity, O daughter of Edom; he will discover thy sins.” God is going to judge Esau for the evil they have done to his people. Everything this devil does is going to be revealed, and his judgment for it. So the hand we have given to the oppressor for bread is the hand of Edom, and the cup he made us drink is passing to him.

“Servants have ruled over us: there is none that doth deliver us out of their hand”. Who is ruling over us? Servants. The Most High made Esau to serve us, but we are serving them now.

Look at the statue they took down: Theodore Roosevelt on horseback, with a Native man and an African man walking beside him. They took it down, but it is too late; they know who they are and they know who we are. Roosevelt represents Esau, the servant. Now watch the scripture come to life: “I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth”. The horse represents authority, power and rulership. The princes walking on foot are Israel, the northern kingdom on the left and the southern kingdom on the right, walking as servants.

Esau knows who he is, and he knows this is his time to rule. But it is coming to an end. There is none that can deliver us out of their hand, not Hugo Chavez, not Fidel Castro, not Maduro with Russian helicopters and Chinese spyware. No man can save us. Our power is to keep God's commandments in the faith of Christ; when we do that, the Most High and his angels will fight for us. We have to see ourselves in these scriptures, no longer as blacks or as Latinos, but as one people, one nation.

“Our fathers have sinned, and are not; and we have borne their iniquities”. Their sins are our sins. Why? It goes back to Exodus 20:5: “Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them”. We cannot serve idols: Christianity, white Jesus. “for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me”.

Our fathers “are not”: they are dead and gone. But the Most High visits their sins to the third and fourth generation, so we take on those sins. Basically, we are our fathers.

That is why Lamentations goes straight on to “Servants have ruled over us”. We bowed to other gods, and a jealous God gave us over to be ruled by the nations. The ones in our own communities who lead our people into thinking we can assimilate, that this is our kingdom, are leading us deeper into it. Our fathers watched for a nation that could not save us, and we are still doing it. The way out is not to serve their idols but to come back to the God who visits the iniquity.

“Servants have ruled over us: there is none that doth deliver us out of their hand.” Esau knows who he is and knows this is his time to rule, but it is coming to an end: servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth. None can deliver us. Hugo Chavez could not do it. Fidel Castro could not do it. Maduro could not do it, even with Russian helicopters and Chinese spyware. The 32 Cuban bodyguards around Maduro went back to Cuba in little boxes, mini coffins draped with the Cuban flag. A head of state snatched out of his fortress in three hours or less, with no casualties on the American side.

So we cannot expect a man to save us from this wicked, demonic people. The small groups picking up arms against them are agitation, agents provocateurs setting us up for failure. Where do you get your bullets? You have no factories. You would have to go to your enemy for the weapons to use against him. Our power is keeping God's commandments and the faith of Christ; then the Most High and his angels fight for us.

The Lord speaks to Esau: “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence.” These things: destroying my people, putting yokes of iron on their necks, having them hate themselves and their people. He says, “thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself.” Because God did not bring swift judgment, since he was punishing us for our iniquities, Esau thought God was with him, thought God looked like him. No, Esau. God is a black God. Jesus Christ is a black God.

Then: “but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.” The Most High will reprove Esau for the evil he has done to our people, and set Israel in order before his eyes. They call us whatever they want: Power Rangers, LA Lakers, spics in purple and gold. We may seem harmless, but we are God's army, his chosen people rising up.

While Esau is busy stealing land and resources, the Most High is setting us in order, giving us time to get our minds, spirits, families and children right: coming out of drugs, drug dealing, gangs, alcoholism, prostitution and selling our people out. No longer blacks and Latinos as separate nations, but one people, one nation.
“Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people”. Your body is a house; that is the house you live in. Set your life in order, brother, with God's laws, statutes and commandments, and then you can reprove and teach your people. And the Most High has set men over us to do that very work.

“And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.” Our leadership is wise, brothers and sisters; the Lord set them over us for a reason. They teach the people knowledge: how to overcome, how to lead ourselves in the way of righteousness.

Set in order many proverbs: that is what we do when we go over precepts. There are a lot of proverbs we read and don't understand, and leadership puts the puzzle together and sets them in order so you can understand the things of old. “The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and that which was written was upright”. They search out what the people need and what they are going through. Sometimes they step on toes, just to wake you up or break the chain you have been fighting with.

So God did not leave us without help. When we go off, he set up brothers and sisters to guide us back home. You can never say God did not send help; the one who ignores it is caught up in stupidity.

The Lord told Ezra to “comfort such of them as be in trouble”, and that comfort comes out of the scriptures: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” That which was written was upright, and we have to understand it and follow it. That's the pattern.

That is where our hope comes from. When we look at the history of our forefathers, whatever they went through, brothers and sisters, is what we are going to go through, so we are not shocked at what is going on. And it is the same in the body: the Captain went through it, I can go through it; the Deacon went through it, I can go through it; the sister went through it, I can go through it. That is the comfort that keeps us from giving up.

So don't give up. No matter what, stand up. This profession, made before many witnesses, is all we have; some of us have twenty years and more in this truth. Where can we go? This is our life. Don't let Satan take it away from you, and don't give it up for Babylon's money; Babylon will destroy your soul. Set your house in order, revive your own soul first, and then revive your people.

The Lord God says, “let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves.” And: “Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities like as a field is covered over with bushes.” Brothers give up their position because of the affliction, the little tribulation, or because of their bills, two hundred-some thousand dollars of debt. How could you be that stupid, that ignorant? We all have bills. That is all you have. Their sin is wearing them down so much, and they are so covered with it that they cannot see the brotherhood right in front of them.

David asks the question every one of us has to answer: “Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? or who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?” You have to stand up.

The evildoers are where we are today. Taking a man out of his country and bringing him back to America: the same America that pushes democracy, when democracy put him there, kidnaps him and charges him with unjust judgment. Is that just, or wicked? If it is hard for you to see that America is evil, it is because you are evil yourself. Everything here is a work of iniquity; they push sin everywhere, even in a little karate flick.

Christ said, “I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world.” Have the word of God and the world will hate you, and your family will hate you. “I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil.” He left us in the world because we have a path to go through: from Adam until now it has been good against evil, and our job is to stand for what is right. “Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.”

The stony ground “immediately receive it with gladness”, but has no root, and when affliction arises “immediately they are offended.” What have you given for this truth? Many would wish to sit in a class learning they are the children of Israel, and many will die today without that chance. While you are alive, you still have it. So who will rise up and stand? Do not let your sins weigh you down.

Christ sent Paul “To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins”. These are the people we are fighting for. Our job is to open the eyes of our people and bring them back to the light, to the commandments, and to the knowledge of who God is: Christ is a black man, he died only for the nation of Israel, and he will return for Israel alone.

Our people are in a state of darkness, and Paul says what that state is: “And you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins; Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world”. Our people are dead because they destroyed themselves by breaking God's commandments. They are in a state of death, without conscience, bound by Satan. Whatever the world offers, that is what they follow after.

So when you look at your mother, your uncle, your auntie inside these religions, they are bound by Satan. That is why a sister who separates from her husband and goes to her mother's house, her aunt's house or a friend's house in the world is making Satan's move. What is your mom going to teach you? She is not awake out of this dark place. Leaving a sister in the truth to live with an aunt in the world is a good chess move by Satan, and if you're not wise you won't catch it. Go to the believers who can guide you, teach you and build you up.

Will Smith reached the end of money and fame and found it could not make him happy: a man in pain, crying for help, whose soul is damaged. That is the course of this world. The dead must be quickened, and the pattern to follow is the fruit of the Spirit, meditating in the word, fasting and praying, and examining yourselves whether ye be in the faith.

Babylon's destruction comes “in a moment in one day”, and the Lord gives the reason: “for the multitude of thy sorceries, and for the great abundance of thine enchantments.” There was sorcery used upon our people in America, and then America used that same thing on all the nations.

That is why your uncle and your auntie won't repent after you accepted Christianity. That is witchcraft, used to keep you in the state of mind you are in. It is the pattern of every captivity: from the Assyrian captivity to the Babylonian, from the Medes and the Persians to the Greeks and to Rome, and now we are in America. All the nations have always used enchantments and witchcraft against us to keep us in darkness, and Satan is dealing with them.

The word enchantment means magic, witchcraft, sorcery, wizardry, necromancy, conjuration, hypnotism, mesmerism, voodoo, charms, spells, incantations, mojo. Remember coming out of Egypt, when the magicians were doing their things? Those magicians are who call themselves scientists today, with different titles under that name. They are the witches of this earth. Hypnotism is like the movie Get Out: our people have been sinking, and it is time to help them come out. America did not use only words against us. It used every witchcraft and every voodoo it could find, and the Catholic church is part of that foolishness.

Then the Lord dares them: “Stand now with thine enchantments, and with the multitude of thy sorceries, wherein thou hast laboured from thy youth.” America has been dealing with the devil from its youth up. “If so be thou shalt be able to profit, if so be thou mayest prevail.” The Lord is saying: since you have practiced these things from your youth, let me see if you will prevail against me. Let me see if that little nuke, that robot that is half a man, all that witchcraft and all the media you have through the earth, can stop what I am bringing into this earth.

We saw it when America was trying to attack and the Lord raised up a storm that destroyed helicopters and airplanes. They don't understand the prophecy. These things are already written, and no man can change them. The nuclear weapons every nation holds are not going to sit on a shelf like extra paint; an ICBM can reach Washington in under half an hour, and what Isaiah and Jeremiah spoke of exists in our time.

That is why we are out here teaching and telling our people to repent. We see what is coming. The same way God destroyed the first world with a flood, he is going to destroy this world with fire, and no sorcery or weapon can stop what God has written.

Why do we have to keep the book of the law in our mouth and meditate on it day and night? Because of the work of Satan. Peter shows it: “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”.

Your adversary doesn't sleep. You think Satan sleeps for a minute? He does not sleep, brothers. When you know the enemy and know his job, you understand the scripture more. The book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth because Satan is like a devouring lion waiting to get your soul, waiting for you to come off the commandments.

James 1:14 already showed where the fight is: “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” When you are drawn away of your own lust, you are not in control; the lust is in control of you. So take every little thing as a big thing, because Satan is well alive here.

That is why the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty must continue therein, not a forgetful hearer but a doer. It is easy for us to go left, so we have to constantly put ourselves in the works. Either you are about it or you are not, and you cannot just be cool to everything while the lion is walking about.

James says the blessed man is the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty and continues therein, “not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work”. Joshua says the same thing another way: “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night”.

Ask yourself, brothers and sisters: are you meditating in this book they call the Bible? Don't lie to yourself. If you have to ask, it means you need to do it more, because it is supposed to be a natural thing.

Why meditate on it day and night? Because we want to keep the ministry blameless, and because we know the job of Satan: he is like a roaring lion, waiting to get your soul, waiting for you to come off the commandments. When you meditate on something day and night, you have no time for foolishness. It is like the scriptures warning not to be idle, because when you are idle you fall back into sin. When you are constantly in the scriptures, your mind is focused on keeping the commandments. That is the pattern: stay focused.

The enemy is at work every day. Turn off the TV and the phone and you might have a two or three percent upper hand, but as long as these devices and human beings exist on this earth, our battle is serious and we are battling every day.

Joshua goes on: “that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous”. That is James 1:25 again. The perfect law of liberty is what we look into: the commandments, the mercy of God, the grace of God. Christ died on the cross and gave us that grace as the platform to build upon, so we can no longer go backwards; now we have to go forward. The one who is not a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work “shall be blessed in his deed”, blessed in his teaching and his business, whatever he does.

The enemy does not sleep, and Revelation shows what he is doing: “And I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night.”

Satan isn't sleeping day and night. He is accusing us day and night as we study, trying to accuse us before the Lord. So we don't have time to be idle. We have to keep our minds focused, brothers. Y'all sleep on the devil if you want.

He is at work through this world too. They are trying to change times and laws and make people think that what is immoral is moral. The mind of the sinner says don't judge me and don't snitch, but the one living in sin influences others and destroys others. That is why the laws of God are important.

This is why James 1:25 calls us to look into the perfect law of liberty and continue therein. The accuser works against us before God day and night, so we must meditate in the law day and night and be doers of the work, so that we are blessed in our deed and the ministry stays blameless.

Solomon was knocked down, and David, the man after the Lord's own heart, was knocked down. Did they stay down? No. We are not in the business of staying down; we get knocked down and keep going. Satan tells us to stay down, and some brothers and sisters want you to stay down, but that is not what God said. “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” That is what God is looking for.

So what do we pray when Satan knocks us down? David prayed it: “Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me.” We pray that the Lord does not remove his Holy Spirit from us, because that is what keeps us standing.

“Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.” You have to look at the truth with a joyful and glad heart, because you cannot live without it; it is part of your system, your life. Where else can you go? We do not give up our position; we pray that the Lord keeps strengthening us.

“Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.” When we get back up, our job is to teach, because we have been through the trial and tribulation and understand what it takes. We go right back to the business we left off, teaching our people their transgressions so they do not fall into what we fell into. Do we give that up to go sit on the couch, or sit in the back and puff up on evil?

Nobody sees the prayer, the crying at night, the tears when you are home alone thinking, I could have done better. That is the broken and contrite heart God will not despise. Tell Satan to bring it on. With a position or without it, be the same: a trooper. And when a brother is knocked down, do not applaud it; fast and pray for him, because he is still fighting the same battle you are, and your sin may just not be revealed as quickly as his.

“In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah began Hoshea the son of Elah to reign in Samaria over Israel nine years”. Ahaz, wicked and weak, was over Judah, and Hoshea was over Ephraim, the northern kingdom. Hoshea “did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, but not as the kings of Israel that were before him”.

“Against him came up Shalmaneser king of Assyria”. This is Pul’s son. In 1 Chronicles 5 it was Pul, Tiglath-pileser, who came first and took Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh; now his son Shalmaneser comes and does the most. The northern kingdom was not taken all at once. It was done in waves: one group taken out here, some of Reuben, some of Asher there, until almost all of Ephraim was out of the land.

Hoshea became his servant and paid him, then conspired against him: “he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and brought no present to the king of Assyria”. He tried to align himself with Egypt to defy Assyria, so the king of Assyria bound him in prison, “went up to Samaria, and besieged it three years”, and “carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes”. That is modern day Iran, bordering Russia. From there our people kept migrating further and further east: the northern kingdom became Scythians, moving from Iran into Russia, some as far as China, some as far as Japan, where they became samurai.

Why it happened: “the children of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God”, and they “did secretly those things that were not right”. They thought God wasn’t watching; he saw it all. They built high places in every city, “rejected his statutes, and his covenant”, “followed vanity, and became vain, and went after the heathen”. So “the Lord was very angry with Israel, and removed them out of his sight: there was none left but the tribe of Judah only”. Yet “Judah kept not the commandments” either, and “the Lord rejected all the seed of Israel”. God was done with all twelve: the northern kingdom into captivity, and Judah next.

Then the land was filled with heathen: “the king of Assyria brought men from Babylon, and from Cuthah, and from Ava, and from Hamath, and from Sepharvaim, and placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the children of Israel”. The Lord sent lions to kill them for their evil, so a priest was brought back to teach them “the manner of the God of the land”, how to sacrifice so they could stay in the land in Ephraim’s absence. “Howbeit every nation made gods of their own, and put them in the houses of the high places which the Samaritans had made”. The northern kingdom was called Samaritans because Samaria was their capital, and these heathen sacrificed in the very high places Ephraim made for their idols. And “the men of Babylon made Succoth–benoth, and the men of Cuth made Nergal, and the men of Hamath made Ashima”.

So the carrying away in 1 Chronicles 5:26 was the start of this: God himself stirred up the kings of Assyria against the tribes that went whoring after other gods, and the northern kingdom was broken and scattered, with strangers set in their place.

Solomon fell in love with heathen women, the very nations of which the Lord said “Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods”, and they did. He built a high place for Chemosh for his Moabite wife and for Molech for his Ammonite wife, and did the same for all his strange wives. So the Lord was angry with Solomon, and the prophet Ahijah “rent it in twelve pieces” and told Jeroboam, “Take thee ten pieces”: the kingdom would be rent out of the hand of Solomon’s son, with one tribe left for David’s sake.

Sirach sums up what Solomon left behind him when he died: “Thus rested Solomon with his fathers, and of his seed he left behind him Roboam, even the foolishness of the people, and one that had no understanding, who turned away the people through his counsel.” Rehoboam was an idiot. He did not listen to the elders; he listened to the friends he grew up with, and by his counsel he turned the people away.

“There was also Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, and shewed Ephraim the way of sin”. Jeroboam, the mighty man of valor Solomon made ruler over the house of Joseph, plotted against Solomon to rush the prophecy, fled to Egypt, and came back to take the ten tribes. And he showed Ephraim the way of sin.

So the heart Solomon gave to his strange wives bore its fruit in the next generation: a foolish son on the throne of Judah, a king who led Ephraim into sin, and the kingdom divided in two. That is where the dividing hatred between the houses begins.

“Now for a long season Israel hath been without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law.” That is the northern kingdom: they stopped going to Jerusalem to worship, and Jeroboam set up idols for them. So when Asa gathered “all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon”, the northern tribes are called strangers. And “they fell to him out of Israel in abundance, when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.” Whenever Judah was on point, Ephraim would follow along.

The next king shows the same thing. Jehoshaphat, a good king of Judah, reigned from 870 to 848 BC. “And Jehoshaphat dwelt at Jerusalem: and he went out again through the people from Beer–sheba to mount Ephraim, and brought them back unto the Lord God of their fathers.” Who dwelt at Beersheba? Simeon: that was Simeon’s allotment of land. From Simeon’s land all the way to mount Ephraim, Jehoshaphat caused some of Ephraim to return back to the Lord.

“And he set judges in the land throughout all the fenced cities of Judah, city by city, And said to the judges, Take heed what ye do: for ye judge not for man, but for the Lord, who is with you in the judgment.” “Wherefore now let the fear of the Lord be upon you; take heed and do it: for there is no iniquity with the Lord our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of gifts.” Jehoshaphat was a righteous king, and he set the law back in place.

So Israel was without God, without a teaching priest and without law, and the Lord would always use Judah to bring Ephraim back in, every single time. When Judah was on point, Ephraim followed along; when Judah went off, Ephraim went even worse off.

David was anointed more than once, and it starts here in Bethlehem: “Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of the Lord came upon David from that day forward.” Samuel anointed him in the midst of his brethren, and the Spirit of the Lord stayed on him from that day.

After Saul was dead, David went up to the cities of Hebron, and the men of Judah came and anointed David king over the house of Judah. So he was anointed again in Hebron, but only over Judah; he was the king of Judah in Hebron.

Then all the tribes came: “Then came all the tribes of Israel to David unto Hebron, and spake, saying, Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh.” They remembered that “when Saul was king over us, thou wast he that leddest out and broughtest in Israel”, and that the Lord had said, “Thou shalt feed my people Israel, and thou shalt be a captain over Israel.” So “they anointed David king over Israel.” Now he is king over all twelve. “In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months: and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah”: both kingdoms. And “David took the strong hold of Zion: the same is the city of David.” Zion is the city of David.

But the beef was already there before the split. In 2 Samuel 19 the men of Israel asked, “Why have our brethren the men of Judah stolen thee away”; Judah answered, “Because the king is near of kin to us”: he is our tribe. Israel said, “We have ten parts in the king, and we have also more right in David than ye”: there are more of us than you, why can't we anoint him over here? “And the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.” Judah cursed Ephraim out, and that enmity between the two stayed.

Ephraim felt more entitled, and in a way rightfully so: Joseph saved Israel from starvation in Egypt, Joshua of Ephraim brought us into the land and gave out the allotments, and Ephraim held Shiloh, Bethel and the first places of worship. So the anointing that began in the midst of David's brethren is also where the dividing hatred between Judah and Ephraim shows itself, a rivalry that went on long after David.

Peter saw “a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners”. A vessel knit at the four corners. Remember the Lord told Jacob his children would be scattered abroad to the north, east, south and west. Hosea says what that vessel is: “Israel is swallowed up: now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure.”

A vessel wherein is no pleasure means unclean, no good, unable to be used. Vessels were used in the temple for service, but a vessel in which there is no pleasure cannot be used for temple service; it is deemed unclean. That is Israel scattered among the nations, counted unclean.

So the vessel full of “all manner of fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air” is Israel scattered to the four corners and swallowed up among the Gentiles. Peter said, “Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean.” But “What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.” It is not talking about no damn animals; it isn't about pork.

At Hezekiah's Passover many of Ephraim and Manasseh, Issachar and Zebulun “had not cleansed themselves”, yet Hezekiah prayed, “The good Lord pardon every one That prepareth his heart to seek God”, and “the Lord hearkened to Hezekiah, and healed the people.” Cornelius, of West Manasseh, was a devout man who prepared his heart to seek God. God cleansed that vessel of no pleasure, and Peter learned he “should not call any man common or unclean.”

The sheet Peter saw was “knit at the four corners”, and Isaiah shows why: “And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.”

The nations here are Israel. He will assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather the dispersed of Judah, as Hosea said, from the four corners of the earth. A vessel knit at the four corners: that is Israel scattered to every corner, and the Lord gathering them.

That is what the vision meant. Peter doubted in himself what it should mean, thinking what Christians think, that he was told to eat unclean food. But he saw it three times, and three men came from Cornelius. Then he understood: “God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.” The vision was about a man, Cornelius, one of the outcasts of Israel from the northern kingdom whom Judah called common and unclean.

What God hath cleansed, call not thou common: the Lord is gathering both houses, the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah, and making them clean, one nation again, as Ezekiel said, “neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”.

Where is Cornelius from? Some people say Italy. He is from Cesarea. There are three Caesareas: one in Africa, which is not written of, Caesarea Philippi, and Caesarea Maritima. Cornelius is from Caesarea Maritima, the place the maps call Strato's Tower, right under Dor, in Samaria, the same country where Christ spoke to the woman at the well. When Rome colonized our land they named it for Caesar, and Maritima because it is a port on the water. And the maps mark that land West Manasseh.

Somebody will say that's just a map, it ain't in the Bible. So here it is in the Bible, for the doubters: “And the coast of Manasseh was from Asher to Michmethah, that lieth before Shechem; and the border went along on the right hand unto the inhabitants of En–tappuah.”

Read on. “Now Manasseh had the land of Tappuah: but Tappuah on the border of Manasseh belonged to the children of Ephraim”. The coast went down to the river Kanah: “the coast of Manasseh also was on the north side of the river, and the outgoings of it were at the sea”. “Southward it was Ephraim’s, and northward it was Manasseh’s, and the sea is his border”: the Mediterranean Sea. Peter dwelt in Joppa and went some thirty to forty miles up the coast to Caesarea Maritima, just before Dor.

Then verse 11: “And Manasseh had in Issachar and in Asher Beth–shean and her towns, and Ibleam and her towns, and the inhabitants of Dor and her towns”. Under Dor was Caesarea Maritima; that was all Dor before. Endor, Taanach and Megiddo were Manasseh's too. “Yet the children of Manasseh could not drive out the inhabitants of those cities; but the Canaanites would dwell in that land.” There were too many of them to conquer them all.

So that is Manasseh's land. It is called West Manasseh because Manasseh also dwelt on the other side of Jordan, East Manasseh. This was once Manasseh's allotment right under Ephraim, the sons of Joseph. Asher shared that port, but the land was Manasseh's.

Cornelius was not Italian. He was of the Italian band, a unit of the Roman army. There were Israelites in Rome's military, just as there are Israelites in America's military today. But negroes love master so much they see the word Italian and get excited: yes, he's white, I knew it. No, he was of the Italian band, from Caesarea, West Manasseh, one of the northern kingdom. A centurion was over a hundred men. He was “A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway”, the exact same thing Tobit said he did.

Peter said, “Ye know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation”. Sound familiar? It is the same thing the woman at the well said to Christ: the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans. “but God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean”. Any man, not food, not animals. The vision was about a man, Cornelius.

Who is one of another nation? In Genesis 35 Jacob was told a nation and a company of nations would come of him. Ezekiel shows the two becoming one: “And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”. Judah and Ephraim, both the houses, gathered together under one king.

“Neither shall they defile themselves any more with their idols, nor with their detestable things, nor with any of their transgressions: but I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God.” He will cleanse both kingdoms and make them clean.

So Cornelius was of another nation, another kingdom: the northern kingdom. Judah called the northern kingdom common and unclean, not my people, strangers. But what God hath cleansed, that call not thou common. God promised to cleanse them and make the two one nation, and that is why Peter could go into Cornelius's house.

Peter said, “Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.” In every nation, because Israel is in every nation. Luke shows it at Pentecost: “And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.”

Israel is scattered everywhere, to all four corners: that is the vessel knit at the four corners in Peter's vision. So “in every nation he that feareth him” is not every people on earth; it is the Israelites scattered in every nation who fear God and work righteousness, like Cornelius, a devout man who feared God with all his house and gave much alms.

And read the next verse; they always skip it. “The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ”. The word was sent to the children of Israel. Those accepted in every nation are the children of Israel in every nation.

Peter told Cornelius, “To him give all the prophets witness, that through his name whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins.” Isn't that what Cornelius was receiving? Joel is one of the prophets giving that witness: “And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be delivered”.

That word whosoever again. But where is the deliverance? Not in all the heathen nations: “for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as the Lord hath said, and in the remnant whom the Lord shall call.”

The whosoever is the remnant whom the Lord shall call. Peter said to Cornelius, “That word, I say, ye know”: the Samaritans and the northern kingdom knew it, as Isaiah said Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria shall know, and as the woman at the well said, I know that Messias cometh. Cornelius was devout; he knew the law and that he would be called eventually. He was of that remnant.

“Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people”. The Lord God of Israel visited and redeemed his people, not every people.

Read on to verse 77: “To give knowledge of salvation unto his people by the remission of their sins”. To whom? Unto his people. Remission of whose sins? Their sins.

So the word Peter brought to Cornelius was for the remission of their sins, and that includes Cornelius too. “in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him” because Cornelius was one of his people, an Israelite of the northern kingdom in West Manasseh, whom the Lord God of Israel came to visit and redeem. Acts 15 says it: “God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name.” That visit, beginning with Cornelius, is the building again of the tabernacle of David, all twelve tribes reunited.

Amos warns Ephraim, “seek not Beth–el, nor enter into Gilgal”, for “Beth–el shall come to nought.” These were places built for worship by Abraham and Jacob, and Ephraim turned them into seats of idolatry. So Gilgal would surely go into captivity, and Beth–el would be destroyed. “Seek the Lord, and ye shall live; lest he break out like fire in the house of Joseph”: the house of Joseph is Ephraim.

Jeremiah turns the same judgment on Judah: “But go ye now unto my place which was in Shiloh, where I set my name at the first, and see what I did to it for the wickedness of my people Israel.” Go look at Shiloh and see what I did to it. “I spake unto you, rising up early and speaking, but ye heard not; and I called you, but ye answered not”: they refused the prophets.

“Therefore will I do unto this house, which is called by my name, wherein ye trust, and unto the place which I gave to you and to your fathers, as I have done to Shiloh. And I will cast you out of my sight, as I have cast out all your brethren, even the whole seed of Ephraim.” What was done to Ephraim will be done to Judah: the heathen come in, destroy the sanctuary and lead them captive. The exact same way. The same thing happens to both houses, both kingdoms. He raised up Assyria to overthrow Ephraim, and he raised up Babylon to overthrow Judah.

And they would not hear it. Amaziah the priest of Bethel, one of the low-level priests raised up that was not Levi, told Amos, “go, flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there: But prophesy not again any more at Beth–el: for it is the king’s chapel”. Go teach Judah; you are disturbing the king's church. Amos was blitzing the churches. But the Lord said to him, “Go, prophesy unto my people Israel.” The Lord always sent his prophets to his people, and his people alone, to repent. It is the same with Jacob today: the one preaching the word of God is called a troublemaker.

So Bethel came to nought as Shiloh did, and Israel went “into captivity forth of his land”: their wives made harlots, their sons and daughters fallen by the sword, their land divided by line as it is to this day, dying “in a polluted land”. That began with the northern kingdom, but eventually it happened to all of us as a whole.

“When Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob, and sent him away to Padan–aram, to take him a wife from thence; and that as he blessed him he gave him a charge, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan; And that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother”, Esau, seeing “that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father”, went his own rebellious way anyway. “Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham’s son”. That is how Ishmael and Esau started intermingling, and that is where the light-skinned Arabs come from.

Jacob went toward Haran, and at a certain place he dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven, “and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it.” The Lord promised, “the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed; And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south”. That is all four corners: before they were even born, it was prophesied that Jacob’s seed would be found in the four corners of the earth, scattered among the families of the earth, “and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.” And the Lord promised, “I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.”

Jacob said, “this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven”, a portal to paradise. He set up his stone for a pillar, poured oil on it, “And he called the name of that place Beth–el: but the name of that city was called Luz at the first.” He vowed the tenth, the tithe.

Keep Bethel in mind. On the map it sits right under Shechem, the place where Abraham first built an altar in Canaan and where Rehoboam was later crowned. These early holy places all lay in the land that would become Ephraim’s.

The division between Ephraim and Judah did not begin at the split of the kingdom; it was building long before. Part of it goes back to Joseph, the father of Ephraim.

Joseph was raised up to tell Pharaoh what was coming: “Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt: And there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land”, and “it shall be very grievous”. “And for that the dream was doubled unto Pharaoh twice; it is because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.” Joseph prophesied the famine and showed Egypt how to prepare for it, and by it Israel was saved when Jacob and his sons ran down to Egypt.

The same pattern ran through Abraham. After the Lord told him, “Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house”, he came from Ur of the Chaldees beyond the Euphrates, up to Haran, and down into Canaan, the stretch called the Fertile Crescent. When famine struck Canaan, Abraham ran to Egypt too, just as Jacob and his house later did. The parallels line up.

So Joseph’s house carried a great deal: Joseph saved Israel in the famine, and later Joshua, of Ephraim, divided the land. That is part of why Ephraim felt more entitled than Judah, and why the rivalry that tore the kingdom in two was already there long before Rehoboam.

“And the whole congregation of the children of Israel assembled together at Shiloh, and set up the tabernacle of the congregation there. And the land was subdued before them.” From there each tribe received its allotment of land.

On the map, the hill country of Ephraim holds Shiloh, Ai, Shechem at the top, and Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal, where the law’s blessings and curses were received. Bethlehem and Jerusalem lie further down, in Judah. All of Israel’s earliest places of worship were in Ephraim’s land: Abraham’s first altar at Shechem, Bethel, the mountains of the law, and the tabernacle at Shiloh.

So Ephraim felt entitled. They had the places of worship, the historical landmarks, and they were more in number than Judah. That is where the beef started, the buildup of the dividing hatred.

It broke open with Rehoboam. “And Rehoboam went to Shechem: for all Israel were come to Shechem to make him king”, crowned at the very place of Abraham’s first altar. Solomon had laid a heavy yoke of taxes on the people to build sanctuaries of heathen worship for his wives. The old men who had served with Solomon said, lift it and they will serve you forever; Rehoboam “forsook the old men’s counsel” and listened to the young men he grew up with: “my father also chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.” It was so “for the cause was from the Lord”, to fulfill what Ahijah the Shilonite told Jeroboam when he tore the garment into twelve pieces and gave him ten.

Israel answered, “What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David.” They stoned Rehoboam’s tax collector, and made Jeroboam king. Only Judah, with Benjamin at its side, followed the house of David. When Rehoboam gathered an army, the Lord said, do not fight your brethren, “for this thing is from me.” The split was the Lord’s doing, and its roots ran back to the land at Shiloh.

“Jesus the son a Nave was valiant in the wars, and was the successor of Moses in prophecies, who according to his name was made great for the saving of the elect of God”. This is Joshua. He fought for us to gain the land and possession promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, “taking vengeance of the enemies that rose up against them”, the ones who did not belong in the land, “that he might set Israel in their inheritance.” Joshua was used to set us in our promised land through war, as David did later as king.

Joshua 8 shows him valiant in the wars. At Ai, when the men of the city looked back and saw the smoke of their city rising to heaven, “they had no power to flee this way or that way”, and Israel smote them until none remained: twelve thousand fell that day. “And the king of Ai he hanged on a tree until eventide”, and they raised a great heap of stones over him at the gate.

“Then Joshua built an altar unto the Lord God of Israel in mount Ebal”, “an altar of whole stones, over which no man hath lift up any iron”. All Israel, “as well the stranger, as he that was born among them”, stood “half of them over against mount Gerizim, and half of them over against mount Ebal”, and there they received the blessings and the cursings of the law.

Ebal and Gerizim, like Ai, Bethel and Shechem, are in Ephraim’s land. And Joshua himself was of Ephraim. The one who set Israel in their inheritance and divided the land came from that tribe, which is part of why Ephraim felt so entitled.

Hosea's children were for signs. His daughter Lo-ruhamah means no mercy: “I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away”, which is Assyria overthrowing Ephraim so that it would be not a people. Then his son: “Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” When you are not God's people and he is not your God, what does that make you? A Gentile, a heathen, a stranger, a non-Israelite. Judah read this and said, good, the hell with Ephraim; they ain't his people no more, they're Gentiles, and we can't deal with them.

But Hosea goes straight on: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” When they were told they were Gentiles, it would be said to them, no, you are not Gentiles; you are God's people.

Judah forgot this. Judah said, you guys are Gentiles forever. But Hosea says eventually you have to come together again: “Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head”. That one head is Christ, and they are delivered together, united as one. Chapter 2 says the same: “I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy; and I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my God.” Judah just took a black highlighter and covered that part, because they were evil and stupid.

The same thing is in Chronicles. The northern kingdom was “without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law”, because Jeroboam set up idols in Dan and Shiloh so they would not go south to worship in Jerusalem. That is why they were called strangers: King Asa “gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon: for they fell to him out of Israel in abundance, when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.” Whenever Judah was on point, Ephraim came in. The Lord always uses Judah to bring Ephraim back, and the strangers, the not my people, turn out to be the sons of the living God.

Sennacherib came against Hezekiah and mocked his God, and one angel of the Lord went forth and smote “in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.” One angel killed 185,000 soldiers in their sleep. Judah was saved without bow or sword, just as Hosea said. “So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh”, and his own sons smote him with the sword while he worshipped in the house of Nisroch his god. He went home pissed off, and Tobit shows what he did.

Tobit was “of the tribe of Nephthali”, led captive in the time of Enemessar, which is the Greek form of Shalmaneser the fifth, out of “Nephthali in Galilee above Aser.” He is northern kingdom, carried to Nineveh. “I Tobit have walked all the days of my life in the ways of truth and justice, and I did many almsdeeds to my brethren, and my nation, who came with me to Nineve, into the land of the Assyrians.”

“The most High gave me grace and favour before Enemessar, so that I was his purveyor”, overseeing the food and rations. When Enemessar died, Sennacherib his son reigned, the same Sennacherib that attacked Hezekiah and lost 185,000 men. Tobit “gave my bread to the hungry, and my clothes to the naked: and if I saw any of my nation dead, or cast about the walls of Nineve, I buried him.” Assyria was very brutal and vicious; they would take Israelites to the top of the walls and throw them off, and Tobit would bury his brothers broken in pieces on the ground.

“And if the king Sennacherib had slain any, when he was come, and fled from Judea, I buried them privily; for in his wrath he killed many.” Why did he flee from Judea? Because he lost 185,000 men. He was mad that he could not overthrow Judah, so out of anger he started killing Ephraim. When a Ninevite complained of Tobit to the king, his goods were forcibly taken away, and “there passed not five and fifty days, before two of his sons killed him”, the same death Isaiah 37:38 records.

Then Sarchedonus, Esarhaddon, reigned and appointed Achiacharus, Tobit's brother's son, over all his father's accounts, so Tobit gained standing again through his nephew. So Isaiah shows the angel saving Judah, and Tobit shows the other side of that same day: the northern kingdom in captivity in Nineveh, bearing Sennacherib's wrath, and a faithful Naphtalite burying his brethren.

In the days of Ahaz, Ephraim conspired with the Syrians to overthrow Judah: the Syro-Ephraimite war. Rezin was the king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah was king of Ephraim, and their plan was to take Judah's land and set the son of Tabeal as king over it. Ahaz was weak and wicked, and his heart shook “as the trees of the wood are moved”. But the Lord said the counsel of Syria and Ephraim would not stand: “within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.”

In Isaiah 8 the Lord brings “the king of Assyria, and all his glory” like a river over his banks. Assyria would rise up and conquer Ephraim, and also pass through Judah and take some portions of it, but not fully like Ephraim. “Take counsel together, and it shall come to nought” … “for God is with us.” Isaiah's sons were born as signs that Ephraim and Syria would be overthrown by Assyria and would not succeed against Judah.

So the Lord tells Isaiah not to fear their confederacy, and not to be like Ahaz, cowardly and weak: “Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread. And he shall be for a sanctuary; but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel.” It says both. The Lord speaks of one Israel as two houses: the house of Judah and the house of Ephraim, the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom. And that stone of stumbling is Christ.

He is “for a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem”, a trap to both houses, but specifically to those in Jerusalem. “And many among them shall stumble, and fall, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken.” The context has not changed. Not only did Ephraim fall physically and spiritually; Judah fell physically and spiritually too, but worse, because they stumbled at that stone.

Hosea shows Ephraim's side. His daughter Lo-ruhamah, no mercy: “I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away”, which is Assyria overthrowing Ephraim so that it be not a people. His son Lo-ammi: “for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” When you are not God's people and he is not your God, that makes you a Gentile, a heathen, a stranger, a non-Israelite. Judah read that and said, good, the hell with Ephraim, they are Gentiles, we don't deal with them anymore.

The rock ties it together. Moses said “He is the Rock, his work is perfect” … “a God of truth and without iniquity”, and “is not he thy father that hath bought thee?” That rock of Isaiah 8 is Christ, our God and our father, and the stone both houses of Israel stumbled over.

Under Josiah, when the money for the house of God was brought to Hilkiah the high priest, it was “the money that was brought into the house of God, which the Levites that kept the doors had gathered of the hand of Manasseh and Ephraim, and of all the remnant of Israel, and of all Judah and Benjamin”.

Manasseh donated toward the temple in Jerusalem, and Ephraim donated too. Why “the remnant of Israel”? Because Assyria had taken most of them out of the land in waves; remnants remained, some idolatrous and some faithful. And that was during Josiah’s reign: whenever Judah is on point, Ephraim follows along.

Then Isaiah speaks to those same northern lands: “the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali”, afflicted “by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.” Zebulun came to keep the Passover in Hezekiah’s day, and Tobit was of Naphtali. Galilee of the Gentiles is where the northern kingdom resided, and they were called Gentiles. “The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light”: the people of verse 1, the northern kingdom.

“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”: unto us, not all. He is the Prince of Peace because he must bring peace between those who have hatred for each other, so that there is no more division between the two kingdoms. “The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel. And all the people shall know, even Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria”. The same Ephraim and Manasseh whose remnant gave to the house of God in Judah’s good days would see the light of the son born of Judah.

Christ “must needs go through Samaria”, to Sychar, “near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph”, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh. The woman of Samaria said, “How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” The Samaritans were the northern kingdom, and the Jews had no dealings with them because of that beef from way back.

Hosea is where it came from: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” The Lord said leave them alone, they're joined to idols, and Judah took that as okay: what the hell with them, they're cast off. But Judah forgot the part where it said they would be joined together and appoint themselves one head. That was dismissed because of the hatred the houses had for each other, that back and forth.

Yet the woman said, “Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well”? She called Jacob our father, and Joseph's house got that well: she was Israel. She said “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”, Gerizim, where all Israel worshipped before Jerusalem. And Isaiah said “The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel. And all the people shall know, even Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria”, so she said “I know that Messias cometh”.

The disciples “marvelled that he talked with the woman”, because the Jews didn't deal with the northern kingdom. But those are our people. Christ taught the Samaritans two days, and they knew “that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world”: the world is Israel. The dividing hatred said let him alone, but Christ came to heal it.

Paul and Barnabas went about “Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.” The tribulation hasn't fully started; you see it on a certain scale, but it will intensify. It will get worse, and worse, and worse.

Micah says how to go through it: “Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail”. The Bible says to be in pain. Pain is coming, and it has already begun; pay attention to what Trump and these people are doing. But whatever pain you go through, you still have to labour, labouring in this truth.

“for now shalt thou go forth out of the city, and thou shalt dwell in the field, and thou shalt go even to Babylon”. Where are we living today? Babylon: Mystery Babylon the Great, the United States of America.

Why does it say like a woman in travail? Because the pain comes and it goes, and when the baby is close to coming the pains increase and get worse and worse. That is what you see taking place now. Whether this society has another ten or twenty years, as the time draws nearer the pains will increase: the affliction rising against those of us that fear God. Keep labouring through them.

That is why the brother who is not studying and applying the scriptures has no root and will not survive it; when things get real he will be offended, scared, and go back into the world. Sisters, a brother who never teaches and is never in a camp video is a gamble.

Much tribulation is coming, and Revelation shows where it comes from: “And the dragon was wroth with the woman”. The dragon is the beast, the white man, Esau. According to the prophecy they will be angry at us, “and went to make war with the remnant of her seed”.

Why? Not because we are evil or terrorists, but because we “keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.” The testimony of Jesus Christ is everything written in this book, everything the prophets said would happen, everything written about who the wicked are and all the evil the so-called white man is doing. That testimony says these people are the synagogue of Satan, and that God is bringing judgment on them for all their evil on the earth. As you teach it, they get angry and make war with us.
