The tribulation will be attacks from the government: labelling us a hate group, lying on us, putting us in prison, hitting your pocket and your food, attacking your wife and your children, because those are the things we care about. In the end they will force idol worship: worship the beast, or you can't buy, sell, work, get a job or go to the doctor.

The dragon is wroth, and he will make war with us. That is the much tribulation through which we must enter into the kingdom of God, and why we must be exhorted to continue in the faith.

Daniel asks to know “the truth of the fourth beast, which was diverse from all the others, exceeding dreadful, whose teeth were of iron, and his nails of brass”. The fourth beast is the fourth kingdom to rise up and rule the earth: it began with Rome, and Europe and America are the extension of Rome. The beast is Edom, the so-called white man.

“And of the ten horns that were in his head, and of the other which came up, and before whom three fell”. The ten horns are the Europeans; when the European Union was first formed it was ten nations, though today it is much more than that. The other horn that came up among them is America, and the three that fell before it are the powers America fought for its independence: France, Spain and Britain. This year America turns 250 years old.

“even of that horn that had eyes, and a mouth that spake very great things”. Look at the back of the dollar bill: the eye of a man set in the top of the pyramid, separated from the rest of it so it looks like a horn, with light illuminating all around it. It is not only the eye of Ra; they put the eyes of a man there. Those eyes are this man's wisdom and his technology, the wisdom Satan gave him. And it is his claim to be God: God sees everything everyone does, and the white man sets himself up as God and says, I see everything.

The great mouth speaks great things: he calls himself the people of God, calls himself a Jew, and says the land of Israel belongs to him. America has spoken many great things against God. And the great mouth is his power to communicate, to speak from one side of the world to the other.

“whose look was more stout than his fellows”: America is stronger than all the European nations. Why? Because of the technology, because of that great mouth and those eyes. Ezekiel shows the same wisdom in the prince of Tyrus, a rich ancient city on the coast of Lebanon that God uses as an analogy for America: “thou hast said, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God”, “yet thou art a man, and not God”. “Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from thee”. With the technology we have, you can talk to someone on the other side of the world and see him on a device. There is no secret you can hide from the white man; every evil you do, everything you buy, he sees it.

“By thy great wisdom and by thy traffick hast thou increased thy riches”: that is how America became rich, through its technology and trade, the system that made the American dollar the dominant dollar in the world. But because he has set his heart “as the heart of God”, God says, “I will bring strangers upon thee, the terrible of the nations: and they shall draw their swords against the beauty of thy wisdom”. That is future prophecy.

Isaiah says, “Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them, which shall not regard silver; and as for gold, they shall not delight in it.” Before the 70s Iran was always known as Persia; that is the Medes and Persians, the second of Daniel's beasts counting from Babylon. God is going to stir them up against the United States of America, Babylon, and all the bombs, the warfare and the destroying of their economy that America and Israel are doing is what will make them rise up. They will not care about money or gold.

“Their bows also shall dash the young men to pieces; and they shall have no pity on the fruit of the womb; their eye shall not spare children.” They will even kill children. That is the third woe: it starts in the land of Israel and ends with America destroyed. “And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms” … “shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.” That is nuclear destruction.

Ezra shows who sets it off: “Behold an horrible vision, and the appearance thereof from the east: Where the nations of the dragons of Arabia shall come out with many chariots, and the multitude of them shall be carried as the wind upon earth, that all they which hear them may fear and tremble.” The dragons of Arabia are the Arabs, the sons of Ishmael. They are the ones who will fully set it off, with the Israelis in the land over there. It will not be Iran first.

“Also the Carmanians raging in wrath shall go forth as the wild boars of the wood.” The Carmanians are Iran, the Persians. Why are they raging in wrath? Because of all the oppression, the sanctions, the bombing of their cities, the killing of their leaders. In the following years Iran will be under heavy sanctions and bombed a lot by the United States, and America and Israel are trying to back a coup against the Iranian regime. Everything Trump is doing is just fulfilling Bible prophecy: he is making the Persians mad.

We don't give a crap about the Arabs or the Iranians. Those people enslaved us, and God is bringing judgment on them. America is the hammer of God, and God is using America to judge the Arabs and the Persians. Then in the end that same cup America is pouring on them is going to be poured on America.

America is about to turn up affliction on everyone on this earth, including us, and it will get worse and worse, like a woman in travail. So this is not the time to be in la-la land or in the midst of sin. It is the time to prepare ourselves and get our spirit right for what is about to take place.

Job 20 is talking about America being destroyed: “a fire not blown shall consume him”, the nuclear bomb that needs no fanning to burn; “it shall go ill with him that is left in his tabernacle”, left here in America. “The heaven shall reveal his iniquity”: as we teach the word of God, the angels make things happen, Europe starts showing America's shame, and everybody sees America, and Israel too, as the oppressor. Europe has already brought charges against Netanyahu and put out a warrant for his arrest for war crimes. “and the earth shall rise up against him.”

Isaiah explains it: “Hell from beneath is moved for thee to meet thee at thy coming: it stirreth up the dead for thee, even all the chief ones of the earth; it hath raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations.” Hell is the low condition everybody on earth is in under him. Raised up from their thrones: all the nations rising up to fight against America and destroy America.

“All they shall speak and say unto thee, Art thou also become weak as we? art thou become like unto us?”

“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!” How are you fallen from ruling, O America. That is the earth rising up against him: the nations he weakened rising up to destroy this place.

Esau “hath said in his heart, I shall not be moved: for I shall never be in adversity.” The white man's mouth is full of cursing, deceit and fraud. “He sitteth in the lurking places of the villages: in the secret places doth he murder the innocent”: that is Mossad and the CIA, the black sites where they would put us and kill us. And “his eyes are privily set against the poor”: the eye on the back of the dollar bill, and the social media and technology set up to monitor us. Every porn video you watch, every site you go on, the white man knows. The ADL monitors bank accounts, and even the police can see all that information. Everything is coming under one system.

David says it plainly: “The wicked watcheth the righteous, and seeketh to slay him.” Brothers and sisters, they are watching you. With the system they have set up they can tell everything you are doing. They are watching those of us who keep the commandments, who call ourselves Israelites. They know there are more than a million people in America who identify as Israelites and agree with these teachings.

And they seek to slay him: they want to destroy us. “He lieth in wait secretly as a lion in his den: he lieth in wait to catch the poor.” He wants to catch you slipping, clicking on the wrong thing. “He croucheth, and humbleth himself, that the poor may fall by his strong ones”: the government, the police, the military.

So walk right and be an example. Build yourselves up. If the wicked is watching the righteous, let him find nothing on you but the commandments of God.

The wicked sits in the secret places and “his eyes are privily set against the poor.” David describes how they watch: “Every day they wrest my words: all their thoughts are against me for evil. They gather themselves together, they hide themselves, they mark my steps, when they wait for my soul.”

They mark your steps: they watch everywhere you go. When you download TikTok now, you have to agree to terms that let them check your immigration status and follow your location wherever you go. The new terms are set up to monitor you and follow you. They want to destroy our soul.

Christ went through the same thing: “And they watched him, and sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words, that so they might deliver him unto the power and authority of the governor.” They watch us through these devices; even YouTube lets our channels stay up so they can monitor us. You see it happening today. Europe is saying you are wrong for what Israel did in Palestine, killing all these kids, and they brought charges against Netanyahu and put a warrant out for his arrest for war crimes. Whistleblowers are telling on each other. That is their own tongue falling upon themselves. That is why they want to take TikTok and X and control the warfare, but they are not going to be able to change nothing.

Job shows the same end for the wicked man: “The heaven shall reveal his iniquity; and the earth shall rise up against him.” The heaven revealing his iniquity starts with us: as we teach the word of God, the angels make things happen, Europe starts showing America's shame, and everybody sees the oppressor for what she is, and not just America but Israel too. Then “a fire not blown shall consume him”: a fire you do not have to fan, the nuclear bomb, and “it shall go ill with him that is left in his tabernacle”, left here in America.

The earth that rises up against him is the nations. Isaiah shows it: “Hell from beneath is moved for thee to meet thee at thy coming”, hell being that low condition everybody on the earth is in, and “it hath raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations.” “How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning!” How are you fallen from ruling, O America. All nations rise up to fight against America and destroy her.

So leave social media alone. It was created to monitor you, brainwash you and control you. God is going to save the poor from their mouth, and their own tongue will bring them down.

Paul says the meat “is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” So where were the animals sanctified to be eaten or not to be eaten? In the law.

Leviticus 11 closes: “For I am the Lord your God: ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.” He repeats it: “ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.” How do you become holy? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy”. To sanctify yourself and be holy you have to apply the law, the statutes and the commandments.

Then: “This is the law of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth: To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.” This law takes in all the animals, whether they live on the earth or in the waters. That is how the word sanctifies the meat: by making a difference between what can be eaten and what cannot. Some animals are clean, some are unclean. It is basic.

The churches don't want you to learn the Old Testament, because they don't want you to be saved. “Keep my commandments, and live”. If you don't keep the law you are not going to live. John says “sin is the transgression of the law”, and “the wages of sin is death”. Eating unclean food is sin; eating pork is going to kill you, and overeating is going to kill you.

You are supposed to be the temple of God. If you keep destroying yourself with the way you eat, you are working against what the Lord says, and against the work we are all called here to do. The meat that is received with thanksgiving is the meat the law sanctified.

Christians take this chapter and say every creature is good to eat, so long as you pray over it. But Paul says the meats God created are “to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.” So what is the truth? “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” The truth is the law.

That changes the whole verse. The meat is not received by everybody who bows his head over his plate. It is received by them that know the law. People say, just give thanks, just pray on it, and it's all right. Then can I pray on a human's foot and eat it? Pork carries the worm that lives in the muscle and can go to your brain; the shrimp, the lobster, the catfish and all the shellfish are bottom feeders whose job is to clean the ocean, the roaches of the sea. A prayer does not change what they are.

“For every creature of God is good” means what Genesis means: “God saw that it was good.” Every creature is good to serve its purpose. Worms prepare the land for planting, but we don't eat worms. The pig was the garbage disposal before there were trucks to pick up the garbage. Good for its work, not for your plate.

And Paul finishes: “For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” A Christian never reads up to that verse. The word of God is the law, the truth, and the law is what tells you which creatures are sanctified to eat. Many who have come into the truth, who know Christ is black and that we are Israel, are still struggling with that pork and that shrimp. This is the answer to that struggle: the ones who receive it with thanksgiving are those who know the law.

Paul says the meats are received “of them which believe and know the truth.” What is it to believe? “He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment”. If you take heed to the commandments, you believe. Does a Christian believe in the commandments? So when he says you can eat anything as long as you receive it with thanksgiving, no: you can pray all you want, but you don't believe and you don't know the truth. Those are the very things that can save your life.

Finish the verse: “and he that trusteth in him shall fare never the worse.” If you believe in the commandments and keep the dietary laws, will you be worrying about high blood pressure? Will you be worrying about a foot amputation because of diabetes, about high cholesterol, about gout that takes brothers' fingers and feet? No, because you are not eating in a way where those sicknesses can come your way. The law tells you the food you can eat and the food you cannot eat.

All of that comes because people wanted to eat nasty, dirty food the Lord said don't eat. So take heed to yourself. Believing is not a prayer said over the plate; it is taking heed to the commandment, and the one who does fares never the worse.

Ezekiel says the proverb will be used against us: “As is the mother, so is her daughter.” Very rarely do you see a fat mother and a skinny daughter. If the mama is big, the daughter is big, and if there is a son, he is really big too, because what you eat to get there is exactly what the kids have in the house to eat. The kid models himself or herself after the parents. If you are in the house working out, your kids will want to do push-ups and pull-ups and be in the gym with you. If you like to lie on the bed eating ice cream, they will lie in the bed eating ice cream with you. That self-hatred gets passed on, and that is how the cycle continues: grandmama's fat, mama's fat, the kid is fat, and they all give the same excuse, my thyroid, we big boned. Garbage.

So Proverbs gives the command: “Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.” It is you that has to shape and mould the trajectory of the kid's life. That goes from teaching them the laws, to showing them what is good to eat and what is not good to eat, to showing them to exercise and to do their studies: train them in the right direction in every aspect.

If there is no candy in the house, can a six-year-old go outside and buy candy? Hell no. If there are no donuts in the house, can a six-year-old go and buy donuts? The kid eats what you feed them. And stop giving your kids choices: put sugary food and good food before a kid and ask what they want, and they will always choose sugar. A kid does not know. When your kid loves a healthy food, give it to them all the time.

If you are big and your kid is big, how will you feel when your young kid needs insulin shots because he is diabetic from being overfed on all kinds of garbage? Where is the love in that? Laziness is why a lot of the time we don't deal with our kids right and we don't deal with ourselves right. If we want to save our kids, it starts with you first: control your eating and exercise, and then you are setting the right example, so that the daughter who is as her mother is trained in the right way.

Many of our people who believe Christ is black and believe they are Israelites still struggle with Paul’s words: “For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving”. They take it to mean, just pray over it and eat whatever you want. But what makes every creature good? “And God made the beast of the earth after his kind, and cattle after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the earth after his kind: and God saw that it was good.” Every creature is good for its purpose. Worms are one of the best ways to prepare land for planting, but we do not eat worms. Pigs were the garbage disposal, because they eat everything. Can you pray over a human foot and eat it?

The bottom feeders have a purpose too. Catfish, loaches, shrimp and snails are sold as natural tank cleaners: they eat the uneaten food, the algae and the waste. Put crab or any bottom feeder in murky water and in a few hours it will be clear. The filter you change in a fish tank is what you eat when you eat shrimp; that is why they are called the roaches of the sea. Lobster was once fed to prisoners. And pork carries the trichinella worm, which can travel into the muscles and even the brain. If a creature’s job is to eat garbage, what will it do to you? Gout, high cholesterol, hypertension, even lost fingers and feet.

Read the verse before and the verse after. The meats are “received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth”, and “thy law is the truth.” To believe is to keep the law: “He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment; and he that trusteth in him shall fare never the worse.” And the creature “is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” Christians never read that far.

So where does the word of God sanctify the animals? Here: “ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.” He says it twice: “ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.” And how are we holy? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy”. “This is the law of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth: To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.”

“Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.” You move like a flash when something comes at your eye; flee from sin that fast. John says, “sin is the transgression of the law”, and “the wages of sin is death”. Eating unclean food, and overeating, is destroying the temple the Most High gave you to do his work. He wants a fit army: you cannot teach discipline in the street without having it yourself, and you cannot go to camp and become a liability.
blog/2026/2026-01-31-2026-01-31-the-prid:
Nebuchadnezzar is the head of gold in Daniel's dream, and before God humbled him in chapter 4, his pride is shown in chapter 3: “Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image of gold, whose height was threescore cubits, and the breadth thereof six cubits: he set it up in the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon.” In his pride he set up a golden image and said everybody should worship it.

He gathered the princes, the governors, the captains, the judges and all the rulers of the provinces to its dedication, and “an herald cried aloud, To you it is commanded, O people, nations, and languages”, that when they heard the music they should “fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king hath set up”. And “whoso falleth not down and worshippeth shall the same hour be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace.”

That is the same thing America does now with the flag. You don't bow down to it; now you have to stand up and salute it and honor it. It is the same as it was in ancient Babylon, just a different way.

This is why the decree of Daniel 4 came upon him. Nebuchadnezzar got prideful, and pride brings a man low. Twelve months after Daniel's interpretation he said, “Is not this great Babylon, that I have built for the house of the kingdom by the might of my power, and for the honour of my majesty?” God calls America Babylon the great, and Nebuchadnezzar called Babylon great himself. “While the word was in the king’s mouth”, the kingdom departed from him. You try to make people worship you, and it is taken.

He was made to eat grass as oxen “until thou know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men”. Until you humble yourself, you are eating grass. And he did humble himself; he came back and confessed there is no God like the God of Daniel. All kingdoms fall because of pride, Assyria, Babylon, the Greeks, Rome and America, and nobody is exempt from God's judgment for it.

Every kingdom on earth has failed because of pride, even ours. Isaiah says “Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim”: the northern kingdom fell because of pride. They separated from God, went to the north and said, we are doing our own thing. It goes back to the split between Rehoboam and Jeroboam. Rehoboam could have listened to the elders who were already there to run the nation correctly, but he mocked the leadership above him and dealt with his buddies, and we are in the condition we are in today because of that pride.

The northern kingdom was the first to fall, but the southern kingdom was not exempt. “Thus saith the Lord, After this manner will I mar the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem.” Judah looked at what their brother was doing and followed right after their treacherous sister Israel. The great pride of Jerusalem takes in Benjamin and Levi too: all of the southern kingdom was full of pride in God's eyes.

“This evil people, which refuse to hear my words, which walk in the imagination of their heart, and walk after other gods, to serve them, and to worship them, shall even be as this girdle, which is good for nothing.” When pride comes, you separate yourself from your maker, as Sirach 10 says, and walk after your own heart. When you are full of pride you are good for nothing in God's eyes.

Then the judgment for it: “And I will dash them one against another, even the fathers and the sons together, saith the Lord: I will not pity, nor spare, nor have mercy, but destroy them.” Pride destroyed the kingdom, and it destroys every kingdom.

“Hear ye, and give ear; be not proud: for the Lord hath spoken.” You better listen up, Israel, and not separate yourself from him. He is our creator and he controls all of this, so you better humble yourself and do as he tells you. This could be over right now if all of us said, Lord, I'm done with pride, I humble myself, what do you want me to do? And Christ would crack the sky.

But not on the surface, saying forgive me and then waiting till you get out of here. You are not fooling God. That is why we are still here as a people: even those of us that repented are not ready to go back to the kingdom yet. And pride is not always loud. It can be subtle, shutting down, thinking you can do it on your own, and Satan still has you there.

Pride destroyed every kingdom on the earth, and Assyria is the first king in line. Sennacherib took all the defenced cities of Judah, then sent Rabshakeh, his herald, with big words: “What confidence is this wherein thou trustest?” When Hezekiah's men begged him to speak in the Syrian language so the people on the wall would not hear, he said he was sent to “the men that sit upon the wall, that they may eat their own dung, and drink their own piss with you.” Then he mocked the Lord himself: “Hath any of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?” … “that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?” All that pride came out of the king of Assyria's mouth by way of his messenger.

God heard all that smack. “Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Whereas thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria: This is the word which the Lord hath spoken concerning him; The virgin, the daughter of Zion, hath despised thee, and laughed thee to scorn; the daughter of Jerusalem hath shaken her head at thee.” She is laughing at this man's tough talk, the way a parent shakes their head when they told you not to do it and are about to whoop your ass. You are not going to one-up God, and that goes for everyone making videos mocking God's prophets. God will one-up you.

“For I will defend this city to save it for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake. Then the angel of the Lord went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand.” One of God's angels destroyed 185,000. The sun went down and they were all alive; at the crack of the morning, “they were all dead corpses.” Talking prideful against God, everybody had to die.

But God was hunting Sennacherib himself. “So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh.” He thought he got away. Then “as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god”, his own sons “smote him with the sword”, and they escaped into Armenia, and his other son Esarhaddon reigned in his stead and didn't even care.

Pride destroyed the king of Assyria, as “a man’s pride shall bring him low” in Proverbs 29. And it is the same line through every kingdom after him, Babylon, the Greeks, Rome and America: none is exempt from pride, and none is exempt from God destroying them for it.

Obadiah speaks “concerning Edom”: the white man, the Caucasian, by his biblical name. “Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars”. They were so proud that they went to the moon and claimed it for their own, something they did not even create. They do not let other nations plant a flag there; they said, the Eagle has landed. And now one of their government says, we own the moon, why not Greenland? That is pride.

There is a reason behind it, and Luke shows it: “the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it. If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine.”

This Edomite is prideful because he has the spiritual power of Satan rolling with him. That is who gave him the power to go to the moon and to make these weapons to destroy all of mankind. No brown nation on the earth came up with the invention to destroy everybody; that belongs solely to the white man, because Satan is behind him. That is who he made a covenant with, not the God of the Bible.

So when you see In God we trust on the money, know he is not talking about anybody in this Bible. The Psalm proves it: “The wicked, through the pride of his countenance, will not seek after God: God is not in all his thoughts.” “The wicked in his pride doth persecute the poor”, and you judge whether a man is prideful or humble by how he treats the lowly: the blacks, Hispanics and Native Indians, who have no army. Out of all the kingdoms, Assyrian, Babylonian, Persian, Greek, Roman, none has been more prideful than Esau.

But the kingdoms Satan gives are not the Lord's, and Obadiah answers the pride: “thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.” From the moment they said the Eagle has landed, they have been going down, because that is when the Israelites started hitting the streets with the word of God. The more we are gathered together, the more Esau comes down.

“Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.”

Actions are weighed when it comes to the Most High. That is why he gave us the excellent things of Proverbs 22:20: to learn them and apply them, because he wants actions behind those things. Not lip service, but actual action from all of us that he called.

Romans 15:4 says the scriptures were written for our learning; 1 Samuel 2:3 says what he does with that learning. He weighs what we do with it. Proud talk and arrogancy out of the mouth weigh nothing with him, because he is a God of knowledge and knows whether the words are backed by works.

That is the pride of thine heart: to talk big about the things of God and not live them. The one who has been given the excellent things has to put his actions where his mouth is, and keep arrogancy out of it.

“Verily thou art a God that hidest thyself, O God of Israel, the Saviour.” He hides himself. That means he is not dealing with everybody. It is not like you just say, hey God, and he turns around. He answers and reveals himself to whom he wants to.

So for you to have even a little understanding of his excellent things, to learn them and apply them to your life, means something. He is the “God of Israel, the Saviour.” If God has revealed himself to you, that you are an Israelite, that you even have a mind to conceive his words and understand them, that means something to God. It means you are worthy enough for him to reveal his words to you, so that you get a chance to know what these excellent things are.

You can’t take that lightly. Far too many people in this world do, and use the Bible for material gain and to feel good on their terms. God doesn’t get down like that. He is a God that hides himself, so if he is letting you know what these words mean, you better take heed to him.

And that is where the humbling comes in. Romans 12:3 follows it: “not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.” If he is revealing himself to you when he does not deal with everybody, you better have some humbleness, because that is the King of kings, the omnipotent Most High God. We are Israelites and we have to keep God’s commandments, so don’t think too highly of yourself. Humble down.

“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning.” The excellent things God wrote in Proverbs 22:20, the counsels and knowledge that make us “know the certainty of the words of truth”, were written for us to learn.

And not only to learn: “that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” These excellent things are written for us to apply to our lives, so that we can be excellent and great in God’s eyes. Learn and apply, that is what Romans 15:4 is telling us.

Everything in this Bible is the excellent things of God, the truth he wants us to know. It is not to be used to get rich off of prosperity teaching, and it is not up for debate for us to decide what we should and should not do. It is not up for debate whether we want to be great or average. God gave us excellent things because he expects excellence out of us.

So we have to change our mindset and live up to the standards of God, not the standards the world has placed on black men and women and Hispanic men, to be comfortable with the crumbs society gives us. Those excellent things are what we have to apply, and it starts with a change in the mind.

The first thing on the list of what the Lord hates is “A proud look.” Proverbs 16 shows where that proud look ends: “Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.”

Whenever you see somebody fall off, just know there is some form of pride in that man or that woman: something they do not want to address, an inflated ego, disdain, a haughty look, a refusal to come back to God. You might not have seen it. They might have masked it as confidence in your eyes, but God saw it as pride.

Pride is not always loud and in your face. It can be subtle: not asking for help because you do not want to seem weak, holding grudges because you feel justified, saying I am good when you are not, shutting down and thinking you do not need anybody. Pride always points the finger at somebody else and never at yourself. So when you start feeling yourself too much, puffing your chest out, say, Oh no, I am not trying to fall; let me be humble, let me be loving.

Every kingdom has failed because of pride, even ours. “Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim”: the northern kingdom fell because of pride, separating from God to do their own thing, going back to the split under Rehoboam, who would not listen to the elders. Then the southern kingdom: “After this manner will I mar the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem.” And the warning to us: “Hear ye, and give ear; be not proud: for the Lord hath spoken.”

So the proud look is first on God’s list because it is the start of the fall. God made your eyes, your body and the mind you think with; walking in pride is departing from your maker, and it ends in destruction.

Paul says “not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly”. If God is revealing himself to you, and he doesn't deal with everybody, you had better have some humbleness, because that is the King of kings, the omnipotent Most High God.

Solomon shows why: “I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” We are all beasts. Although we may be the sons and daughters of God, at the same time we are still beasts in his eyes.

“For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other”. The lion, the bug that has no value in the eyes of God and just serves the purpose it was created for: we die just like them. “yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all is vanity.” This is Solomon, the wisest man ever to walk the earth besides Jesus the Christ, saying you have no preeminence above a beast.

So who are you to think you are better than that, to reject what God has written and do as thou wilt? Break it down to its lowest form, and we perish just like everything else. That is where humbleness comes in. We came here and we are going to leave here, so apply these excellent things to your life before you go back to your Maker.

“I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” That's why we say it: the Israelites are gods upon this earth, children of the Most High.

But read on: “But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes.” We die just like men, just like the beasts of Ecclesiastes 3. In the grand scheme of things, we have no more power over death than the animals do. Are we higher up on the ladder of God's creation? Sure we are. But we perish just like everything else he has created.

That is exactly why a man must not think of himself more highly than he ought to think. Being called gods and children of the Most High is no ground for pride, because the same ones called gods fall like the princes. Think soberly: the one who knows he will die like men humbles himself before the God who made him.

“The days of our years are threescore years and ten”: seventy years is what we have. “and if by reason of strength they be fourscore years”: if God is merciful, we might get eighty years out of this body. You know the Bible is a true book: you get to hitting around forty and you say, damn, David was right.

That's why Captain Gideon did the class about working out, not drinking sodas and calcifying the bones, eating once a day and taking good care of yourself, so God can be merciful: he did real good with that temple I gave him; let me give him eighty years.

“yet is their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.” We fly away means the spirit goes back to its Creator. That is the one day a man is going to fly: when he gets up out of this body.

And even eighty years is nothing to God. Peter says one day with the Lord is as a thousand years; by that measure a whole human lifetime is less than two hours in God's eyes, and it could be even less. Your life is but a vapor. So how do you look down on others and think so highly of yourself? Think soberly, and humble yourself.

Why do we die? We try to break it down so the new people coming into the faith can put the puzzle together: “For the wages of sin is death”. That is why the covenant, thou shalt die the death, passed upon all of us. When Adam listened to his wife Eve and consented to the idolatry she brought to him, sin came into the world, and when sin came, death came with it.

“but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” That is what we get in the repentance. But we still have to go through the covenant of all flesh. You can't receive the gift of eternal life while you are still in the flesh; flesh and blood cannot enter into the kingdom of heaven. We have to pass through that covenant.

And one thing we had better make sure we don't have on us when we leave this body is pride. That will keep us out of it for sure. That is why Paul says not to think of yourself more highly than you ought: the one who dies like the beasts receives the gift only through Christ, and only if he goes to his grave humble.

“All flesh waxeth old as a garment: for the covenant from the beginning is, Thou shalt die the death.” That is what we just read in David: seventy, maybe eighty years. That is the covenant God pronounced from the beginning: thou shalt die the death.

“As of the green leaves on a thick tree, some fall, and some grow; so is the generation of flesh and blood, one cometh to an end, and another is born.” That is why we have kids. You watch them grow up, and you say, man, I'm getting old. You know the covenant God pronounced upon all flesh, and you are about to cross it too.

“Every work rotteth and consumeth away, and the worker thereof shall go withal.” That is the covenant: thou shalt die the death, thus saith the Lord. Everything a man builds goes with him. So there is no room to think of yourself more highly than you ought; think soberly, knowing the covenant is coming for you like every other leaf on the tree.

“For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.” That is who your body belongs to.

This isn't something the young ones usually fight with. It's us, as we get older, who start smelling ourselves: I'm going to do this, this is what I want to do. We forget that at the end of the day we are still the children of the Most High God. You don't get to tell him what you are going to do with that body. The way parents look at their son and say, you'll always be my baby, even at forty-seven with gray hair: apply that to your life with God.

You have to keep these commandments, because he is still your Father and that is what he said to do. And that is the beginning of pride in Sirach 10: “when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” As we get older we start thinking we can decide whether to serve God or obey our Father, and that is pride. Pride is the beginning of sin; don't tell yourself you have a good heart while you depart from his commandments. Pride is hateful before God, and what he hates has an expiration date.

“As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit”: you don't know how the spirit was even made, and the body doesn't function without a spirit in it. We say someone is soulless, and it may be jacked up and crooked like the Esau in them, but that body isn't walking around with nothing in it. This is not a movie where they clone you and you come back with no soul, or a vampire who lives forever and can't see his reflection. There is a spirit in all of us, and the Most High made that.

“nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child”. Science tries to explain it the best way it can, by the mitochondria and this and that, but they don't know what God did to make it. Science is God giving man some sense of his mastery, and man takes it and says, I can do better than God: let me put this rod on you as a woman, let me cut yours off. That's why the Bible warns us to beware of science that opposes God.

“even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.” So why is earth and ashes proud? Man does not even know how he himself was made; pride was not made for men.

Solomon mentions that spirit again: “Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.”

The body goes back to the dust it came from, and the spirit goes back to God who made it. All of this, the dust and the spirit, belongs to the Most High God. That is why pride is not made for us.

Sirach asks, “Why is earth and ashes proud?” and says that when a man is dead “he shall inherit creeping things, beasts, and worms.” The man who is today a king tomorrow shall die. Neither the body nor the spirit is ours to boast in: one returns to the earth, the other to its Maker. So the beginning of pride, departing from God and turning the heart away from the Maker, is turning away from the very one the spirit must return to.

“Pride was not made for men, nor furious anger for them that are born of a woman.” Pride, arrogance, disdain, the inability to admit fault, the inflated ego: God said it wasn't made for you. You are nothing but dust that shall return to where it came from. And anger doesn't get you anywhere either; it holds you back and stunts your growth.

Why wasn't pride made for us? “Know ye that the Lord he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves”. You didn't put one finger on your hand. You didn't put the knee bone with the hip bone and the leg bone. All of that belongs to God, the Creator, from way back when he said, Let us make man in our image.

He didn't consult you: where should I put the knee? How high up on the leg should it go? What should the arch of the foot look like? What skin tone should I give them? What should I make their hair like? None of us were included in that conversation.

So pride has no ground to stand on. The one who did not make himself cannot be proud before the one who made him. That is why the beginning of pride is turning away from your Maker.

Wisdom tells the kings of the earth that “the desire of wisdom bringeth to a kingdom”, and to “honour wisdom, that ye may reign for evermore.” David shows why the kingdoms of the nations never did: “For the Lord is great, and greatly to be praised: he is to be feared above all gods. For all the gods of the nations are idols”.

They are all idols. All kingdoms fall because they do not walk after the wisdom of God. Name a kingdom that has kept the commandments of God. They don't. They fall because they serve idol gods, and pride destroys them, as it destroyed Herod, who gave not God the glory and was eaten of worms. Assyrian, Babylon, Greek, Rome, America: nobody is exempt from pride and God destroying them.

It is no different with Babylon the Great. This Edomite has the most gods of all: he has all the idol gods of every kingdom wrapped up in one, in different forms. That is why Obadiah follows, “concerning Edom”, the white man, the Caucasian, his biblical name: “thou art greatly despised”, and “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”. None of the kings before him, Assyrians, Babylonians, Persians, Greeks or Romans, was more prideful than Esau.

The same judgment is on us. The power God gave was given to us by God too, and for our pride as a nation we have been destroyed. The only way our kingdom will last for ever is when we walk in wisdom and humility toward God. Outside of that, the kingdom comes down, the same as it did with all the nations before us.
blog/2026/2026-02-01-2026-02-01-the-divi:
John says it again in his fourth chapter: “If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” And: “this commandment have we from him, That he who loveth God love his brother also.”

You can't love one and hate the other. It is impossible. If you love your brother, by default you love God; if you love God, by default you love your brother. They go hand in hand: God and people, God and race. What the white man promotes among his people is what we should promote among ourselves. That is the light and darkness of 1 John 2. “He that saith he is in the light, and hateth his brother, is in darkness even until now.” Picture our people in captivity, while the ones who enslaved us rule. Where did John get this “new commandment”? From Christ: “A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another. By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.”

Christ said it to the disciples, and John repeated it in his epistle. Christ said it over and over again: “These things I command you, that ye love one another.”

That is why John can say in the same breath, “I write no new commandment unto you, but an old commandment which ye had from the beginning”, and then, “Again, a new commandment I write unto you”. It is old because it came from Moses' time. It is called new because Israel was not following it. Going back to Moses, we were children in whom is no faith, rebellious; we waxed fat and kicked.

So the mark of Christ's disciples is love one to another, among our own people. “He that loveth his brother abideth in the light, and there is none occasion of stumbling in him.” The one who despises his brother and his people will stumble, and stumble in a lot of deep but basic things.

Christ isn't saying anything new. He calls it a new commandment, but we heard it before, in the law: “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him. Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the Lord.”

Your neighbour is your people. Your neighbour is your brother. Love your neighbour as yourself. When you despise yourself, you despise your God that resembles you and your brother that resembles you. It is a domino effect. You can't love one and hate the other.

That is what John means: “Brethren, I write no new commandment unto you, but an old commandment which ye had from the beginning.” It was there from Moses' time. And it is the very hatred Moses warned against in the beginning, when we were all together, that divided Ephraim and Judah. They began to despise each other, and that is why both fell: the northern kingdom first, and the southern kingdom afterward.

So “he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth”. Christ's new commandment was already in the law, and Israel's fall came from not keeping it.

Normally Matthew 22 is read for this, but Mark is heavy. A scribe asked, “Which is the first commandment of all?” “And Jesus answered him, The first of all the commandments is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God is one Lord: And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: this is the first commandment. And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these.”

There is none greater, because if you love your brother as yourself you can keep all the commandments; they all go hand in hand. You cannot love God and hate your brother. By loving God you will love your brother, and by loving your brother you love God.

What Christ is really saying is: love your people, love your ways. Why would the Most High give us these laws? Because we had learned how to hate one another, and the law was given to teach us. The same laws we give to our people today: love your ways, love your people, love your neighbour.

Think how brainwashed you are in this captivity if, like Deacon Nathan was saying earlier, you are in captivity and care more about your oppressor than your own kind. “until the wrath of the Lord arose against his people, till there was no remedy.” They pissed the Lord off until there was no remedy left. The killing of the prophets Elijah complained of was not one king’s sin; it was the way of the nation until the wrath came.

“Your houses will I give to a people that shall come; which not having heard of me yet shall believe me; to whom I have shewed no signs, yet they shall do that I have commanded them.” That is us today. We are born again.

Christ said the same in the parable of the vineyard: the husbandmen beat one servant, killed another and stoned another, and last of all killed the son, and the lord of the vineyard “will miserably destroy those wicked men, and will let out his vineyard unto other husbandmen”. The other husbandmen are us today, the people Ezra spoke of. “The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.”

Stephen prophesied against the rulers, the builders of his time: “Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye.” As your fathers did, so do you.

“Which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted? and they have slain them which shewed before of the coming of the Just One”. The prophets were killed in the Old Testament, and who were they prophesying of? The Just One. So when the prophets prophesied of a Messiah, they were killed. The killers who got away with it had children, and their children knew who they had killed. Then when Christ was born, they killed him too: “of whom ye have been now the betrayers and murderers: Who have received the law by the disposition of angels, and have not kept it.”

“When they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed on him with their teeth.” Why cut to the heart? Because they knew. Stephen was in the spirit; he saw their fathers killing the prophets: your father killed Zechariah, your father killed Isaiah. They knew and did not care, and they were pissed off that he said it. They gnashed on him, cursing him out.

The prophets were sent to bring us back to God, and the rulers hated them because the prophets could see right through them. It was the same spirit in Elijah’s day, in Christ’s day, and in Rome against the apostles, and it is the same spirit today.

Susanna says wickedness came from Babylon from ancient judges, “such as the Lord spake of”. Where did the Lord speak of it? In Jeremiah, to “all ye of the captivity, whom I have sent from Jerusalem to Babylon”.

“Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, of Ahab the son of Kolaiah, and of Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah, which prophesy a lie unto you in my name; Behold, I will deliver them into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon; and he shall slay them before your eyes”. These were the wicked leaders among the people, false prophets instead of the true ones they persecuted. The Pharisees did the exact same thing when Rome ruled: ancient evil from Babylon, from the elders.

Christ says it to the city: “O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee”. Over and over again, the same thing Elijah cried about: they slew the prophets.

“how often would I have gathered thy children together”: gathered both kingdoms together, “even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!” They refused him, the stone which the builders refused.

“Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.” These are the same words the Lord spoke through Ezra, “Your house is desolate”. The rulers who killed the prophets would kill the Son too, and their house would be left empty, cast out as the wind doth stubble.

Who were the rulers who killed the prophets? The history of Susanna shows where their wickedness came from. “There dwelt a man in Babylon, called Joacim”, a great rich man with a fair garden, “and to him resorted the Jews; because he was more honourable than all others.” He was an elder, a leader, and the people came to sit with him.

“The same year were appointed two of the ancients of the people to be judges, such as the Lord spake of, that wickedness came from Babylon from ancient judges, who seemed to govern the people.” We had ancient judges in Babylon, and they brought Babylonian doctrine and ideals along with them. They seemed to govern the people, but they were not true governors; they were evil and wicked as hell.

These same elders who came out of Babylon, and whose line made its way down to the time of Roman rule, started the Talmud. The Babylonian Talmud: they got it from Babylon. So when Christ condemned their traditions, those traditions came from Babylon. These are the fathers of the Pharisees, the same spirit of the rulers who slew the prophets.

Deuteronomy 17:14-15 is law. If, when you get into your land, you decide you want a king like all the nations round about, the law says fine: set a king over you. But “whom the Lord thy God shall choose”: God has to choose him, you cannot. He must be “one from among thy brethren”, of your own people, and “thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother”: do not set a heathen over you. Now 1 Samuel 8. “when Samuel was old, that he made his sons judges over Israel”, Joel and Abiah, judges in Beer-sheba. “And his sons walked not in his ways, but turned aside after lucre, and took bribes, and perverted judgment.” So the elders of Israel gathered to Samuel at Ramah and said, “now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.”

That is exactly what the law allowed. Samuel was righteous, and he was a priest, so it should not have been a problem. Yet “the thing displeased Samuel, when they said, Give us a king to judge us. And Samuel prayed unto the Lord.” Why would something found in the law upset such a righteous man? The Lord answers: “they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them.”

So he said: I have something for them. I will come down through David's loins and be king over them anyway, either up here or down there. We should not want a king over us; we have a king right there.

The Lord saw it before it happened. Israel was appointed, predestined, to desire a king over them and to reject him, and he came and ruled over them on the throne down here regardless. That goes to another level, a class in itself.

Paul writes to the saints at Ephesus, and the saints are the children of Israel. Yet he tells them, “Wherefore remember, that ye being in time past Gentiles in the flesh, who are called Uncircumcision by that which is called the Circumcision”. In time past the saints were called Gentiles. They were uncircumcised in the flesh because they had been walking “according to the course of this world”, raised in pagan customs, in idolatry. The Circumcision, cut in the flesh made by hands, is the southern kingdom.

“That at that time ye were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world”. That sounds like Chronicles: “Now for a long season Israel hath been without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law.”

Who were they? “And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon: for they fell to him out of Israel in abundance, when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.” The strangers are Ephraim, Manasseh and Simeon: the northern kingdom.

An alien is a stranger, a foreigner, the way they call migrants illegal aliens today. The ten tribes became aliens to the covenant, no longer part of the commonwealth of Israel, the nation, because they were cast off. The Lord told the northern kingdom, you are not my people, and I will not be your God: without God in the world. Those are the strangers Paul says are “no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints”. The northern kingdom got its citizenship back.

“But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.” Who is far off? Peter answers it on the day of Pentecost: “Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost. For the promise is unto you, and to your children, and to all that are afar off, even as many as the Lord our God shall call.”

The promise is to those Peter spoke to, to their children, and to all that are afar off. The far off are the ones who were cast off, the strangers of the northern kingdom scattered away from the land and the covenant.

So when Paul says Christ “came and preached peace to you which were afar off, and to them that were nigh”, it is the same promise Peter preached. Christ taught the woman at the well and he taught the Jews: the far off and the nigh, both brought near by his blood.

Who are the far off and who are the near? Daniel names them in his prayer: “O Lord, righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day; to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them”.

Unto all Israel, that are near and that are far off. Both the near and the far off are Israel, driven through all the countries because of their trespass.

So when Ephesians says “ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ”, the far off are not the nations; they are Israel. Christ “hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us”, abolishing the enmity, the hatred between the southern and northern kingdoms, “for to make in himself of twain one new man”. Isaiah 56 ties directly into Ephesians 2. The context is “my salvation is near to come, and my righteousness to be revealed”: that is Christ.

“Neither let the son of the stranger, that hath joined himself to the Lord, speak, saying, The Lord hath utterly separated me from his people”. Who is that? The northern kingdom, the one the Lord cut off and called not his people. “neither let the eunuch say, Behold, I am a dry tree”: they could not bring forth children.

“Also the sons of the stranger, that join themselves to the Lord, to serve him, and to love the name of the Lord, to be his servants, every one that keepeth the sabbath from polluting it, and taketh hold of my covenant; Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer”. But read the next verse: “The Lord God which gathereth the outcasts of Israel saith, Yet will I gather others to him, beside those that are gathered unto him.”

The others are the other sheep: Christ said, I have other sheep not of this fold. Those gathered are this fold, and the others are the “all people” of the verse before. The son of the stranger in Isaiah 56 is the same as the strangers from the covenants of promise in Ephesians 2, who said the Lord had cut them off from his people. Now, in Christ, they are made nigh, grafted back in with their brothers, the natural branches.

At Bethel the Lord promised Jacob, “thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south”. Israel would be everywhere on the earth, through captivity and through migration, forced or willing. And the promise goes on, “and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed”: that is the Israelite families in those lands, north, south, east and west. The nations are not the ones blessed; their blessing is servitude.

Then the Lord renamed him: “Thy name is Jacob: thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name”. “I am God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins”. In context that can mean all twelve tribes, but prophetically it is written that way for the division to come: the nation is the southern kingdom, Judah, and the company of nations is the northern kingdom, Ephraim. The kings out of his loins are Saul, David, Hezekiah and Josiah.

So the Lord said, “I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.” Isaiah names who is not a people: “within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people”, after the northern kingdom joined Syria against Judah.

Hosea says the same of the company of nations: “Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” Ephraim became as Gentiles, heathens, the uncircumcision. “But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah”. Yet the number of Israel “shall be as the sand of the sea”, as promised to Jacob, and “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God. Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head”, and that head is Christ. Ezekiel agrees: “they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”.

The hatred between the nation and the company of nations is why both fell, the north first and Judah after. The law always said, “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart”, and “he that hateth his brother is in darkness”. Esau never forgets and holds his grudges, while Jacob in captivity forgets his own and cares more for his oppressor. In captivity, your people being oppressed, and all you care about is your oppressor: you're a dummy, and that is the kindest word for it. Love your people and love your ways, and the nation and the company of nations become one again.

Hosea says, “Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head”. You read the same thing from multiple prophets, and Ezekiel says it this way: “And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all”. The one king is the one head.

“and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”: no more southern and northern. Remember, one of them was not a nation at all. Isaiah said, “within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.” Ephraim became Lo-ammi, not my people, Gentiles, heathen, uncircumcised, all the same. “Neither shall they defile themselves any more with their idols, nor with their detestable things”. The builders were appointed to reject Christ so he would be killed, and by his death the northern kingdom would get the chance to repent and be redeemed back into the fold. That could not be done unless Christ died.

So the not my people of Hosea 1 are the strangers Peter wrote to, “Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God”. Christ gathers both kingdoms together as one nation under one king.

Isaiah 28 ends saying “it shall be a vexation only to understand the report.” The report is that Christ is the Messiah, the head of the corner (Isaiah 53:1), and they would not hear it because they were in darkness. Isaiah 29 shows that darkness: “Stay yourselves, and wonder; cry ye out, and cry: they are drunken, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink.”

“For the Lord hath poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep, and hath closed your eyes”. That deep sleep goes back to them being in darkness, blinded. Closed your eyes: you can't see, you're blind.

“the prophets and your rulers, the seers hath he covered.” Today it is your priests and pastors, your politicians, your modern-day educators, conservatives and liberals. They are blind to the word and cannot see.

That is why the rulers could not see the stone laid in Zion. They were in darkness, and whereunto they were appointed, they stumbled at him.

Isaiah 28 says they would “fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken.” Broken by what? By that stone of stumbling, that rock of offence. Isaiah 8 names it: “Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread. And he shall be for a sanctuary”.
