“But in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.” Beauty became part of Absalom's identity. It was synonymous with him: his hair, his physical perfection.

And what came behind that? Ambition and rebellion. You get a big head about yourself and you start to believe certain things. Absalom rose up against his father, it came to civil war, and he died hanging from that very hair, the same thing that was vanity to him.

That is the same lesson as David on the roof in 2 Samuel 11:2. David saw a woman “very beautiful to look upon”, he saw her, he inquired, and he took her, the same pattern as Shechem with Dinah. Out of one fleeting moment of attraction came adultery, the murder of Uriah, a national scandal, the death of the child, and chaos in David's house the rest of his days. The Lord forgave him, but he left him with drama for moving that way. Then Absalom, celebrated for his own beauty, came to pride and rebellion.

Whenever physical attraction becomes the forefront of anything, the Bible shows you that trouble comes behind it. Y'all take chess and spades seriously, seeing moves ahead and counting books, but not marriage: she look good, I got to marry her so I can have her. Attraction is the gateway to destruction if that is the only thing you are moving on.

This is why the scripture says these things: “Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids.” The scripture teaches you not to lust after her beauty, and it says where: in thy heart, in thy mind.

“neither let her take thee with her eyelids.” She gives you the look back. You make the eye contact, you feel the chemistry, the sparks fly, the tentacles of auras come out and they embrace, and you done lost your mind. I got to have her. Bring me that. That's what I want.

That is exactly what happened to David in 2 Samuel 11:2. He walked on the roof, saw a woman washing herself, “and the woman was very beautiful to look upon”, and he moved on what he saw. Shechem saw Dinah and took her, and it ended in violence and massacre. Samson went after the one who pleased him well, and it ended in betrayal and blindness. David saw Bathsheba's beauty, had to have her, and it ended in adultery and murder.

So Solomon's warning is the guard against the very thing David fell into: do not let the beauty get into your heart, and do not let the eyes take you. Attraction is not the foundation, and a man who moves on it alone gives up his strength.

“And, behold, there met him a woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart.” There is the physical again: the attire of an harlot and subtil of heart. She is trying to entice, and you fall for it. It works.

Here Solomon warns about being captured by appearance. How does he know these things? He said not one out of a thousand of the women he dealt with. He knew, and he probably knew before the thousandth. It goes to show how intoxicating it can be. You get caught up.

That is the thread through David on the roof in 2 Samuel 11:2. Shechem saw Dinah and took her: violence and massacre. Samson, she pleased him well: betrayal and blindness. David saw Bathsheba's beauty and had to have her: adultery and murder. Absalom, celebrated for his own beauty: pride and rebellion. And the strange women, being beautiful, lead to ruin.

That is why the Bible rarely makes much of the beauty of wives. Rebecca is known for her character, her hospitality and her faith; Zipporah's beauty is never described; Elizabeth is called righteous, not beautiful. What is highlighted in our foremothers is righteousness, obedience, wisdom and faith. The Bible doesn't deny attraction; it just isn't the foundation.

“Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel”. The knowledge and the honour you give is the commitment to play your role as a husband in all matters. Not, this is the wife you gave me. Not complaining, and not hating her, because the scripture says no man ever hated his own flesh. You deal with the situation.

Men have a moral sense in us, most of us, though some are full of error and lack that integrity. “The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him”. Integrity is doing what's right when nobody's looking, when nobody is there to hold you accountable, like Paul said, not in my presence only. A just man moves with integrity in how he manages and steers his household and in everything else he does as a man of God.

And his children are blessed after him because he raised a stable, sound household. Dwelling with your wife according to knowledge and giving her honour is part of that provision, leadership, instruction and honour the husband owes the house, the same duty Exodus 21:10 says he shall not diminish.

Husbands are responsible for provision, leadership, instruction, and showing honour in the household to the wife and the children. Exodus 21:10 shows the provision: “her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage, shall he not diminish”. He has to provide for his wife's basic needs. “But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel”. That is how bad the Lord sees it.

Ephesians 5 describes the husband's role as sacrificial leadership: “For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body”. And verse 25: “Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it”. He gave himself for it. It is a sacrificial relationship.

That is why the brother who destabilizes the whole household economically is out of order. Hard times may come and the wife may hold it down for a while, as in Tobit, where she took woman's work to support the house. But Tobit did not say, you're doing good, so I'm going to play around and figure out what I want to be when I grow up. Brothers here have done that: not happy with the job, so try this business, since the wife makes good money. Knowing damn well you couldn't take those risks by yourself, you take more risk with more lives on the line than when you were responsible only for you.

The husband's measure of accountability is the heavier one. He is the saviour of the body: accountable for his wife, the house, the children, and for those moving for the nation, the nation behind that too. He puts his soul on the line for that accountability, and that is what giving himself for it means.

In Eden there was no courtship, no feast and no attraction language. God took the rib and made a woman, “and brought her unto the man.” God formed the union himself, and behind that union is a covenant. Malachi shows it: “the Lord hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth”. God was the one who did the first marriage, and God is in the midst of every marriage; what God joins together, man is not to put asunder.

The world kept pieces of this. When a minister says, before the Lord and all these witnesses I now pronounce you man and wife, that is a rudiment of what the Bible says, and a rudiment is only a part, not the whole.

A covenant is a contract. People understand contracts: a sports fan understands a player's contract, you understand the contract for your job and the contract for your phone plan, but somehow we do not understand the contract of marriage, which is far more powerful and profound. Covenants are built on commitment and obligation, not feelings: if you do this, then this will happen.

God speaks of the wife “against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant.” Even if you are being treacherous with your wife, or she with you, you are one flesh, and that is still your companion, the wife of the covenant you made.

Signing a contract on feelings is how people get ripped off buying a car: they like the smell and the color and end up paying the interest rate and the add-ons. Some brothers marry that way: I will deal with all this because she is bad. She is not going to be bad forever. When you get old and the hormones change, you have to be able to live with that person through every dinner, every drive and every wake-up. It has to be stronger than romance and attraction.

Modern ideas about marriage assume feelings are the foundation: find the love of your life, find your prince charming. That is the confusion. The marriage God ordained in Eden stands on his order and on the covenant he witnesses, and that is what carries it through the trials.

Christ said “ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled”, and “the end is not yet”. Ezra shows what the end involves, and it is not here yet.

“Where the nations of the dragons of Arabia shall come out with many chariots, and the multitude of them shall be carried as the wind upon earth, that all they which hear them may fear and tremble.” That is the Arabs, Ishmael, the wild men.

“Also the Carmanians raging in wrath shall go forth as the wild boars of the wood”: the Carmanians are Iran. “And with great power shall they come, and join battle with them”: join battle with the Arab nations. “And shall waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians”, over on that side of the earth.

When it says waste a portion, it is dealing with nukes, and it is dealing with unity: Iran and the Arab nations together. Right now neither of those things is present. So what you are seeing is contractions. It is extremely significant and we should not sleep on it, but it is the beginning of sorrows.

That is why we are not troubled. We do not sleep as others do; like a team moving ten yards at a time down the field, we see ourselves moving toward the goal every time these things happen. It should only trouble you if you are not in the right spirit to move with urgency and repent.

“And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect’s sake those days shall be shortened.” Things are going to get so crazy in the earth that the Lord has to move events forward. Shortened means events will accelerate.

That is what the similitude of a woman in travail goes into: there are times of contraction, then a time of relief from it. But never forget that every contraction means you are being inched closer, moved another ten yards down the field. It is an acceleration of events, just as the prophets described.

So what we are actually witnessing is the stage being set. Do not think what is happening over there is insignificant by any measure. For Iran and the Arabs to be united the way the prophecy says, certain steps have to happen, and it may seem far off; but the Lord can put spirit on men to move things along quicker, shortening the days and increasing the speed of those events.

Christ did not give dates and times, because much depends on when we are sealed, when the 144,000 and the other pieces are in place. Prophecy is not meant to entertain us; it is meant to correct us. The more signs we see, the more urgently we should be repenting, correcting our lives and strengthening our households to prepare for those days. “Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you”: Jacob's trouble is not here yet, but it can escalate quickly on the Lord's timeline.

“The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him.” Why are they blessed? Because he raised a stable, sound household. The other purpose of marriage is “Be fruitful, and multiply”: marriage is nation building, and that implies children if you are able. Psalms 127 explains why.

“Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the Lord keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.” The house is the house of marriage, the foundation of it, and by extension Israel as a people. That is why it is so important to handle this right: if you let the world build the house, you are going to get what we have repeatedly gotten as a people.

“It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so he giveth his beloved sleep.” Why put yourself in a situation and then say woe is me, I am miserable in my marriage, full of sorrows, as if you had no control, power or authority, and as if God were not on your side to fix it?

He did not randomly decide to talk about children; he started with building a house. “Lo, children are an heritage of the Lord: and the fruit of the womb is his reward.” That is how we carry on. “As arrows are in the hand of a mighty man; so are children of the youth.” If the just man walks in his integrity, his children are in good condition.

“Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them: they shall not be ashamed.” They are not ashamed because you raised them godly, and it is not only what you tell them but what they see and experience in you as an example. “but they shall speak with the enemies in the gate”: that is the purpose. They follow behind you and fill your shoes, to point out the evils of our oppressors, to point out the evils of our people, and to give them the hope of salvation that they know not.

So the children of the just man are blessed after him because of Psalms 127: the Lord built the house, and the man kept his integrity in it.

Tobias prayed, “mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.” To age together is the long, intertwined journey of partners growing old side by side: shared history, mutual support through life's changes, companionship, and facing life's challenges as a team. Aged means refined, like wine or cheese.

Then Solomon: “Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity”. There's your romance. Live joyfully: that's part of the aging. “all the days of the life of thy vanity”, because we are here just for a fleeting moment, seventy or eighty years at best. All the days God gives you, you should live joyfully with your wife. That's a commandment.

“for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.” This is how things are supposed to be set up. If you want to navigate this world the right way, you have to navigate your marriage this way.

So the joy is not the foundation; it grows out of it. Everything else has to be established first, or the romance will be fleeting and break the foundation of the scriptures. Tobias took his wife uprightly, and the living joyfully comes in the aging together.

You want passion in the relationship? Here it is: “Let thy fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of thy youth. Let her be as the loving hind and pleasant roe; let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; and be thou ravished always with her love.”

Ravished is not a regular word: it means to fill someone with intense delight and rapture. Delight, charm, enthral, captivate, spellbind, bewitch, fascinate. That goes into the power a woman has in her voice and her conversation. There's your passion, there's your romance, after the foundation of your marriage is set up correctly and you age together.

But that can't exist if the other, divine parts of the marriage are not set up correctly; it's not going to happen. You don't seek this first. It's like looking for furniture, things for the walls, carpet and rugs, when you haven't even bought the house yet and don't know if the walls will hold or the foundation is strong. That's how we treat marriage nowadays.

Tobias did it in the right order: “I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly”. The being ravished always with her love comes after that foundation, as the fruit of it.

Tobias prayed, and Sara “said with him, Amen.” She agreed, because her mind was on her lord; she didn't say, wait, what about the house, what about the gifts. Sirach gives more insight into the character that strengthens marriage: “In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.”

A man and a wife that agree together. The agreement is not that you both like the same music, the same colors, the same food; that's part of the aging stuff. The agreement is this: she agrees to follow the scriptures that pertain to her as a wife, whether or not there are contingencies, because the Bible gives no contingencies for a wife's behavior. You do or you don't. And he agrees to do the same as a husband.

You agree in God that you are going to follow his order of marriage, running it with your responsibilities as a wife and yours as a husband the way the Bible says. That is what is beautiful in God's eyes, because it will work the way he intended when you do those things.

“Blessed is the man that hath a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double.” Virtuous deals with her character. Look how everything gets better in the marriage when the wife moves in that spirit; a virtuous wife brings peace. Tobias asked God that he and his wife might become aged together, and a virtuous wife doubles those days.

“A woman that honoureth her husband shall be judged wise of all; but she that dishonoureth him in her pride shall be counted ungodly of all.” She honors him by agreeing to follow what the Lord says; that's the honor. A woman that honors her husband equals wisdom for the woman. But not how you think: you measure it against the scripture and ask, am I fulfilling all of these things? Pride is what breaks the submission.

When Titus says to teach the women to love their husbands, we have taken it for years as surface emotions. A man experiences love through respect; that is the chief love language of a man. Why does he like being around the brothers so much? Because he's respected among his peers. If the wife reverences him, he'll feel the love, and everything else falls into place behind it.

And not forced respect. It has to come from a sincere place. If you have to remember and remind yourself to respect your husband, you're not in submission. If you really desire your husband and see him as he is, not through a warped worldly view, it will come out of you innately, and watch what will come out of him innately.

Tobias prayed, “Thou madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay”, and “let us make unto him an aid like unto himself.” Sirach says the same: “He that getteth a wife beginneth a possession, a help like unto himself, and a pillar of rest.”

Marriage describes partnership and support, plain and simple. Not a rom-com romantic movie, not a novella or a soap opera. A help like unto himself, a pillar of rest.

What do you see in those words? Stability and wisdom over emotional intensity. We have to stop emphasizing the wrong thing. The emotional intensity comes as a byproduct of those things.

The Bible shows men taking wives: he took a wife, he got a possession. That is the foundation Tobias laid in his prayer, a helper and stay from whom came mankind, a nation, and it is what we must get back to.
blog/2026/2026-03-07-2026-03-07-wars-are:
Amos says “the Lord God of hosts is he that toucheth the land”. When Iran is being touched right now, and Israel, the Lord is involved in all of it; by his counsel the land gets touched. Isaiah shows that counsel: “Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done”.

This is the power we have: understanding that the Most High God from the very beginning planned every war, including the third world war to come. Ancient times means way back when Adam and Eve walked. From then he declared it. As his sons and daughters, the Israelites, we have to know our Father has this covered and his Son is coming back. Right now we have to rehearse the righteous acts and get right.

That is how we can make the bold statement that God is behind the Israelis doing what they do in the US government, and behind the Iranians spending twenty years building huge, elaborate tunnel systems and storing munitions and advanced rocketry. All of it was set up from ancient times. They send drones that cost fifteen to twenty thousand dollars, and the other side fires interceptor missiles that cost a million or more to take them out. You see how they will not be able to keep up. God put all that in these leaders.

“My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure”. It was his pleasure when we went into chattel slavery, through Jim Crow and through civil rights. We had to learn the lesson.

Jeremiah shows the same counsel: “Therefore hear ye the counsel of the Lord, that he hath taken against Babylon”. “Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out”: Israel, the least of Esau's flock, draws the United States out into the Middle East, and “At the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth is moved”. Amos lived way before anything could melt the land. Today thermonuclear ICBMs can, and it is all by his counsel.

Amos says, “And though they go into captivity before their enemies, thence will I command the sword, and it shall slay them”. Who is the sword? The wicked at the time. David shows it: “Arise, O Lord, disappoint him, cast him down: deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword”, and he goes on, “From men which are thy hand, O Lord”.

God wields the wicked as his sword. The wicked today is the United States. He is going to use them to bring in all these wars you are seeing, and we have to get right.

That is why we can't bug out or get caught up in everything going on. Nobody wants to see Arab children losing limbs; nobody wants to see destruction. But we understand why it is happening, and we understand what we have to do, so that when the final war comes, he that endureth to the end shall be saved. That is what we want: deliverance.

So it was with us. The twelve tribes went into captivity after captivity before our enemies, because God allowed every bit of it. He commanded the sword and it slew us, and he set his eyes upon us “for evil, and not for good”, because we did not keep the commandments. The Iranians don't get a pass; they had us in captivity too, as did the princes of Ishmael. There is slavery happening right now in parts of Africa, and it is not Black Americans or Israelites running it, but Arabs and Caucasians with financial power. Wars are here: seek good and not evil.

“The Lord is my strength and song, and he is become my salvation: he is my God”. He will guide us. Many of us choose the ways of the world to guide us: the job guides you, the children guide you. But each of us has to walk a path, some of us start to go off it, and we have to seek good and not evil. Proverbs 3 shows what his guiding looks like.

“My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments”. Whose law? God's laws. Your heart is your mind. You have to learn the laws and keep the commandments, and that proves the laws are the commandments. “For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee”. You want to live long? Despite all these wars, rumors of wars and mayhem throughout the world, you want peace? Do what he said.

“Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding”. Trust that the prophecies have to go in order. Iran is not going to bring in World War III; Iran will help unite the Arabs, and you are seeing it. And lean not on your own understanding: in the Christian church some of us used to say we're already saved. No, that's not the understanding. He that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved, and we don't know when that end is coming. So we keep enduring, keeping the commandments, seeking the good and not the evil. “In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths”.

That is how the Lord becomes our salvation in Exodus 15:2: trust in him, endure to the end, and do his commandments. Then the habitation we prepare him is the kingdom, where we have power and rule and every wrong done to us is turned upside down, not the pie-in-the-sky fairy tale of modern Christianity. The Lord is a man of war, and he is using these nations to bring a final battle. I pray I make it, and I pray you make it.

God told Noah, “Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.” Why was Noah chosen to be delivered with his family? Peter explains it: God “spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly”.

The old world is the world we read about in Genesis 7, and God did not spare it: he killed all flesh. Noah was righteous because he preached righteousness and kept the commandments. He was a godly man in an ungodly world, and he had received his orders from God on exactly how to build the ark and did it faithfully. His standing up for God is what brought the flood in upon the ungodly.

Why is he called the eighth person? The other seven were his wife, his three sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth, and their wives. Noah is counted eighth because a true captain, a true leader, made sure his wife, his sons and their wives were on first, and he was the last one to get on the ark. When Noah gave the word, they did not question him; they got on.

That is why men of God have to be strong. We come to the Sabbath because we are sick. We are surrounded by the world all week and fighting the sin around us and in our own thoughts, so we need to be around brothers and sisters who will correct us in righteousness.

The flood shows the mind of God for destruction. Nobody was righteous except the ones on the ark. The coming destruction, a thermonuclear war, will be on another level, and we want to be spiritually the men and women in that ark, not the ones drowning. A lot more than eight will make it this time, but very few, so do not be surprised when your family does not listen. Keep the commandments, preach righteousness, and God will deliver us.

Isaiah says “thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon.” We know from Psalms 137 that the United States of America is the daughter of Babylon, and Isaiah is speaking prophetically of Babylon the Great to come, the same one John wrote about in Revelation.

“And upon her forehead was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS.” Is that saying Babylon is one big brothel, with the main hoe in the United States pimping out the other hoes? No. It is similitude.

Think about who wrote it. John lived way after Isaiah, during the Roman Empire, long after ancient Babylon had fallen. Why would John be writing about ancient Babylon? He is talking about the same Babylon the Great Isaiah saw: the United States of America. This is not talking about Iraq.

Everybody sees it except the Israelites. They will say no one knows who this is. Are you kidding me? Our Black people, our Hispanics and Native Americans who cannot see it, we hope the Lord opens your eyes.

That is why Isaiah asks, “Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms; That made the world as a wilderness, and destroyed the cities thereof?” The man is the so-called white man running the United States, whose real power began with the atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in '45. He is weakening the nations, even his own allies like India and Japan, which depend on oil coming through the Strait of Hormuz, and God is hardening the hearts of Trump's circle to do just what he wants, as he did with Egypt.

Isaiah cries, “Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity”. We are laden: like a ladle dipped in soup, we are soaked and drenched with iniquity. A sinful nation means we break God's laws. So what is sin? Ezra answers: “Woe to them that sin, and keep not my commandments! saith the Lord.”

Sin is when we don't keep God's commandments. Brothers, put this in your arsenal. We always go to 1 John 5:3, of course, but we have to understand that it is precept upon precept, and Ezra says the same thing.

And who are the people that were given God's commandments? The twelve tribes of Israel. That is who Isaiah is calling the sinful nation. He was never talking about the Hittites or anybody but the Israelites.

This matters now because wars are here, and it is no time to think you are ready. You may wear your fringes, keep your beard right, keep the Sabbath and put the pork down, but still battle with patience, anger, a brawling spirit, an evil eye, or the weed you won't put down. Woe to them that sin. The whole head is sick: you're sick and I'm sick, and we have to keep getting right.

Isaiah says the sinful nation has “provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger”. To prove which nation that is: “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel.” Jacob was the forefather of the twelve tribes, and his name later became Israel. The statutes and the judgments were given to the nation of Israel.

“He hath not dealt so with any nation”. So for modern-day Christians to say that God is dealing with all nations and all people, they don't know the Bible.

Then: “and as for his judgments, they have not known them.” The Israelites are the ones that get judged. That is why Black people went into slavery, in the trans-Saharan slave trade and the trans-Atlantic slave trade, and many other times in history we have served our enemies in slavery.

So Isaiah was never talking about anybody but the Israelites. We are the seed of evildoers who call evil good and good evil, led astray by Christian pastors and the leaders in the mosques. From 1865 to 1965 we lived under more overt racism, but we had civility, women had a dress code, and there was an order to talk to a sister. Since 1965 we have gained almost twenty million abortions by Black women alone and the dumbest generation of children with the smartest technology. We provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, and that is why we went into slavery.
blog/2026/2026-03-08-2026-03-08-hope-ami:

“In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits”. When he is full, because he did all the destruction and robbed the nations, he shall be in straits, meaning he is going to catch hell. This is talking about the same thing as Isaiah 33:1.

“every hand of the wicked shall come upon him.” We read that in Habakkuk 2, where all the remnant of the people shall spoil him, and you can read it in Revelation 17, when NATO turns on them, because it is going to happen.

“When he is about to fill his belly, God shall cast the fury of his wrath upon him, and shall rain it upon him while he is eating.” That is the same thing Thessalonians said: when they say peace and safety, sudden destruction.

They are trying to make it look like we are the bad guys. But the real bad guys are written in the Bible, and it is the people they are friends with now, the other nations and their own people, that are going to turn on them and attack them. The Lord told us to wait upon him till the day that he rises up. We trust in our God.

“If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people.” This defines the wine of Habakkuk 2:5. Wine is a metaphor for the spirit of falsehood and lies.

So when Habakkuk says the spoiler “transgresseth by wine”, it is not speaking of a drunkard. This white man transgresses by his falsehoods: his philosophies, his political policies, his religions. That is the wine he prophesies, and he makes himself the prophet of the people with it.

That is the one in Isaiah 33:1 that spoils and deals treacherously: proud, in everybody's business, setting up his democracy wherever he goes. Isaiah 33:1 says woe to him, because when he ceases to spoil, he shall be spoiled.

When the books of Jerusalem were burned, the Lord told Ezra not to worry, and gave him the cup: “And I took it, and drank: and when I had drunk of it, my heart uttered understanding, and wisdom grew in my breast, for my spirit strengthened my memory.”

That last part is the point. God needed something to work with. The Spirit had to access Ezra's memory so that he could rewrite the records. It is like the movie Limitless: the pill opened his memory all the way back, so he could remember things he had only glanced at.

So if you do not read the Bible except on the Sabbath and you pray, Lord, open my wisdom, the Spirit comes and there is nothing in there: no memory to access and bring to your mind. Wisdom and knowledge can only be the stability of your times if the word has been put in you first, so give the Lord something to work with.

Wisdom and knowledge are the stability of our times. 2 Peter 2:14 is the flip side of that, what it looks like when your life is not stable and your mind is not saturated with the word of God: “Having eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin; beguiling unstable souls: an heart they have exercised with covetous practices; cursed children.”

Our people have eyes full of adultery and cannot cease from sin. They beguile unstable souls, the ones without the stability of the word. Our people are cursed children.

Many of us have children, and we all want them to walk right with the Lord. We train them up the best we can, just like the prophet Samuel, yet Samuel's sons went to hell off. Be mindful, especially the women: you have to know the spirits in your children. You are going to find out which ones serve the Lord and which ones don't.

“And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times.” Why is that important? The wisdom and knowledge of this Bible keeps us mentally and spiritually stable. Deuteronomy 28:28 shows the opposite: “The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart.”

Madness: our people are crazy, mentally unstable, mentally insane. Blindness: we are spiritually blind. Astonishment of heart: our people are always shocked at what is going on in the world.

That is the curse that wisdom answers. Brothers, we all need the wisdom of God and the knowledge to keep us mentally and spiritually stable. The people who know the Bible are not shocked when these things happen, because the Bible already said it; the people without it are astonished at every turn.

“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.” If any of you are dumb as a rock, ask of God. Some do not have the spirit of discernment: they see right and wrong in front of them and cannot discern it. When judgment is passed there is always that one who asks why a brother or sister had to be put out of the school when all they did was commit a little adultery. Shut up and sit down; they cannot discern. So pray, as Hezekiah laid his prayer before the Lord: pray for wisdom, knowledge and the spirit of discernment.

“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.” And give the Lord something to work with. You cannot sit at the table with a chicken leg in one hand and a steak in the other praying, Lord, help me lose weight. Likewise you pray for wisdom but the Bible is closed Sunday through Friday and opened only on the Sabbath. The views on the classes peak on Saturday and nobody watches the rest of the week, the same as Christians on Sunday. Many are called, few are chosen; this is for the chosen few that know what to do.

“For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways”: not some of his ways, all of them. Reading once a week leaves nothing for the Lord to work with.

“Let the brother of low degree rejoice in that he is exalted.” That brother is studying, reading and praying, Lord help my understanding, even when he does not understand yet. The quiet brother who did not do much talking years back becomes the one breaking down what the scriptures mean. If reading hurts your eyes, put on Bible audio at night and wake up to the scriptures.

How has the Lord “filled Zion with judgment and righteousness”? Jeremiah 23:5: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.”

This righteous Branch is Christ. He is the King who shall reign and prosper, and he is the one who executes judgment and justice in the earth. So when Isaiah 33:5 says “The Lord is exalted; for he dwelleth on high: he hath filled Zion with judgment and righteousness”, it is through Christ, the King, the King of kings.

That is our hope amid destruction. When the Lord rises up, the nations are scattered and their spoil is gathered like the gathering of the caterpillar, and the righteous Branch of David reigns over Zion with judgment and justice.

“O Lord, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee”: that is our prayer, just like Hezekiah prayed. We have to wait on the Lord. “The Lord is exalted; for he dwelleth on high: he hath filled Zion with judgment and righteousness.”

Jeremiah 9:24 shows what Israel glories in: “But let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me, that I am the Lord which exercise lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight, saith the Lord.” That is what we have to glory in, brothers: that we understand and know the Lord.

All nations do not understand and know the Lord, so they do not glory in the Lord. The judgment and righteousness the Lord delights to exercise in the earth are the same judgment and righteousness he has filled Zion with. Knowing him is Israel's glory, while the nations are scattered at the lifting up of himself.

Luke 21 shows people who are unstable in all their ways, wavering like the waves of the sea. “And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars”: eclipses of the sun, lunar eclipses, what they call blood moons. “and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity”: we are living in that time now. Perplexity means confusion. They said Venezuela was drug dealers, as they did with Manuel Noriega; they said Iraq had weapons of mass destruction and did not find one bomb. Anytime white people say it is a complex issue, it is something very easy that they don't want you to know: Maduro was selling his oil in foreign currencies, not the United States dollar; Iran was doing the same; Gaddafi wanted to.

“Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth.” Why are they afraid? We are not afraid, because wisdom and knowledge are the stability of our times: this is what the Bible was talking about, while everybody else is confused. “for the powers of heaven shall be shaken”: America, England, France, Germany.

“And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory. And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.” It is going to be almost time to go home.

But there is more to the one word perplexity: it goes into Jacob's trouble, the great tribulation that comes to try us. People want to skip the tribulation and say, war, Christ might come back tomorrow. No he won't. Jacob's trouble has to come to pass first.

Christ says it himself: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days.” People say there is no tribulation; there is going to be tribulation. Then “shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light”, as Luke read, “and the stars shall fall from heaven”: missiles. “and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken”: America, Britain, Germany, France, Russia, Canada, Spain, all those European nations, shaken with war.

How do we know the heavens are those nations? Isaiah 34: “And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine”: bombs, nuclear bombs, missiles and satellites dropping out of the sky. “For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea.” Idumea is the Greek and Roman name for Edom: America, France, Germany, Britain, Russia. That is heaven.

“And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven.” After the tribulation there is still war; so don't say there's war, we're going home tomorrow. Where is the great tribulation, Jacob's trouble?

“And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds.” He is not gathering everybody, only the elect: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect.” The elect are the Israelites, not Baptists, Pentecostals, Muslims or Catholics. That is our hope amid destruction.

For the brother who says he has a reading impediment, or that his eyes hurt: “Again, there is another that is slow, and hath need of help, wanting ability, and full of poverty.” This is a brother who is mentally slow, lacking ability, and poor.

“yet the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good, and set him up from his low estate”. The Lord lifted his head from misery, so that many who saw it marveled. It is the same as James's brother of low degree who rejoices that he is exalted.

So it is not impossible, but give the Lord something to work with. Show him that you believe and have faith, and he can do wonders. If you want to lose weight, get in the gym, eat smaller portions, walk around the block once, then twice, and let the Lord do the rest. Instead of five pieces of chicken, eat one; you won't die. In the same way, put on Bible audio if reading is hard. Do your part and the eye of the Lord will look upon you for good.

“the fear of the Lord is his treasure.” Sirach 19:20 says “The fear of the Lord is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.”

So the fear of the Lord is all wisdom. Brothers and sisters, if you don't fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.

And in all wisdom is the performance of the law: the application of God's law. We must not just talk about it; we must be about it. We must do it. The wisdom and knowledge that are the stability of our times are not only words in the head; they are the law performed, joined to the knowledge of his omnipotency. That is the treasure the Lord loves.

Psalm 60 says “Judah is my lawgiver”, when you would expect it to say Levi. Hebrews gives the reason: “For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.”

So Christ is the lawgiver. He comes from the tribe of Judah, and he is the one that gave Moses the laws. That is the Lord Isaiah speaks of: “the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king; he will save us.” Our judge, our lawgiver and our king is Christ out of Judah, and it is he who will save us when the warships and navies of the nations come down.

Isaiah says “then is the prey of a great spoil divided; the lame take the prey.” Who is the lame? Jeremiah shows it: “For thus saith the Lord; Sing with gladness for Jacob, and shout among the chief of the nations: publish ye, praise ye, and say, O Lord, save thy people, the remnant of Israel.” The Lord is not saving all Israelites; he is saving a remnant.

“Behold, I will bring them from the north country, and gather them from the coasts of the earth, and with them the blind and the lame”. The blind and the lame are Israel, with “the woman with child and her that travaileth with child together: a great company shall return thither.”

“They shall come with weeping, and with supplications will I lead them: I will cause them to walk by the rivers of waters in a straight way, wherein they shall not stumble: for I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.” Ephraim is the firstborn, meaning he was chosen over the northern kingdom.

So the lame that take the prey is Israel. When the tacklings of their ships are loosed and they cannot spread the sail, we are going to take the nations: we are going to prey on the nations.

Isaiah says “the lame take the prey. And the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick”. Jeremiah 31 showed the lame is Israel, and Christ shows the lame being made whole: “Insomuch that the multitude wondered, when they saw the dumb to speak, the maimed to be whole, the lame to walk, and the blind to see: and they glorified the God of Israel.”

The dumb speak, the maimed are whole, the lame walk and the blind see, and they glorified the God of Israel. That is the lame of Isaiah 33. The lame take the prey: we are going to take the nations and divide the spoil, and in that day the inhabitants of Jerusalem will never say, I am sick.

Isaiah ends, “And the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick: the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity.” Nobody is going to be saying they are sick. David shows why: “Bless the Lord, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name. Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits”.

Watch the benefits: “Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases; Who redeemeth thy life from destruction; who crowneth thee with lovingkindness and tender mercies”. The same Lord who forgives all our iniquities heals all our diseases, and the Lord can redeem our life from destruction.

That is the hope amid destruction. While the indignation of the Lord is upon all nations and his fury upon all their armies, the people that dwell in Jerusalem are forgiven their iniquity and healed, never to say I am sick again.

Isaiah says, “For the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king; he will save us.” The Lord is our judge, not the nations. And the Lord is our lawgiver. Brothers used to get confused over this, so David shows which tribe the lawgiver comes from: “Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; Ephraim also is the strength of mine head; Judah is my lawgiver”.

You would think it is supposed to be Levi, the priestly tribe. It says Judah. Why? Because the Lord who is our lawgiver came out of Judah, as Hebrews 7:14 shows. Christ is the lawgiver: he is the one that gave Moses the laws, and he is from Judah.

“Now will I rise, saith the Lord; now will I be exalted; now will I lift up myself. Ye shall conceive chaff, ye shall bring forth stubble: your breath, as fire, shall devour you.” What does that mean, your breath as fire shall devour you? When you speak great words and talk big talk that you can't back up with God, you are going to eat your words. Like Nicanor pointing at the temple and saying we are going to tear it to the ground. Antiochus is the example.

“Then swelling with anger, he thought to avenge upon the Jews the disgrace done unto him by those that made him flee.” He commanded his chariotman to drive without ceasing, “the judgment of God now following him. For he had spoken proudly in this sort, That he would come to Jerusalem and make it a common burying place of the Jews.” He wanted to destroy us.

“But the Lord Almighty, the God of Isreal, smote him with an incurable and invisible plague.” As soon as he had spoken those words: that is what “your breath, as fire, shall devour you” means. “A pain of the bowels that was remediless came upon him, and sore torments of the inner parts; And that most justly: for he had tormented other men’s bowels with many and strange torments.” Good for him.

“Howbeit he nothing at all ceased from his bragging, but still was filled with pride, breathing out fire in his rage against the Jews.” There it is again, breathing out fire, the bottom of Isaiah 33:11: your big talk is going to burn you up. Then “he fell down from his chariot, carried violently”: he fell off the chariot and it dragged him. It was bad enough he had stomach pains; now his whole body hurt.

“And thus he that a little afore thought he might command the waves of the sea, (so proud was he beyond the condition of man) and weigh the high mountains in a balance, was now cast on the ground” … “So that the worms rose up out of the body of this wicked man” … “and the filthiness of his smell was noisome to all his army.” He began to stink worse than shit; his whole army could smell him.

That is what is coming to the nations talking big right now. America breaks the covenant and regards no man, and Israel broke the 2024 ceasefire and advanced into Lebanon saying they will silence Hezbollah by the end of the week. Their breath as fire shall devour them.

Isaiah 33 ends: “And the people shall be as the burnings of lime: as thorns cut up shall they be burned in the fire.” There is going to be fire, but it is not the kind of fire we read about in 2 Kings, men being burnt up with fire from heaven in that way. Isaiah 9 shows what kind of fire it is.

“For every battle of the warrior is with confused noise, and garments rolled in blood.” That is how battles have always been fought: noise, confusion, men's garments rolled in blood.

“But this shall be with burning and fuel of fire.” This battle is going to be with fire. What kind of fire? Thermonuclear fire.

That is the fire of Isaiah 33, where Lebanon is ashamed and hewn down, Sharon, which is Tel Aviv, is like a wilderness, Bashan, which is Syria, and Carmel in northern Israel shake off their fruits. The highways lie waste, the wayfaring man ceases, and the valiant ones, the generals and armies, cry without. The people are burned like lime and like thorns cut up, and then the Lord says, “Hear, ye that are far off, what I have done; and, ye that are near, acknowledge my might.”

“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read: no one of these shall fail”. We must all get into the habit of consistently reading, four chapters a day minimum, because not one prophecy in it shall fail. Solomon witnessed it at the dedication of the temple:

“Blessed be the Lord, that hath given rest unto his people Israel, according to all that he promised: there hath not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by the hand of Moses his servant.”

Not one word failed of what he promised by Moses, and not one word shall fail of what he promised by Isaiah. The same God who gave Israel rest in the land according to all that he promised has promised the day of the Lord’s vengeance, “the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion”, the sword coming down upon Idumea and the great slaughter in the land of Edom. We are living the controversy of Zion now, with Amalek claiming the land is theirs.

None of the promises in this Bible shall fail. That is why we seek out of the book of the Lord and read: what he said by his prophets will come to pass just as surely as the rest he gave Israel in the days of Solomon.

Isaiah says “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read”, and Paul tells Timothy the same thing: “Till I come, give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.” Read, brothers and sisters. Give attendance to reading, to exhortation and to doctrine until Christ comes.

“Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery”: the presbytery is the congregation. Just as Timothy had the gift of the Holy Spirit within him, we all have the gift of the Holy Spirit within us. Don’t let anybody tell you that to show the gift you have to speak in tongues. John the Baptist had the gift of the Holy Spirit, anointed in his mother’s womb. Did John the Baptist speak in tongues? No. Stop listening to these Christians.

And what we read must be the book of the Lord alone. “none shall want her mate”: you cannot mate the Bible with any other book. Islam tries to do that, mixing the Quran with the Bible, and God says you cannot. “for my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them.” God’s mouth commanded these words to be written and his spirit gathered them together; “he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath divided it unto them by line”. As he divided the land of Israel by line, he gave the prophets lines to write: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel and David big portions, Obadiah, Micah, Amos, Jonah and Nahum small ones. “they shall possess it for ever”: as we will possess the land for ever, we will possess the word of God for ever, and we give attendance to reading it until he comes.

This is to the brothers who teach, the up-and-coming soldiers in the MOV program. Ezra prepared his heart to teach in Israel, and the Lord says: “Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.”

Who is speaking? The Most High said, I have made thee a watchman. It is not the Bishop that made you a watchman. It is not the deacons, and it is not the captains. The Lord called you to be a watchman. That is why you were called into this truth: to warn our people, to warn Israel that they need to repent.

Habakkuk shows the watchman's posture: “I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower”. He is awake and paying attention. As watchmen we must be faithful and pay attention to the signs of the times, hear the word at the Lord's mouth, and give Israel warning from him.

“For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.” What is the heart? The mind. Ezra had prepared his mind to seek the Lord his God. We are in captivity, always working and tired; some days you get stressed. But the Most High has to remind us that we are living in the last days. So brothers, prepare your minds; sisters, prepare your minds.

David shows who the Lord prepares: “Lord, thou hast heard the desire of the humble: thou wilt prepare their heart, thou wilt cause thine ear to hear”. We are the humble. We are supposed to humble ourselves to whatever the Bible says we ought to do.

And when we humble ourselves, the Lord hears our desire and prepares our hearts. We will prepare our minds. That is what Ezra did before he went to teach Israel, and that is what is required of us now, as we watch Iran and Israel go to war and America get involved, and more of our people wake up and repent.

Why prepare our minds and our spirits? Because war is imminent. We are seeing Iran and Israel at war and America getting involved, and the wars are only going to get worse. What we see right now is a birthing pain. Yet all of us are supposed to rejoice, because the scriptures already told us this was going to happen.

Sirach says: “They that fear the Lord will prepare their hearts, and humble their souls in his sight”. All of us that fear the Lord will prepare our minds, so that whatever evil comes upon the earth, we will remain faithful in serving the Lord.

That is Ezra's example: a heart prepared, and a soul humbled in the Lord's sight, ready to seek the law, do it, and teach it, whatever comes.

Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law and to teach it. Sirach shows why: “A man of understanding trusteth in the law; and the law is faithful unto him, as an oracle.” We must trust in the laws of God, and the law will be faithful unto us.

“Prepare what to say, and so thou shalt be heard”. We have to prepare what to say. Prepare what to say in prayer when we speak to the Most High, and we will be heard. Prepare what to say and teach in the streets, and we will be heard. We must prepare to lead, guide and organize blacks and Hispanics.

“and bind up instruction, and then make answer.” Bind up the instruction first, and then make answer. That is how Ezra could teach in Israel statutes and judgments: he had prepared his heart before he opened his mouth.

These are the kind of people we are trying to persuade to change: “Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane.” It is for our people who are lawless.

“For murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers.” If you knew a brother murdered his father or his mother, you would not treat him the same; your instant reaction is, bro, you cold, who does that? “For manslayers”: imagine being cool with a brother and not knowing the whole time he had bodies on him. But there is repentance for those spirits. These are the spirits we are trying to win over and get to submit to the Lord.

“For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind”: women with all kinds of men, men with all kinds of women, and homosexuality. There is repentance for all of these sins. Some of us are struggling with one, two, three, four, five of these. God damn. We have demons on us.

The only way to get it out is to have one counsellor of a thousand and open up. That is the problem: some of you don't want to open up, and by the time we find out what you are struggling with, it's too late to help. It doesn't mean you can't repent, but it is a lot harder because you kept it secret so long, and by the time you tell us you are already having sex and we have to throw you out. Repent, submit yourself to the Lord, and stay close with the pack.

“For menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine.” How many of us lie? We all lie. Why didn't you come to the Sabbath? My back, I was tired: a lie. Why didn't you come to the new moon? I got off work late: a lie, because in your mind you already said, I'll go next time.

Can you persuade a murderer, a lesbian, a homosexual to change their life? Can you turn a liar or a thief into a soldier? You can, and the proof is that you are sitting in the building. Don't say only Deacon Eythan or Black Rhino knows how to talk to people.

Isaiah sees the war coming on Babylon and the prophets still lifting up the banner and exalting the voice. Paul says why we do it: “Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men.” In Job he is called the king of terrors. We know what the Lord is going to do. The Lord set us up as watchmen, and since we know the terror of the Lord, we must persuade men.

“But we are made manifest unto God; and I trust also are made manifest in your consciences.”

Who are we trying to persuade? Our people, in the midst of all kinds of sin. So brothers, we must be studying, so that when we come across our people we are able to help them. The scripture says the whole head is sick: we are sick individuals ourselves. But we must learn to discipline ourselves, and we must learn how to persuade our people to change their lives.

We are to persuade our people, but this is what we have to overcome: “Surely he knoweth your inventions, and what ye think in your hearts, even them that sin, and would hide their sin.” That is what we do. We sin, and we hide our sin.

The Lord says, I know your inventions. I know why you watch HBO at night; I know why you like Spartacus, why you like Power. I know you love to smoke weed and spray yourself with cologne right before you come to the Sabbath, and then security says, that brother smells like weed. Keep smoking weed and you will end up face down in the street like the man in the video, calling the officer papi.

Some brothers are tied to unbelieving wives who cook pork on the same grill next to your lawful food, still go to the club and don't respect you, and you refuse to leave. Sisters are tied to unbelieving men. There is no love among our people, and we are caught up in these sins, lawless, like 1 Timothy 1:9.

You can hide it from the brothers and the sisters, but you cannot hide it from the Lord. He knows your inventions and what you think in your heart. So before we can persuade our people, we have to get ourselves right.

“That there should not be such heaviness in their destruction, as shall be joy over them that are persuaded to salvation.” We must persuade men to salvation. We see the wars going on with Iran; we see the prophecies coming to pass and escalating. But the Lord told us, go persuade my people to salvation, go bring them into the sanctuary.

How do we do it? Proverbs 25:15: “By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.” To forbear is to patiently restrain. A prince is a very high rank, and with long patience you can persuade even princes. And what does Israel mean? Prince of the power. We have to be patient with the Israelites.

As teachers, be patient and strategic. When you are having that conversation, don't think they are just wicked as hell; they might actually repent, but you were not patient enough. Be diplomatic, learn how to reason. When people come up to you in the street, don't hit them with the first death scripture. You were once in that spot, and the only reason we are in this building is that the Lord opened our eyes.

A soft tongue breaks the bone: somebody can be pissed with you, and you respond with peace. You from Brooklyn, from DC, from PG County, want to respond even more aggressive. But the joy over one of our people persuaded to salvation is greater than the heaviness over the destruction of the rest.

“The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz did see. Lift ye up a banner upon the high mountain, exalt the voice unto them, shake the hand.” The high mountain is the government, America. The banner we lift up upon it is the Bible. So in the midst of all this chaos, Isaiah sees the prophets still going out teaching.

“Exalt the voice unto them”: that is what we do, and Isaiah 58 says how. “Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet, and shew my people their transgression, and the house of Jacob their sins.” We exalt the voice, we spare not, we lift up our voice as a trumpet.

“Shake the hand”: warn our people, “that they may go into the gates of the nobles.” The nations have drunk Babylon's wine, her lies and philosophies, what Daniel calls her policy, and therefore the nations are mad. War is coming, and in the midst of all that war, the prophets are still crying aloud, showing our people their transgression so they can be saved.

Isaiah gives an analogy of a farmer: “Doth the plowman plow all day to sow? doth he open and break the clods of his ground?” He breaks the dirt, makes the ground flat, and casts abroad his seeds. But is Isaiah really talking about farmland?

Paul answers it: “Or saith he it altogether for our sakes? For our sakes, no doubt, this is written: that he that ploweth should plow in hope; and that he that thresheth in hope should be partaker of his hope.” It wasn't really talking about farms. The plowing and the threshing were not about growing seeds.

The plowing represents teaching. We are to plow in hope: to teach, instruct, and give hope to our people. You brothers are fishers of men, and the field is our people. That is how Isaiah 28 applies to you.

So the fitches, cummin, principal wheat, appointed barley and rye are the different people we plow for, and the farmer's instruments are the different ways we must deal with them to persuade them to salvation. By long forbearing even a prince is persuaded, and Israel is a prince: we have to be patient with our people.

The farmer casts “the principal wheat and the appointed barley” in their place, and there is a time to grow barley: you have to know when to show mercy, when to be strong and assertive, when to be diplomatic, and whom to talk to. “his God doth instruct him to discretion”: careful and circumspect in speech and action, to avoid causing offence or to gain an advantage. You know how to speak, and you know when to speak.

You may say, I'm putting my time in teaching this brother and he won't come to the school. Read this: “To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven”. Not to some things, not to little things: to every thing there is a season.

So when we're fishing, there is a time to talk about the truth with that brother. Sometimes you're talking out of season. He was stressed from work, things were going on, his mind just wasn't open, and you didn't discern it. But if you pay attention and watch, the moment comes: Leroy calls and says, I was watching this documentary about the space landing, and I'm starting to think this world isn't what I thought it was. Got him. You waited two years for Leroy, and Leroy opened up.

At the end of the day the Lord brings them in. But we are at war, Russia and China are about to get involved, and it's only going to get worse. We have to be better fishermen, and be patient with our brothers and sisters.

The fitches are not threshed with a threshing instrument, nor the cummin under a cart wheel; each seed has its own instrument. Even the disciples used the wrong one. The Samaritans “did not receive him, because his face was as though he would go to Jerusalem. And when his disciples James and John saw this, they said, Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them, even as Elias did?” Let's go get the death scriptures; let's pray the Lord takes them out.

“But he turned, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of.” Brothers, you have to know what manner of spirit you're supposed to be in when you deal with the people in the street. Sisters, the same way. Sometimes the brothers do the work, the people come in, and the sisters undo the work by not saying hello, shalom, or Christ bless. Sisters need to learn how to fish too.

Always represent this truth with the utmost professionalism, because we have a job: to win souls, and we don't have much time. As soon as you step into a room or a store, map out whom you think you can bring the truth to. You don't have to be a soldier to do that. Brother O'Shea in New York is 83; he hands out his fifty flyers a week, and the home health aide who came to him from the nursing home started wearing dresses.

We must be fishers of men, because war is imminent and danger is coming. Knowing the right spirit for each person is the discretion God instructs the plowman in.

When we teach the Bible and bring out the prophecy, in the street or in classes, what are these scriptures supposed to do for our people? The prophet told King Asa: “Be ye strong therefore, and let not your hands be weak: for your work shall be rewarded.” The days we are living in now are not the time for us to be weak.

“And when Asa heard these words, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage, and put away the abominable idols out of all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and out of the cities which he had taken from mount Ephraim”. When Asa heard the words of the prophecy, he took courage.

That is what prophecy is supposed to do for us: give us the courage to let go of our idols and our secret sins. We are seeing prophecy unravel right before our eyes: Iran and Israel going to war, and now America getting involved. It was a rumor and talk for years, and now we see it unfold. That means more Israelites are repenting, and more of our brothers and our people are waking up. That is the doctrine poured out as prophecy, laboured for all them that seek wisdom.

“Behold, speak thou in the ears of my people the words of prophecy, which I will put in thy mouth, saith the Lord”. Speak in the ears of my people. That is why in Ezekiel he said not to go to a people of a strange speech: we have to deal with our people.

“And cause them to be written in paper: for they are faithful and true.” Everything written in the Bible is faithful and true.

“Fear not the imaginations against thee, let not the incredulity of them trouble thee, that speak against thee. For all the unfaithful shall die in their unfaithfulness.” Do not fear what the nations are going to do to us for teaching against America and against governments. The Bible says do not fear.

“Behold, saith the Lord, I will bring plagues upon the world; the sword, famine, death, and destruction.” The Most High says he is going to bring judgment upon the world. That is the doctrine Sirach says was poured out as prophecy and left to all ages, and we do not labour for ourselves only: we speak it in the ears of our people.

“I will yet make doctrine to shine as the morning, and will send forth her light afar off.” Peter says, “We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed”. Take heed to do what the scriptures say. The Most High called us into this truth, so we have to take heed.

“as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts”. We are that light shining in a dark place. That is why Christ said, let your light so shine before men. We have to be that example for our people, to win them over into the faith. Whether you are in DC, New Orleans, California or the UK, the Most High chose us, and through our example we have to win our people over.

“Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation. For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.” Prophecy is the foretelling of future events in the Bible, and it did not come by the will of man. Holy men of God, holy black men, holy Hispanic men, spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost. That is the light sent forth afar off.

Sirach says “I will yet pour out doctrine as prophecy, and leave it to all ages for ever.” With a war between America and Iran unfolding and many prophecies being fulfilled, we look at what the Bible says about prophecy itself.

“Blessed is he that readeth, and they that hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written therein: for the time is at hand.” Blessed is he that reads and hears, and keeps the things written therein. What is written in the scriptures? The laws of the Most High God.

So the blessing is not only in reading the prophecy but in keeping the law. We are blessed when we read and keep the things written in the law, because the time is at hand, and the doctrine poured out as prophecy was left for all ages, including ours.

Matthew 1 is “The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham”: the link between Christ and the royal seat promised through David's loins, through Solomon and their sons. At the end of it: “Eliud begat Eleazar; and Eleazar begat Matthan; and Matthan begat Jacob; And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary”. Someone claimed Jacob and Heli were brothers. You do not read that anywhere in the Bible.

Luke 3: “And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli”. Did it say the son of Heli? No. “As was supposed” refers to him being the son of Joseph. It had nothing to do with Heli at all.

Now line them up. Luke goes on: “Which was the son of Matthat, which was the son of Levi, which was the son of Melchi”. Even if Matthat and Matthan were the same man spelled differently, Matthan's father in Matthew is Eleazar, and in Luke Matthat's father is Levi. Eliud and Eleazar are not mentioned in Luke 3 at all. These are two completely different bloodlines. They do not expect you to bounce back and forth and make sure it lines up; they bank on you not fact-checking.

Matthew starts with Joseph: the angel comes to Joseph, you follow his story, and his lineage is given. Luke chose to follow Mary: it begins with her cousin Elisabeth and the babe leaping in her womb, and in the third chapter it gives her lineage, all men. That is why not one woman is named in Luke 3, while some women are named in Matthew 1. Where it would have said Mary, it names her husband.

And “Booz begat Obed of Ruth” is where the levirate marriage actually shows up, but we will not be bamboozled by a spin move into an Old Testament law that has nothing to do with the question. Not knowing something does not make you an idiot. Pick up the phone and ask a Bishop or a Deacon. Making it up does.

“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments”. You cannot have a good understanding if you are not keeping the commandments. It is biblically impossible to understand this Bible while you are not observing the laws of God. There is no way around it. All the foolishness that gets exposed comes from those that refuse to repent and keep God's commandments.

That is why Christ's message from the start was this: “From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.”

So many of our brothers and sisters out in the world have yet to come to grips with what we are here for. Being an Israelite in Christ is not about dressing up as an Israelite. It's not about arguing with white folks in the streets. It's not about flexing your muscles and trying to be a tough guy. And no, it is not about multiple wives.

Being an Israelite in Christ is about observing the Most High God's commandments and faith in his Son, so that we don't die when the Lord returns. The kingdom of heaven is at hand, and you are at risk if you do not repent and seek the kingdom. Point blank, period.

Those who deny Christ and deny keeping the commandments, because they want to fulfil their own lust, come up with absurd breakdowns of scripture. Without repentance there is no good understanding.

“Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith.” What are the works Paul is talking about? Not what your son did today while you were at work. One so-called leader stood up and asked a room if you go home and ask your son what his deeds were today. Who does that? He is an idiot, and whoever listens to him needs to repent.

Chronicles shows what the works are: “And in every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the law, and in the commandments, to seek his God, he did it with all his heart, and prospered.” The works are the works done in the service of the house of God: the sacrificial law.

Earlier in the same chapter, “Hezekiah appointed the courses of the priests and the Levites after their courses, every man according to his service, the priests and Levites for burnt offerings and for peace offerings”. Those are the works of God in the temple.

So when Paul says boasting is excluded, it means you cannot boast that you are sacrificing, as though it makes you something special, because that is done: Christ died for us. The justification is through Christ, by faith, not by the works of the temple service.

This is one of the first scriptures we learned when we came into this truth, elementary but important: “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.” An elder has men under him who look to him for wisdom, knowledge and understanding. The brother who said a man’s deeds are what his son did today embarrassed the hell out of himself and his organization. Now he is being clowned, and because he represents the Israelite community, they label us all as stupid. And never trust a man wearing dark sunglasses inside: he can hide his embarrassment and his eyes. Brother, you have to repent and change your ways.

“But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness.” That is profane and vain babbling; it doesn’t make any sense. And nobody in the room, nobody equal to his rank, says, hey, listen, brother, next time. He keeps having a pattern of doing the same thing.

Here, if a captain starts talking crazy, a captain junior to him is going to correct him, because we represent Israel United in Christ, and our elders have taught us with knowledge, wisdom and understanding how to conduct ourselves. There are checks and balances. That brother does not have any of that, and so he cannot rightly divide Romans 3.

“Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.” What are the deeds of the law? Nehemiah shows them: “Then contended I with the rulers, and said, Why is the house of God forsaken? And I gathered them together, and set them in their place.” We are talking about the house of God.

“Then brought all Judah the tithe of the corn and the new wine and the oil unto the treasuries.” This is what they brought: the offerings. He “made treasurers over the treasuries, Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and of the Levites, Pedaiah”, “for they were counted faithful, and their office was to distribute unto their brethren.”

“Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God, and for the offices thereof.” The deeds were the sacrifices and offerings he brought to the house of God.

And it is in the same chapter of Romans where God is justified in his sayings and overcomes when he is judged: let God be true, and every man a liar. This is serious. Your salvation is at hand, and a teacher who is up at the podium drinking, talking about sex and baby oil and prostitution, instead of instructing the people what these scriptures are talking about, is not a leader to lead people to God. He is a joke.

How do you identify a leader? Some people say you can’t say he’s not a leader. Yes, we can, because you can tell who a man is by his speech. Sirach gives the rubric: “Leaders of the people by their counsels, and by their knowledge of learning meet for the people, wise and eloquent are their instructions”.

Leaders of the people by their counsels: you should be able to tell by their godly counsel, coming from the Bible, whether or not they are leaders of the people. By their knowledge of learning meet for the people: Bishop just showed the works in Chronicles and the deeds in Nehemiah 13, proving what Romans 3 means. Wise and eloquent are their instructions.

The leaders here in Israel United in Christ prove everything they say with the scriptures. That is why I am here. Why are you there? What is your agenda? Are you there because he talks about baby oil? Are you there because he cannot break down Romans 3? The Bible is the rubric that lets us know who the real leaders are and who are not.
