“And the Philistines came up yet again, and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.” “And when David enquired of the Lord”: David sought counsel of the Lord. David used to talk to the Lord: Lord, should I go up now? Should I do this? Should I do that?

We have to learn to do that. Before you make a decision, talk to the Lord: I want to do this, but show me what's right, show me should I do this or not; and if it's not right, Lord, shut it down. Sisters, do that when you are marrying some of these brothers: Lord, if this brother ain't right, shut it down. Brothers, do that too: Lord, if this sister is a demon, make me see it. You can talk to the Lord. He does hear you; you are not talking to yourself.

The Lord answered, “Thou shalt not go up; but fetch a compass behind them, and come upon them over against the mulberry trees.” Don't go up right now; go around them and come up behind them, behind the mulberry trees. This goes back to the Lord teaching David how to war.

“And let it be, when thou hearest the sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry trees, that then thou shalt bestir thyself: for then shall the Lord go out before thee, to smite the host of the Philistines.” See in your mind what is taking place: when you hear me running on top of the mulberry trees, the Lord running on top of the trees, then rush yourself. I am going out before you. I'm there fighting with you, David, and we are going to smite the host of the Philistines.

That is the wars of the Lord, and it is what David meant before Goliath: “for the battle is the Lord’s, and he will give you into our hands.” The Lord goes out before his people and fights with them. When you read the Maccabees, angels came down and fought with Judas Maccabeus too, shielding him so nobody could hit him.

David said to Goliath, “Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel”. When we fight and when we war, we war in the name of our God. Then Psalm 144 shows where David's fighting came from: “Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight”.

This is David, and he says God is his strength, and it is God that teaches his hands to war. David understood that the Lord was with him in every fight and every battle he was in, and the Lord was the one teaching him how to fight. David didn't go to no kung fu school. The Lord was literally teaching David how to fight. David chased a lion and killed it; David was fighting with bears. How was he able to do that? The Lord was with him.

“and my fingers to fight”: and my fingers to punch a dude and break his teeth. Y'all don't be doing that to nobody today, unless you are defending yourself.

So the Lord is our strength, brothers. Always remember that. That is how you learn to war and fight: the Lord is with you, and you can't war without the Lord warring with you. That is why David could tell the Philistine, “This day will the Lord deliver thee into mine hand”, “that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel”, and that “the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord’s”. Anytime you go to war, it's the Lord that's with you fighting.

Do not be afraid of armies and people; teach the word of God no matter what they threaten you with. You are not going to be a servant of God and have everything be good. You are not going to be a soldier in Christ and not suffer.

“Forasmuch then as Christ hath suffered for us in the flesh, arm yourselves likewise with the same mind”. The same way Christ suffered for us in the flesh, when the Romans crucified him, lynched him and beat him, you have to arm yourself with that same mind. If your mind is not ready to suffer the same way Christ suffered, you are not a soldier in Christ. The Bible is telling you what is going to happen, but some of you are in la-la land.

Eventually an army is going to surround my house, and they are going to lie on me and call me a terrorist or something stupid like that. I already know that is what they will do, so I prepare my mind. Federal agents are waiting to set you up. Do you think the American government is going to let us keep teaching and waking Israel up and just leave us alone? Read about COINTELPRO. Do you think that stopped? We are going up against a wicked, evil people who will put you away for the rest of your life and lie on you, knowing you did not do it, because of the teachings of Christ.

“for he that hath suffered in the flesh hath ceased from sin”. That is how you become perfect: you have to go through things and suffer in the flesh. Those of you who want a comfortable life, this truth is not for you. The battle is the Lord’s, and he fights with us, but we arm our minds to suffer as Christ did.

“for the battle is not yours, but God’s.” Why does the battle belong to the Lord? Because the Lord is always there fighting with you, even though you cannot see him. Even when you are doing evil, the angels are right there watching and writing down everything you do; the eyes of the Lord are open on all of us. For those who do not believe the Lord is with them and fighting with them, for those with weak faith, look at Elisha.

“And when the servant of the man of God was risen early, and gone forth, behold, an host compassed the city both with horses and chariots. And his servant said unto him, Alas, my master! how shall we do?” A whole army surrounded the city, and they came for this one prophet, this one brother.

“And he answered, Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.” As men of God you have to realize the Lord is always with you, and those with you are stronger than those with the enemy. “And Elisha prayed, and said, Lord, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see. And the Lord opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.” Chariots of fire: angels, just waiting for the word. A man’s army surrounded Elisha, and the Lord’s army surrounded that army, waiting to set it off.

You cannot see things spiritually, but understand: the Lord is with us, his angels are with us, and the Lord is fighting with us. There is no way we could do what the Lord sent us to do on this earth, and no way you would see the growth of IUIC and of Israel, if he were not with us. And it will be the same in the future: they came for one prophet, and federal agents will surround the houses of some of you who teach the word of God. That is the mind you have to have. So be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of the great multitude.

Paul speaks of the same thing Moses did in Deuteronomy 4. “See that ye refuse not him that speaketh. For if they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth”: the one that spoke on earth is Moses. The people said, we do not want to hear God, lest we die; Moses, you tell us what he says. Moses gave us the laws, we refused them from Moses, and everybody was killed in the wilderness.

“much more shall not we escape, if we turn away from him that speaketh from heaven”. The one speaking from heaven was the Lord. “Whose voice then shook the earth”. When he spoke the commandments the earth was shaking, and that is why the people were terrified and said, Moses, you speak to us. “but now he hath promised, saying, Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven.” He is going to shake nations: that is when he returns in the future. The Lord already knew we would go off and that he would have to come again to deliver us. Then those things “which cannot be shaken may remain”, and we receive “a kingdom which cannot be moved”.

“For our God is a consuming fire.” Why does Paul say this? Because that is what the people saw. The Lord said, do not let anybody come near the mountain when I come down, because anyone who comes near will die. When he came down it was a consuming fire; that is all everybody saw, except the seventy elders, who had the Holy Spirit on them and saw his majesty. That is Deuteronomy 4:36: “upon earth he shewed thee his great fire; and thou heardest his words out of the midst of the fire”, the fire that issues forth from his throne.

“Out of heaven he made thee to hear his voice, that he might instruct thee”. Whose voice did they hear from the heavens? Some people think that is the Father. No, that was Christ's voice. That was the Lord speaking, the one who came down and gave us the commandments.

Christ said it himself: “And the Father himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape.” The Father sent Christ and bore witness of him, but at no time in history have you ever heard the Father's voice, and you never saw his shape.

So the voice our people heard in the wilderness, out of the midst of the fire, was Christ's. And the shape the seventy elders saw when the Lord came down was Christ. It was always the Lord, always Christ there: the rock and the chariot that followed us, the one who came down and smote the Egyptians, the same one who will come back in the future and smite spiritual Egypt that we are living in today.

Exodus 14 is one of the wars of the Lord: the Lord fought for Israel, overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea, and “there remained not so much as one of them.” Paul looks back on the same crossing: “Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea”.

That cloud is a chariot. And who is Paul speaking to? The Corinthians. If all their fathers passed through the sea, then the Corinthians were Israel. Did the Egyptians pass through the sea? No. And some will say there was a mixed multitude; the mixed multitude came out lusting after evil things and all died in the wilderness. If the wicked of our own people did not make it, what about the mixed multitude?

“And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”: baptized unto Moses means Moses taught us; he taught us God's laws. “And did all eat the same spiritual meat; And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.”

Who was following us in the wilderness? Christ. Who killed the Egyptians? Christ. The Lord who fought for Israel at the Red Sea, the one Moses wrote of, was always Christ, and he is the one who will come back and smite spiritual Egypt, the land we live in today.

In Exodus 14:19-20 “the pillar of the cloud went from before their face, and stood behind them: And it came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel; and it was a cloud and darkness to them, but it gave light by night to these”. Who was in that pillar? Exodus 13:21 says it: “And the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night”.

Who went before them in the pillar of cloud? Christ. That pillar of cloud is a chariot, and the Lord was inside it. It is the Rock that followed them in 1 Corinthians 10. Imagine seeing something bright, what you would call a UFO today, come down and stand between you and your enemy. The Egyptians saw that, and you know they were afraid.

“He took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, from before the people.” Day and night it was with them. And it was through that same “pillar of fire and of the cloud” that the Lord looked unto the host of the Egyptians in the morning watch, troubled them and took off their chariot wheels, until they said “Let us flee from the face of Israel; for the Lord fighteth for them against the Egyptians.”

Who is the Almighty word that leaped down off his throne? “The first man is of the earth, earthy: the second man is the Lord from heaven.” The Lord from heaven is Christ. He is the one who came down and killed the Egyptians in Exodus, and that is why Moses says the Lord is a man of war.

Paul says the same thing about the wilderness: our fathers “drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” And Exodus 13:21: “the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire”. That pillar of cloud was a chariot, and the Lord inside it was Christ. Who was following us in the wilderness? Christ. Who killed the Egyptians? Christ.

So when Exodus 15:3 says “the Lord is his name”, it is speaking of the anointed. He smote the Egyptians, and the same way he is going to come back in the future and smite spiritual Egypt, the land we are living in today.

Some people still question it and say the Lord in Exodus 15:3 is the Father. Solomon gave the same account Moses gave. “For while all things were in quiet silence, and that night was in the midst of her swift course, Thine Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of thy royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction”.

Who is the word of God? The anointed, Christ. He has a royal throne in the heavens, and during Exodus he leaped off his throne and came down for war. So when Moses says “The Lord is a man of war”, he is speaking of the word of God that came down at the Passover, killed the Egyptians and drowned them in the Red Sea. Moses said it because he saw the Lord warring for his people.

He “brought thine unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death; and it touched the heaven, but it stood upon the earth.” The Lord filled all things with death when he came down in Exodus. A lot of you do not fully understand what Passover is really about: it is about death and destruction of our enemies.

“Then suddenly visions of horrible dreams troubled them sore, and terrors came upon them unlooked for. And one thrown here, and another there, half dead, shewed the cause of his death. For the dreams that troubled them did foreshew this, lest they should perish, and not know why they were afflicted.” The Lord sent the Egyptians horrible visions and dreams; he was afflicting them and warring with them. That is the right hand of Exodus 15:6 that “hath dashed in pieces the enemy.”

Isaiah says, “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read.” The book of the Lord is the Bible, and whose book is it? Hebrews answers: “Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.”

Christ comes in the volume of the book. Everybody has to understand that. The Lord comes in the volume of the book, and it is written of him. When you read the Bible and it says the Lord said this and the Lord did that, it is talking about Christ. He is the one who was speaking right through the scriptures, and he is the one who was dealing with us right through the scriptures.

So tie it back to Isaiah: seek ye out of the book of the Lord, the book of the Lord. What we read there is written of him; that is him, the Lord, right there. And because it is his book and his word, “no one of these shall fail.” Nothing written in it will fail. Everything we read about in it is going to come to pass, whether you believe or not, and you cannot mate the Bible with any other book.

“for my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them.” The words on those pages are the Lord’s spirit, the words of Christ, who came in the volume of the book to do the will of God.

Christ says, “For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me.” Moses wrote of Christ. When you read it in Genesis, in Exodus, in Numbers, in Deuteronomy, right through the scriptures, the one Moses was talking about when he wrote “the Lord said” and “the Lord did” was always Christ. That is why Christ can say that if you believed Moses you would have believed him.

“But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?” The writings of Moses and the words of Christ stand together; to reject one is to reject the other.

This is the book Isaiah sends us to: “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read.” Read with Hebrews 10:7, where Christ says “in the volume of the book it is written of me”, it shows that the whole book of the Lord, from the writings of Moses on, is written of Christ. So when we seek out of that book and read, we are reading of him, and “no one of these shall fail”: everything written there is going to come to pass.

“Now the acts of David the king, first and last, behold, they are written in the book of Samuel the seer, and in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the book of Gad the seer”. We have the book of Samuel, but do we have a book of Nathan the prophet? Do we have a book of Gad the seer? We are missing Nathan and Gad.

Nathan the prophet wrote a book where the Lord showed him certain things. A seer is a prophet: somebody that sees things, sees the future. These look like the books the Lord told Ezra to show only to the wise, because in them are things not everybody can understand.

So we see in part. “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face”. The glass we see through darkly is the Bible. God told Moses to hide some things, so we get bits and pieces; one apostle explains it here and another there, and we put together the full picture piece by piece. We don't have all the books, but we have enough to get the understanding to get the kingdom. When Christ comes, he will teach us face to face, and whatever you are confused about now, the Lord will make it clear.

“And the rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, are they not written in the book of the acts of Solomon?” So there is a book called the acts of Solomon, and we don't have it today. I would love to read that book.

Some of those books are full of what Ezra was told of the seventy: “For in them is the spring of understanding, the fountain of wisdom, and the stream of knowledge.” Things Solomon revealed there, the Lord likely did not want us to know today, so he made it that we don't have possession of those books now.

That is also why the other books out there are left alone: Enoch, Jasher, the letter of Thomas and all that crazy stuff. This is warfare. Evil communication will corrupt you. You go reading that and certain thoughts start coming to your mind, and where did those thoughts come from? From that book you read. If you think you are strong enough to read it, that's on you, but it could confuse you. I'm going to stay with what the Lord gave us.

The southern kingdom had its chronicles, and so did the northern: “And the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he warred, and how he reigned, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.” So there is a book called the chronicles of the kings of Israel, and we don't have that today either.

The book of Jasher is missing the same way. Is it that book of Jasher they have out there on the Bible apps? No. Those of y'all that have Bible apps, leave that book alone. It is said to contradict a lot of the Bible, and the books of all the prophets complement each other; they do not contradict each other. If you read a book talking about angels having sex with women, or Esau being saved, and all kind of wacky things, that is Esau making stuff up to throw you off.

There is a real book of Jasher, and the Pope and them likely have it in the Vatican, in those catacombs. But they put misinformation out there to try to confuse the prophets.

So the chronicles of the kings of Judah and of the kings of Israel, and the book of Jasher, are named in the scriptures but are not in our hands. What is out there under their names is not to be trusted.

In 2 Esdras 14 the Lord had Ezra write the books over: “In forty days they wrote two hundred and four books.” The first were to be published openly, “that the worthy and unworthy may read it”, but the seventy last were kept back. The scriptures themselves show that this is true, because they name books we do not have.

Joshua 10:13 is the first: “Is not this written in the book of Jasher?” There is a book of Jasher, part of the Bible, one of the books Ezra wrote over, and we don't have it today.

Then 1 Kings: “Now the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?” So there is a book called the chronicles of the kings of Judah. Guess what? We don't have that book.

Rehoboam's acts were written down in full, and the Bible sends you to that book for the rest of them. The book is named, but it is not in our hands. It is another witness that more was written than what we hold today.

“Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer unto his God, and the words of the seers that spake to him in the name of the Lord God of Israel, behold, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel.” That is another book, the book of the kings of Israel.

We do have the prayer of Manasseh; it is in the Apocrypha. But that prayer is also part of the book of the kings of Israel, and that book we don't have.

So what are we to do with the books we don't have? Christ answers it in Revelation: “But that which ye have already hold fast till I come.” Today we have 80 books. Don't go looking for other books, and don't try to mix in something someone just found, like a book called Lilith, Adam's second wife. Leave all those books alone.

Read on: “And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations”. If you overcome your lust, the temptations and the white man's lies, and hold on to that little faith and that little understanding you got from these 80 books, you will rule the nations. What is in these 80 books, the laws and the prophecies of what is going to take place, we can get the kingdom with that.

“His prayer also, and how God was intreated of him, and all his sin, and his trespass, and the places wherein he built high places, and set up groves and graven images, before he was humbled: behold, they are written among the sayings of the seers.” So there is a book called the sayings of the seers, the same name as Captain Horab's show, and we don't have it today.

The Lord took those books away. Why? Because some things in them we are not to understand today. He wants us to just trust in him. Some of the things he did back then, he does not want us to have in these last days. And some books were taken away so that the white man could come and lie on the earth and spread all these lies, because some things in those other books were too plain for us to understand. Even though the Vatican took those books and hid them, the Lord allowed that.

One of those missing books is the heart of this class: “Wherefore it is said in the book of the wars of the Lord”. The Lord there is Christ. He is not only going to war in the future; he has been warring since the beginning. We don't have that book, but we can go into the scriptures and see its record in parts, as here in Joshua 10, where the sun stood still until Israel had avenged themselves upon their enemies.

“Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, first and last, are they not written in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer against Jeroboam the son of Nebat?” Nathan's book is another we are supposed to have. There is also a prophet called Ahijah who wrote books we know nothing about, and Iddo the seer, another prophet, another book.

Those prophets went into some heavy stuff. Ask yourself why, in the time of the Greeks, when Antiochus came against us, Judas Maccabeus, the woman with the seven sons and our forefathers thought the way they did. They were ready to die. Even that group that said, I'd rather die than fight on the Sabbath, just kill me, I'm going to die in my innocency. They had a level of understanding that they got from those seventy books. We are not learning about regeneration and certain things today, but they were far past that back then.

They understood things that we are just starting to figure out piece by piece today. That is why we will never say we understand everything or have one hundred percent truth: “now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.” Our flesh cannot contain some of these things, and when Christ returns we will know.

By Jericho, Joshua saw a man standing over against him “with his sword drawn in his hand”, and Joshua stepped to him: “Art thou for us, or for our adversaries?” You for me or for my enemies? Let me know. And he answered, “Nay; but as captain of the host of the Lord am I now come.” Who is the captain of the host of the Lord? This is talking about Christ, and Hebrews shows it.

“But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.” He came down a little lower than the angels when he came the last time. Before that, in Exodus, he did not come a little lower than the angels; he came down like an angel. That is how he stood before Joshua with his sword drawn.

“For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect”. The captain of our salvation is the captain of the host of the Lord, the Lord of armies, that we read about with Joshua in Joshua 5. That was Christ who was there.

This is the book of the wars of the Lord. The same Christ who led the host when Israel came out of Egypt and conquered the land, and who is the captain of our salvation, is the one who fights for Israel. Joshua fell on his face and worshipped him, because the battle is the Lord's.

The first vial brings “a noisome and grievous sore.” Noisome means foul smelling, harmful, noxious, extremely offensive to the senses, particularly the smell: a real nasty sore. It is the same plague that came on ancient Egypt, a boil breaking forth upon man and upon beast throughout all the land.

The record shows what noisome looks like on a man. When the Lord struck the wicked king Antiochus, “the worms rose up out of the body of this wicked man, and whiles he lived in sorrow and pain, his flesh fell away, and the filthiness of his smell was noisome to all his army.” His flesh fell off him and his stink offended his whole army.

What could make a man get like that? A nuclear bomb explosion causes severe radiation burns, known as cutaneous radiation injury, that frequently lead to intense itching, blistering and open sores. The burns come in stages: first redness and swelling, then a latent phase, then severe blistering and deep, long lasting necrotic ulcers. When a nuclear bomb goes off and the blast does not kill you, you are going to be rotten, your skin falling off, and it is going to be noisome.

That is how we know this first plague belongs to that one hour, when the destruction comes on America, modern day Egypt: the same kind of sore that ate Antiochus alive falls on the men who have the mark of the beast.

The key thing in the verse is who the sore falls on: “upon the men which had the mark of the beast, and upon them which worshipped his image.” If it is only them, where are we? What happened to us? We are delivered.

Psalms 91 explains why. “He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.” If you dwell in the secret place of the Most High, you dwell in his shadow, meaning his protection. “I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.”

“Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the noisome pestilence.” That is the first plague, the noisome pestilence, and the Lord will deliver you from it. That is why the scripture says the plague fell only on those that worship the beast and have his mark: because we are delivered.

This plague is coming in that one hour, and in that one hour, when the bombs are falling, it is not going to come near us. The radioactive waves, the noisome pestilence, the poisoned water will not touch us, because the Lord is going to deliver us up out of here. The same pestilence that destroys America passes over the people who dwell under his shadow.
blog/2026/2026-04-25-2026-04-25-judgemen:
“And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever.” Why a sign? When you see a McDonald's sign, it lets you know a McDonald's is there. The curses have to be upon us for a sign because we would be cut off from our heritage, and in the future Judah will need to identify who Israel is. How do you identify the Israelites today? By the curses.

Deuteronomy 32:26 shows why: “I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. We were scattered into corners in slavery, and the remembrance of who we are, our nationality, all of it, has ceased from among men. We did not just forget because time went on. We forgot because the nations made war with us and took crafty counsel: make sure those slaves cannot read and write. They destroyed us as a people and took our nationality. Ask a Chinese man today who the Israelites are, and he points at the fake people in the land, the synagogue of Satan.

Yet go to Africa today and you will see millions of people professing that they are the people of God, the Israelites, though you will not see it on the news. Just in Nigeria there is a large Israelite community of millions. Over generations of misinterpretation and mixing customs with the Hamitic tribes they do not keep the laws the way they are supposed to, but they always knew they were Israel.

So God did it real nice. Esau would take our nationality from us, but the curses would follow us and our seed, so that no matter where we are scattered, in Africa, America, South America, China, Iran, the islands, when we read the Bible we say: wait, this is talking about my people.

“Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people”. There is Judah in Africa too, but this is speaking of Judah on this side of the earth, in the Western Hemisphere, specifically in the United States of America. Judah in North America is under Esau, who controls the world right now, and with an American passport you can go anywhere in the world. A Jamaican, Haitian or Nigerian passport cannot take you everywhere. That is why we tell you brothers: get your passport.

“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first”. God is going to raise up the tribe of Judah first, Judah in America. Then, when it says bring him unto his people, it means Judah will know where God's people are and will go find them. Wherever our people are in Africa, in Japan, in Iran, in India, scattered throughout the four corners of the earth, Judah will be able to identify them, find them, and teach them what God commanded of them.

That is why Genesis 49 speaks mainly of Israel on this side of the world: Judah needed to know who they were first. And it is already happening. The bishops and brothers that travel went into the history of the people, and they found Judah among the Igbo of Nigeria and the tribes scattered across Africa, India and the islands, now written on the revised twelve tribe chart. When people ask how we know, it is because the Lord showed us; the spirit guided us. That is “be thou an help to him from his enemies”: God is a help to Judah, making us find things so we are not guessing, and the chart will keep being updated as the Lord reveals more.

Jacob called his sons to tell them “that which shall befall you in the last days,” and of Judah he said, “thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies.” That says two things: Judah will be fighting his enemy, and Judah will be living in close proximity to his enemy, who today is Esau, Edom. Zechariah 2 is the scripture that proves Judah will be living with that enemy.

“Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord: for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the Lord.” Then: “Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” Zion is the city of Judah. The daughter of Babylon, as Psalms 137 shows, is Edom, the Caucasian race. So Zion is dwelling with the daughter of Babylon: Judah living in the land of the north, in the house of his enemy.

That is the picture of Genesis 49:8. Judah’s hand in the neck of his enemies is Judah living with him and contending with him. In the 1960s and 70s there was the Black Panthers, Martin Luther King, Malcolm X, and many movements where Judah rose up and fought the so-called white man. “he stooped down, he couched as a lion,” and at one point it looked like he was about to strike.

But the lion lay back down: “as an old lion; who shall rouse him up?” Christ is the one who will rouse him up. Until then the word to Zion is to come forth and deliver himself from the daughter of Babylon he dwells with.

Daniel 12 gives the time frame for when our people would be without a king, without an image, and without a sacrifice, as Hosea 3:4 says. Verse 11 reads: “And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days.”

The daily sacrifice taken away is Hosea's “without a sacrifice”. Without the sacrifice, the image and the ephod, all our religious infrastructure and spiritual guidance was stripped away, and there was no priest to guide us and tell us what God needs us to do. The white man came in, whipped us, taught us white Jesus and his lies, and forced it down our throats in Africa. After he brought the slaves over here, he went to Africa and destroyed them there, until the people in Africa don't even know that we in the Caribbean and America are the same people.

So from the taking away of the sacrifice, the days are counted, and the question Daniel asked, “How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?”, is answered with a set time. That goes back to the yoke of iron upon thy neck until thou have been destroyed: it did not just happen to us over here, it happened to our people in Africa, and the scattering of the holy people runs its appointed course.

Hosea says the children of Israel “shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod”. Daniel 12 gives the time frame for it. “How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?” The wonders are our people being destroyed, enslaved and colonized, being without a king, without a prince, without an ephod.

“it shall be for a time, times, and an half”. A time is a hundred years; times is two hundred, three hundred in all; and an half makes 350 years. “and when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished.” Within those 350 years we were totally destroyed. All that power was gone from us; we forgot who we are, and we even forgot our nationality.

When we fled Jerusalem in 70 AD, was our power destroyed? Our country was destroyed, but we went to Africa and built cities there, and the ten tribes were set up on this side of the world doing their thing too. We still had governments, we still had kings over us, and we still knew we were the children of Israel. It was within the slave trade and colonization that the power of the holy people was scattered.

That is the many days without a king: without political sovereignty, when Europe colonized Ghana, Nigeria, Angola, Senegal, Papua New Guinea and the Congo, and when the transatlantic slave trade took us. It is without an image: our minds destroyed until the sisters in Africa bleach their skin and put on weaves, because worshipping the God of your oppressor destroys the way you look at yourself. The same curses fell on our people all over Africa, like the Mau Mau in Kenya, tortured in British camps and paid less than 4,000 pounds each. That is why I don't want no damn reparations.

Christ told the Samaritan woman by the well the same thing he said in Luke 21. She said, “Sir, I perceive that thou art a prophet. Our fathers worshipped in this mountain; and ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship.” The Samaritans worshipped up on Mount Gerizim, because their fathers used to worship up there back in the days.

“Jesus saith unto her, Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father. Ye worship ye know not what”. The Samaritans were not going to worship in that mountain, and the Jews, the Israelites, would not be worshipping at Jerusalem either.

What is Christ saying here? What Luke 21 says: we would “fall by the edge of the sword”, and be “led away captive into all nations”, carried away as slaves into all nations. We fell by the sword in 70 AD, and being led into all nations is a process of time; it didn't all happen in 70 AD. Jerusalem would be “trodden down of the Gentiles”, occupied by heathens, until Christ returns and destroys the Gentiles.

In 70 AD most of us fled into Africa, formed communities, built cities and mingled amongst the Hamitic tribes. Esau drew maps pinpointing where the tribes were all over Africa, the Levite cities of Nigeria, Bnei Ephraim on the slave coast, the Jewish kingdoms, because slavery was not coincidence. Slavery was war.

Deuteronomy 11:12 says the land God gives is “A land which the Lord thy God careth for: the eyes of the Lord thy God are always upon it”. God has his eyes upon a specific place for us. But there is another land his eyes are upon for a different reason.

“Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth”. America is a sinful kingdom, and God is looking at America to destroy it. “saving that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, saith the Lord.” Jacob is the father of the twelve tribes of Israel.

“For, lo, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth.” We were scattered into all nations in slavery and captivity, so he will sift us out of every place we went. The sifting is a teaching process: our people have been trained after the ways of their colonizers, their oppressors and enslavers, and now they must be trained in the word of God to establish the house of Israel.

“All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, which say, The evil shall not overtake nor prevent us.” Those are our people who are rebellious to what God has to say and want to do things their own way. That is what America, aka Egypt, has convinced you to believe: nothing can happen to you here. You hear Donald Trump saying we have the strongest military, no one can stop us, open the Strait of Hormuz or I will blow you back to kingdom come. Stop believing you cannot be touched because this man talks tough and proud. America's kingdom is temporary; the strength that lasts comes from keeping God's commandments.

Amos 9:9 says, “I will sift the house of Israel among all nations”. Christians read Matthew 28:19 and think it means make everyone disciples: “Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost”.

This is what it means: because we were scattered into all nations, we have to be taught in all nations. It is the same sifting Amos speaks of. Christ himself, when he started his ministry, told the twelve, “Go not into the way of the Gentiles”, but “go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” Teaching all nations is going into all the nations where the lost sheep were scattered.

That is why the bishop gives the order: look historically at where our people were slaves, and go there and train them how to behave for God, to establish the kingdom. They have been trained after the ways of their colonizers, so we must train them in the word of God. The brothers who travel find the hardest thing is telling oppressed people that Jesus Christ is not a white man, because that white Jesus, made up in the Renaissance, is how the colonizers modified their behavior. But the charge stands: tell our people, you are not black, not Hispanic, not West Indian, not African; you are the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
blog/2026/2026-05-02-2026-05-02-called-t:
“Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them.” When the Bishop says separate that brother for the work, he is not talking about Atlanta. He is not talking about Miami or California. Did Israel only scatter in Atlanta? Did Israel only scatter in America? Separate them for the work means no matter where the work is, you have to go there.

The prophecy shows where the work is: “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations”. Not in America, not in Florida: among the nations. “and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you.” You know what that scripture is saying? No matter where you go, you are going to see Israelites. That is why a judge must be able to travel. Captain Joham just came from Trinidad and Suriname keeping Passover with the brothers there.

So the work Barnabas and Saul were separated for is the same work now: going to the nations where the Lord scattered Israel. It was the Most High God who called you, not the bishop, deacon or captain, and once hands are laid on you, you are sent away. When the phone call comes to travel, we do not want to hear anything from you but yes. Paul travelled, departing unto Seleucia and sailing to Cyprus, and we continue the Acts of the Apostles, bringing the good news all over the world, whatever hate we get for it.

Moses charged the judges: “Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great”. You shall not have respect of persons in judgment; you cannot be partial. You have to hear both sides, the small as well as the great. That is the qualification of a judge, and if you are not ready for it, do not accept the position.

James speaks of the same thing: “My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.” Here is respect of persons, and James sets it against the faith of Christ itself. You cannot hold the faith of the Lord of glory and at the same time judge one brother by a different measure than another.

“ye shall not be afraid of the face of man”. You are not here to be loved or to be liked; you are judges. Some are afraid to make a decision because of what men will think of them, and some get offended when judgment falls on their friend, even without knowing what happened. What does that have to do with you? The judgment is God's, and a judge in Israel must be just, not partial.

“Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?” Respect of persons goes into having a certain type of man in admiration over another: respecting one over another, preferring one over another, and it shows in how you deal with matters with that brother or those brothers. You are ready to have men's persons in admiration for advantage; there is something you are going to gain by showing favoritism.

And here is the end result: you “are become judges of evil thoughts”. Some brothers are horrible judges because there is something about the person they should judge that they can gain from them. Whether he gives you gifts, whether he is your ride to Sabbath, whether he got you a job, whatever the case may be, now you are partial in your judgment because of what that person can provide for you. The Lord says that is an evil, evil thing.

So you might think, I am just not going to judge because that is my friend. The Bible says you are evil. That is exactly what Moses forbade when he charged the judges to “judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him.”

“But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.” We always hear thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not steal; we know those like the back of our hand. But if you have respect of persons, whether in judgment or in having men's persons in admiration for advantage, you commit sin. You are a transgressor, breaking the commandments of God.

You want to be in that position, but much is required of you in the position as judges. You must judge matters and deal righteously, because that is the law of God we just read in Deuteronomy: judge righteous judgment, whether it is your friend or not. In a position of leadership you cannot conceal your friend's folly; none of us should.

What has been discovered is that because someone is your friend, you do not want to speak out. You do not want to reveal the sin, as Leviticus 5:1 requires, and you do not want to be part of the judgment once the sin is revealed. You sit there quiet while the others bring out the transgressions, because you do not agree with the judgment God says to bring forth. Something is wrong with that. We have to stand on what God said. Anyone you consider a friend who goes against God and does not repent: I never knew you. Give us a little time and we will not even remember his name, because he chose wickedness and evil over the righteousness of God.
blog/2026/2026-05-02-2026-05-02-recoveri:
Sirach says the man whose whole occupation is his worldly job shall not “understand the sentence of judgment”. Why don't you understand when judgments are passed? Proverbs answers: “Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the Lord understand all things.”

That is the brother who is always confused. When leadership makes a judgment, he doesn't agree, even if he disagrees in silence. You don't agree because you don't know the scriptures. All you know is your job, not the word of God, so you are always confused. And the Bible says you are evil.

So that brother “shall not be sought for in publick counsel”. When things are going down, we don't want to hear your opinion, because your opinion is your work, your job. He will not “sit high in the congregation” or have rank, and he will not “be found where parables are spoken”, because he could care less. If the shoe fits, brother, wear it. If you want to be a member, be a member; there is nothing wrong with that.

But they that seek the Lord understand all things. Chapter 39 shows the flip side: the one that “giveth his mind to the law of the most High”. He seeks out the wisdom of the ancients, is found where the subtle parables are, and he shall serve among great men and appear before princes.

The Lord tells Jacob, “Fear not”, and promises, “I will pour water upon him that is thirsty.” Thirsty for what? Thirsty for the truth. Paul shows what that water is: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word.” The water represents the word of God.

Read Isaiah with that in mind. “I will pour water upon him that is thirsty”: I will pour the word of God upon them that are thirsty for the truth. “and floods upon the dry ground”: the floods also represent the word of God, poured out on the dry ground, these places wherein we dwell. “I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thine offspring”: his spirit upon his people and his blessing upon their children.

God only chose Israel, and this washing is for his chosen, Jacob and Jesurun, “whom I have chosen.” The Lord made us and formed us from the womb, and he will help us.

When the word is poured out, “they shall spring up as among the grass.” That is what we are looking at now: the Israelites are waking up and springing up worldwide like grass. And verse 5 shows three kinds of Israelites waking up: one says “I am the Lord’s”, acknowledging we are the children of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; another takes on a new name and calls himself “by the name of Jacob”; another changes his surname and will “surname himself by the name of Israel.” It is the word of God, the water, that cleanses them and brings them back.

The Comforter, the Holy Ghost, “shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.” Why would we need to remember the things Christ said? Because we would be made to forget. Through slavery the nations annihilated our twelve tribes, burned our records and beat us into submission, and we forgot what Christ said.

What did he say? That he would gather his elect from the four corners of the earth. That he was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. And: “If ye love me, keep my commandments.”

The Holy Spirit causes us to remember these things. If you don't remember them, you don't have the Holy Spirit on you. Keeping the commandments is the love Christ asks for, and the Spirit brings back to our remembrance who we are and what he said.

That is what is happening now: brothers and sisters waking up worldwide. Isaiah 44 promised it to Jacob, whom the Lord chose: “I will pour water upon him that is thirsty”, the word upon those thirsty for the truth, and “I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thine offspring: And they shall spring up as among the grass”. The Israelites are springing up worldwide like grass.

“Go not into the way of the Gentiles”: in this verse that includes the other eleven tribes. “And into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not”: that is the Northern Kingdom. Why? Because it was not their time yet. The Lord said he would raise the tents of Judah first. “But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel”: that starts with Judah first.

Some are confused and think this is new. It is not; it has always been taught. Acts shows the order being followed after Christ: “Now they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.”

To none but the Jews only: only to Judah. They were primarily dealing with Judah first.

That does not mean the rest were never to be reached. Christ himself went to Samaria in John 4 and taught the Samaritans for a few days, because he knew the time was coming to deal with them. Judah first, and then the other tribes.

The disciples went first to Judah, “preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.” Then watch what Paul says: “Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?”

“Even us”: the tribe of Benjamin and all the other tribes. “Whom he hath called, not of the Jews only”: not of Judah only. “But also of the Gentiles”: the other eleven tribes.

Some were perverting Zechariah 12:7, where the Lord raises the tents of Judah first, as if it meant only Judah. Judah first is the order, not the whole. So go back to Matthew 10 with a better understanding: “Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” In the beginning it was Judah first; afterward the call went to the rest of the tribes. There is no contradiction once you know the order.

People say the people in the land of Israel today are the Jews. That is not what the Bible says. After the tribulation, when the stars fall (the missiles) and the powers of the heavens are shaken (nations warring against each other), “he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” Notice the angels do not go to one land to gather this people. Christ is letting us know the Israelites would not be in a land; they would be scattered worldwide.

Who is the elect? Some say anybody who worships. Isaiah says: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect”. That is the elect: Israel, scattered in the four winds from one end of heaven to the other.

Before the angels come for them, the Lord calls to the heavens and to the earth: “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” The saints are “the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel”, and only the Israelites made a covenant with God by sacrifice. The call to the heavens is to the angels; the call to the earth is to us.

So the message for us on earth is the same as the angels' commandment: gather the saints. We are not supposed to be looking for other races and nationalities, only the twelve tribes of Israel, scattered worldwide, which is why the gospel has to go out to every land.

Christ said he would send his angels to gather the elect from the four winds, and Isaiah names the elect: “Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel mine elect.” The Israelites would not be in one land; they would be scattered worldwide. Before the angels come for them, the Lord says, “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” So who are the saints?

“He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel.” The children of Israel are the saints.

Now read Psalms 50 again with that. “He shall call to the heavens from above”: that is the angels he is calling to. “and to the earth”: the earth is you and I. And the message to both is the same, “Gather my saints together unto me.” That is what we read in Matthew 24, where Christ tells his angels to gather the elect, and it is the commandment to the prophets on earth too.

“those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice”: only the Israelites made a covenant with God by sacrifice. So we are not supposed to be looking for other races and other nationalities. The work of gathering is for the twelve tribes of Israel, the saints, scattered to the four corners of the earth.

Zechariah says Zion, Judah, “dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” The key is who the daughter of Babylon is. The psalm names her: “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.” The word rase means destroy it: destroy it even to the foundation.

Then the very next words: “O daughter of Babylon.” Notice what it is calling them now. It is calling Edom, the so-called white folks, the daughter of Babylon.

So the scripture lets you know Judah would live among Edom, and where? In the land of the north. That is why the Lord cries, “Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north.” The group of Judah in North America is dwelling with the daughter of Babylon, the children of Edom who wanted Jerusalem razed to the ground.

And the Lord's word to that people is: “he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.” We are God's favorite, and the nations which spoiled us will answer for it.

Zechariah says, “come forth, and flee from the land of the north”: flee from North America. “for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven”: all Israel scattered, like we read in Matthew 24 and James 1. Then he singles out one group: “Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.”

Many scriptures tell us that Zion represents the twelve tribes. But in this context, which Zion is it? Asaph answers: “But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved.” That is the Zion right there.

So “Deliver thyself, O Zion” is talking about Judah: deliver yourself, Judah. That does not mean all the Judahites are in the land of the north; Judah was dispersed like all the other tribes. But God is pinpointing a particular group of Judah that would be in the land of the north, dwelling with the daughter of Babylon.

That fits the rest of the prophecy. In these last days the Lord raises up Judah first: the Lord “shall save the tents of Judah first”, and the blessing of Judah is, “Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people.” The voice of Judah is the teaching of Judah, carried to the other eleven tribes.

Zephaniah says, “for then I will take away out of the midst of thee them that rejoice in thy pride”. Who rejoices in our pride? Sirach proves what pride is: “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God”.

Pride is departing from God, going against his commandments; it is our sin. So those that rejoice in our pride are the ones that rejoice in us going against God's commandments: the pastors, the Christians, the churches, the Democrats and the Republicans. They rejoice in us not keeping God's commandments. The Lord says, I am going to take them out of you, take them away from you, “and thou shalt no more be haughty because of my holy mountain”, the land of Israel.

What he leaves is “an afflicted and poor people, and they shall trust in the name of the Lord.” The elect beyond the rivers of Ethiopia, the daughter of his dispersed, a large portion of them on the continent of Africa, are afflicted and very poor, as we saw going throughout Africa keeping Passover and the feast of unleavened bread. They must be taught to trust in the name of the Lord.

“The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies”, because they are being taught the commandments, and that is what we go out there for. No, Jesus is not white; no, he was not born December 25th; no, we are not to pray to Mary or to the ancestors. Sin has always been the problem, and breaking God's commandments is a sign of unbelief. When the ones who rejoice in our departing from God are taken away, the remnant shall feed and lie down, and none shall make them afraid.
blog/2026/2026-05-02-2026-05-02-the-retu:
“Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord, that take counsel, but not of me; and that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin.” Our people take counsel, but not of God. The covering they cover themselves with is not his spirit: it is Christianity and it is politics, Democrat and Republican, and with it they add sin to sin.

“That walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt!” Literally, our people went down into ancient Egypt for help against Babylon, after God told Jeremiah to warn them not to go. But there is a double meaning. A shadow is not the real thing. The shadow of Egypt is America, the great city that Revelation 11:8 says is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt.

“Therefore shall the strength of Pharaoh be your shame, and the trust in the shadow of Egypt your confusion.” Those who put their strength in Pharaoh, the presidents of America, those who vote for them, will be ashamed, and it will be our people’s confusion. They are going to ask why.

That trust in the shadow of Egypt is the covenant of Isaiah 28:15: “We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement.” The hell and death is America. Our people made that covenant in 1964 and 1965 with civil rights, the Voting Rights Act and integration, and Martin Luther King understood it at the end when he said he had integrated his people into a burning house. Our forefathers did the same with Rome, the gates of hell, when they said we have no king but Caesar, and they were destroyed in 70 AD. It is the same state of mind today: our people love voting for US presidents and trust in this system. But Isaiah 28:18 says “your covenant with death shall be disannulled, and your agreement with hell shall not stand”, and after sixty years it is falling apart before our eyes.
blog/2026/2026-05-09-2026-05-09-called-t:
Peter laid out the instructions for marriages, because hard times are coming. We see marriage troubles where a sister is upset because her husband's socks are on the floor and she calls him lazy; or a sister gives up the faith and wants to go back to the damn world and be a h-o-e to negro Tyrone instead of a wife to the husband the Lord gave her; or a brother wants to be a whoremonger instead of a man of his nation leading his people. There are more trying times coming, when you will be worried about surviving. How much more in a household where a man and woman are striving and going back and forth with each other?

“Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives.” Sisters, your tone, how you speak toward your husband, especially in hard times, means a lot. How you respect your lord, your king in your household, and how you carry yourself toward him shows the level of your faith. You sisters have to increase your faith and learn how to be correct with the man God gave you. And not just husband and wife: all you sisters must honor the men of your nation.

In hard times Satan attacks marriage. He did not attack the government Adam set up first; he attacked the foundation, the marriage, which shows how powerful marriage is. And he did it by going through the woman first, which is why you sisters have to build yourselves up.

The Bible says marriage is honorable and the bed undefiled: righteous marriage, husband and wife, as with Adam and Eve, Abraham and Sarah, Joseph and Mary, not man and man or woman and woman. Keeping that honorable is part of suffering for righteousness' sake and being happy in it.

Peter says, “But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye.” We must begin to learn how to suffer for righteousness' sake, for the sake of Christ. And we are happy in it: that happiness is our peace. Happy are they that keep God's laws.

“And establish judgment in the gate”: establish judgment in yourself, your household, your nation and your communities. Job lost his children and his wealth and was covered in boils, and he said, “the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.” Abraham was called to go out and “went out, not knowing whither he went”, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob. Within fifteen years the Southern states were imprisoning black Americans at ten times the rate of whites; they made loitering and vagrancy felonies and leased the convicts out for forced labor. “And the desolate land shall be tilled, whereas it lay desolate in the sight of all that passed by. And they shall say, This land that was desolate is become like the garden of Eden”. But he can't give us Jerusalem the way it is supposed to be right now, because we are in the midst of sin.

So he says: let me remove the sin, let me cleanse you, let me give you a new heart, let me remove that weak, brittle body and give you immortality. Then he will command the land to transform into the garden of Eden. We are going right back to where we were in the beginning with our father Adam, and we are going to be with our father Adam again: his name is Jesus the Christ, the black Messiah, in the same place.

“and the waste and desolate and ruined cities are become fenced, and are inhabited. Then the heathen that are left round about you shall know that I the Lord build the ruined places, and plant that that was desolate: I the Lord have spoken it, and I will do it.” The nations will say, God is with these people. He has spoken it, and he will do it.

Genesis 2:7 says “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground.” People talk about evolution, that man came up from primates and formed over time into what we know today; that is not true. Everything in Israel United in Christ is done to edify the nation, and what we say we prove out of the word of God. Ecclesiasticus 33:10 is the second witness: “And all men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth.”

Some will ask how we know man was made from the dust, since that is not what the white man’s science says. Science is only good if it goes with the Bible; if it contradicts the Bible, we don't give a damn about science. But the honest science agrees. The infographic From Dust to Dust, the elements that connect us to Earth, shows that the human body is made mainly of elements also found in soil. The six main elements of life, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus and sulfur, are in every cell, molecule and structure of the body and make up over 99 percent of our mass. The essential minerals, calcium for bones and teeth, potassium for the muscles and heart, magnesium, sodium and chlorine, are the same nutrients the soil gives the plants. The trace elements, iron for carrying oxygen, zinc for the immune system and healing, silicon and manganese, are in the soil too. We come from the earth, and to the earth we return, just like the Bible says.

The Most High is a mastermind, the author of beauty, the creator of all things, and he knew what he was doing when he pulled Adam from the dust of the ground. Our bodies are a testament that his word is true. The Bible is a true book, and we don't give a damn what anybody has to say about how our God, our father, created us. The teaching that man came from primates is there to contradict God’s word, because they know our God is a black man.

Paul says the same: “The first man is of the earth, earthy,” and “As is the earthy, such are they also that are earthy.” Adam was earthy, and so are we; we come from the same soil as our father Adam, and “as we have borne the image of the earthy, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly.” Meanwhile the other nations make sure we are deficient in these very things, and much of the food we eat diminishes them to kill us faster. So it is important, brothers and sisters, to keep a healthy diet.

“Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed”. The Lord planted us a noble vine: he gave us the commandments and the scriptures and made us elite, the top people on the planet earth, holy and right. “how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?” The Lord looked at us and said, wow, y'all degenerate.

That is how we became degenerate: our own wickedness. “know therefore and see that it is an evil thing and bitter, that thou hast forsaken the Lord thy God, and that my fear is not in thee, saith the Lord God of hosts.”

Are we feeling it now, brothers and sisters? Look at our conditions: the trauma, poverty, fatherlessness and broken families, the curse of Deuteronomy 28 passed from one generation to the next. That is the bitterness of having forsaken the Lord.

So our mission is the one in Maccabees: “Let us restore the decayed fortune of our people, and let us fight for our people and the sanctuary.” We have to restore the decayed state of our people: learn the word of God, apply it to our lives, and go out and teach our people, so the degenerate plant becomes the noble vine again.

Solomon says “the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” To muse, in the Bible, means to think deeply, meditate, ponder, or murmur on something, especially God's word or works, often in self communion, prayer and praise: to consider closely, to study in silence.

David uses that very word: “I remember the days of old; I meditate on all thy works; I muse on the work of thy hands.” Listen to the word David used. He would think on why life is the way it is, why we suffer the conditions we suffer. Even Esdras said, Lord, it was not in my mind to know the deep things; I just want to know why Israel is jacked up, why we are going through what we are going through.

All of our minds muse daily upon many things. Why did that person die? Why is my life like this? Where did I go wrong? Should I have married her? Should I have gone to that job interview? Why did I get drunk last night? Most of you can't sleep; you toss and turn every night, especially the man who goes to work every morning carrying the burden of his whole family, or the father up at night thinking about what could happen to his daughters.

This earthy tabernacle, this corruptible body we got from Adam, is what makes us overthink and overanalyze everything. David's musing shows the right place to take it: remember the days of old, and meditate on the works of God's hands, because that is where the answer to why we suffer is found.
