Today's traps are the thirst traps. “Flee fornication”: get away from it. Solomon shows how the trap works: “Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids.”

A lot of us are weak to the woman, weak to the box. Them eyelashes are there for a reason: batting them, fluffing them, all dainty. You noticed in the cartoons back in the day, in a little love scene, the eyelashes seem to grow. That little dainty look on the eyelids is designed to take you. Don't let it get you. Don't let it take you over.

“For by means of a whorish woman a man is brought to a piece of bread: and the adulteress will hunt for the precious life.” She is hunting, and what she hunts is your life.

That is why Paul says “he that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body.” Once you go outside of Christ, you are sinning against your own self. It is on you; you put yourself in that predicament. So flee it before the eyes and the heart are taken.

“which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith”. A lot of sisters in marriages covet other people's marriages: he's doing this, he's doing that, and you're mad at your husband because he isn't doing what that brother is doing, when he is probably trying to get where he needs to be. Solomon points you somewhere else: “Every wise woman buildeth her house”.

You're looking at the wrong thing. Instead of watching what that husband is doing, study her. Why don't you go ask her: what are you doing? What's the secret? Why is he so happy? Every time you ask for something he gives it; I see you with the new purse, the new shoes. Ask her how she's building her house up.

The wise woman has a mind to what is going on in the house: these are the things I need to fix to make my household better; this is how I assist my husband. That is why Genesis says her desire shall be to her husband. It means you study him: you know his likes and dislikes, what irritates him, when not to mess with him, and when to come say something. You live in the house; you see it all the time.

“but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands.” Your pride, sister, will keep you from doing it. You think he's supposed to give you everything first before you get on board: if he ain't doing this for me, I ain't doing nothing for him. You're out of your damn mind; that isn't what you're in the marriage for. He is out providing, bringing food into the house, clothes for the kids, paying the bills. You do your job and he does his. If he has to do it all before you reciprocate anything, something's wrong, and you might be the reason your marriage is the way it is.

“And after him rose up Nathan to prophesy in the time of David.” So we know who we are talking about: this is David, in the days of Nathan the prophet, the prophet the Lord sent to him after Bathsheba. The next verse carries on: “As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Israel.”

That is the same David of 2 Samuel 11. He went out on the roof, “he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon.” Bad to the bone. He sent and inquired: I got power, let me send some people over there, let me make this official. One with a spiritual mind made it plain: this is the wife of Uriah the Hittite, this is somebody's wife, bro. “And David sent messengers, and took her” anyway. Wisdom and understanding were right there, and he pushed them aside.

“and she came in unto him, and he lay with her”. She wasn't right either. She didn't resist, she wasn't opposed; she thought she came up. “And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I am with child.”

You see how Satan can deceive you. Satan put that lust in him to where he just didn't care, and he went the extra mile: he put Uriah in the front of the battle, got him killed, and took the wife. What he saw, the desire, the action, the cover-up, and the consequences: his first child was gone. Yet Sirach remembers David as the one chosen out of the children of Israel, and that leads to what the Lord did with him.

“The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.” The Lord did forgive David. He loved David, and David messed up.

David saw Bathsheba from the roof, took another man's wife, put Uriah in battle to be killed, and lost the child. That is as bad as it gets. But David repented, and the Lord took away his sins, exalted his horn, and gave him a covenant of kings and a throne of glory in Israel.

And that's another thing. A lot of times we are going to fall and do things that are not comely according to the scriptures. That don't mean you bunker down, go into a fetal position and say woe is me. You get yourself together, you repent, and you move forward. You don't go back. What did Christ say? Go, and sin no more.

You got to pick up the pieces and keep moving. We are all going to make mistakes. It is how you handle the mistake: it happened, so what are you going to do now, moving forward?

The Lord set both harvests before Israel from the beginning: “I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live.”

What you put in, you are going to get; you are going to receive a reward. Life and blessing for the one who sows to the Spirit, death and cursing for the one who sows to his flesh. Heaven and earth are called as witnesses, so no one can say he was not told. God is not mocked.

And the choice reaches past you: choose life “that both thou and thy seed may live.” What a man sows, his children reap with him.

“he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting.” When you sow yourself into the scriptures, the Lord is going to give you blessings: he will show you favor, have mercy on you, and give you abundance. That is Joshua 1:8: “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night.”

We should meditate on the scriptures day and night, “that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.” Meditating and doing is the sowing.

When we do that, the Lord makes our way prosperous. He gives us the abundance we desire, spiritually, emotionally, all the increases we desire, when we put our mind on the Lord. That is reaping of the Spirit.

“And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve.” You cannot serve two masters. You can't serve the flesh and serve God at the same time. You have to choose; ain't no in between.

That is why he said he would rather you be cold or hot. If you are lukewarm, battling that middle ground and playing games, he will spew you out of his mouth. Sowing to the flesh and sowing to the Spirit cannot be done at once.

“whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.” Choose the Lord, sow to the Spirit, and of the Spirit reap life everlasting.

“whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.” What you put in, you are going to reap. When you put in the sin, the consequences are going to happen, period. Paul says it plainly: “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.”

Sin is death. That is the corruption reaped by the one who sows to his flesh: sow that sin to your flesh and you will be judged by it. And the gift of God, eternal life through Christ, is the “life everlasting” reaped by the one who sows to the Spirit.

What you put in, you are going to receive as a reward. Wages for sin, a gift for the one who sows to the Spirit. God is not mocked.

Jeremiah sets two men side by side. The man who leans on his own heart and on flesh “shall be like the heath in the desert, and shall not see when good cometh; but shall inhabit the parched places in the wilderness, in a salt land and not inhabited.” He is dried up and alone, and he cannot even see good when it comes to him.

Then: “Blessed is the man that trusteth in the Lord”. That is the man who gets counsel, who reads the Bible and applies the commandments. The heart is deceitful above all things; your thoughts, your emotion and your intuition will destroy you. Nobody really cares what you think; it is about what the Bible is saying. So you have to be listening, in the word and studying, and not going and deciding for yourself without counsel.

The Lord set up men to guide us. But Black people hate guidance. When they see a man of the truth, it is low self-esteem: they see themselves in him, so they think, I am not nothing, so I know he ain't nothing. That goes way back, to what was done to us from slavery.

So the deceitful heart of verse 9 is the reason for the curse and the blessing here. The man who trusts himself ends in the salt land; the man who trusts the Lord and takes the counsel of the men he set up is the blessed one.

Judas asked the chief priests, “What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you?” and “they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver.” Sirach shows what that love of money does: “He that loveth gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof.”

“Gold hath been the ruin of many, and their destruction was present.” Sometimes money is the ruin of you. You stop making sound decisions; you are willing to do anything for it. That is why so many young women today are on OnlyFans and on these podcasts, doing anything they can to make money, willing to get booed on in another country for money. What morals do you have, and then you go home and kiss your kids? It might look good because of the opportunity, but all things ain't good.

“It is a stumblingblock unto them that sacrifice unto it, and every fool shall be taken therewith.” If money is all you think about and all you talk about, if your existence is based off money, money, money, then that is your god. That is why it says you made a sacrifice to it.

“Blessed is the rich that is found without blemish, and hath not gone after gold.” Why blessed? Because it is hard to have riches and keep the commandments. With money you can be enticed in so many ways; you can buy what you want and do whatever you want, and some feel they are above everybody. But when you are without blemish, you use your finances properly and it don't mess with your head. You have a lot of money, but you ain't made it your god.

Judas walked with Christ. He saw the healing and was around the commandment keeping, but that money lust is never enough, and he desired riches more than anything. Gold was his ruin: money was his demise.

“Seek not death in the error of your life: and pull not upon yourselves destruction with the works of your hands.” Don't seek death. When you put that sin above everything, that is exactly what you are seeking: death. Judas did it with his own hands when he “sought opportunity to betray him” for thirty pieces of silver, and he destroyed himself.

Money can be your destruction. Women can be your destruction. Food can be your destruction. Alcohol and drugs can be your destruction. These are the appetites in us that we constantly want to feed, and we have to stop it.

This is war, and people will give you up for money. It runs through history: the Black Panther Party, Martin Luther King, Malcolm X. We had a whole Israelite camp back in the day break up because of money, and today certain brothers get pushed on every platform as the face of the Israelites while the bishops and deacons really out here teaching are kept off. If you are weak in spirit, betrayal comes with money.

So be wise. A lot of times we are going to fall, but you don't sit down in a fetal position; you repent and move forward and sin no more. The destruction a man pulls on himself comes from the works of his own hands, and the way out is to stop feeding the appetite before it becomes your demise, like it became Judas'.

Matthew 5:28 says whosoever looks on a woman to lust after her “hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.” A lot of you brothers do that, and a lot of you sisters do that. You're scrolling down, you see something that catches your eye, and next thing you know you are going down the rabbit hole, full-fledged, not caring about no consequences, fully convinced and convicted in your sin. How do you fix that? Job 31.

“I made a covenant with mine eyes”. You have to control what you view. You have to control what you desire. “why then should I think upon a maid?” I should not be thinking lustfully upon a maid. Because you see a beautiful woman doesn't mean you should think lustfully about that sister; you made a covenant with your eyes. Especially you married men: you should have a covenant with your eyes with your wife. Why should I even think about it?

“For what portion of God is there from above? and what inheritance of the Almighty from on high?” The one who looks to lust has already committed adultery in his heart, and what portion does he have from God then, what inheritance from the Almighty? Read on and Job answers: “Is not destruction to the wicked?”

That is how the private sin of pornography is fought: not after the eye has wandered, but by making the covenant beforehand, so that the looking that leads to adultery in the heart never begins.

“Pride goeth before destruction”. Where does pride begin? Sirach: “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” That means you have a froward mind.

“For pride is the beginning of sin”: the beginning of you falling to sin, falling for your temptation, falling to your lust, falling to feed that appetite. You knew better. You had all the warning signs, all the opportunity, everything placed in front of you. You were given a way out, as 1 Corinthians 10:13 said: God will with the temptation make a way to escape. But pride overcame you. Your mind wasn't on the Lord when your back was against the wall.

“and he that hath it shall pour out abomination”. When you have that pride, a negro is unstoppable; a prideful negro, oh my God. “and therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.” When pride overtakes you, the Lord adds things to your demise: I'm going to leave you to Satan to gobble you on up, because your mind ain't right; you're too prideful.

That is why pride goes before destruction. Pride removes correction; you don't want to hear it. You think you know it all, you have all the wisdom and understanding. Pride isolates you, and it precedes the collapse.

This is how much the Lord hates pride. Sirach first shows what God loves: “In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.”

The unity of brethren the Lord loves; the love of neighbors the Lord loves. And a man and wife that agree together: why is that beautiful? Because it's hard for two different personalities to come together and be on the same accord. That's why marriage takes time, brothers and sisters. It isn't overnight; it takes years and experience.

Now the negative: “Three sorts of men my soul hateth, and I am greatly offended at their life: a poor man that is proud, a rich man that is a liar, and an old adulterer that doateth.” He is offended at their life. A negro that's poor and proud: I hate that negro, I hate his soul, I hate everything about him. How can you be that way?

It means you have no humility whatsoever. Nobody can tell you anything; you have all the answers, but no fruits in your life, no solutions, no shame. That is the pride that goes before destruction, and God's soul hates it.

Sirach says pride begins when one departs from God. The Wisdom of Solomon shows how a man departs: “For froward thoughts separate from God”.

Being froward means you are thinking outside of the Bible. Period. That's what it is.

When your mind is not on the Lord, you are separated from him. You can't be both. So pride starts in the thoughts: the moment your thinking goes outside of the scriptures, you have separated yourself from God, and a haughty spirit is on its way to the fall. That is why the man who meditates on the scriptures has something to pull from when temptation comes, and the froward man doesn't.

1 Samuel 10:6 says you “shalt be turned into another man.” 2 Esdras 14:34 tells you what your part is in that turning.

“Therefore if so be that ye will subdue your own understanding, and reform your hearts, ye shall be kept alive and after death ye shall obtain mercy.”

Subdue your own understanding and reform your heart. We have to be transformed in the renewing of our minds. Transformed.

That is what the brother with the addiction runs from. He comes to the table having drunk a whole fifth in one night and says he is not an alcoholic. Even the white man knows the first step of recovery is to admit it: you have to realize you need help, that you are sick. Has he watched the classes on alcohol the Bishops and Deacons go over all the time? No. Why not? Because he is running away from his issues, and you cannot run away from that thing. You have to subdue your own understanding, reform your heart, and let the word turn you into another man, and then you shall be kept alive and after death obtain mercy.

A lot of us are not finding comfort in the scriptures because we lack faith. You don’t believe the Bible can transform you. You don’t believe it can turn you into another man, that you could become a whole different person. But 1 Samuel 10:6 says it: “And the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.”

John 3:3 says the same thing to Nicodemus: “Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”

Being turned into another man is being born again. The brother who drank a whole fifth in one night, the one who says, I can’t put it down, it’s a part of me, is not stuck being that man. Except he be born again, turned into another man, he cannot see the kingdom. The bottle is the battle, and the Bible is how you are turned into another man and win it.

Isaiah 61:1 says the Lord “hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted”. We are the brokenhearted. We are the ones crying out in the streets, to this day. And Job shows what the Lord does with us in that condition: “He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.”

The Lord is telling you there is going to be so much oppression going on that you are going to have to listen to the word of God. The Carmelo Anthony situation, that's oppression: he is in the prison house for defending himself. And the same week of his verdict, a baby was shot dead in Mississippi. These things are going to continue to happen.

Oppression, persecution, tribulation, all these things are going to arise for God's people to realize who they are. That is how he opens our ears. And yet some want to leave the truth because they got called fat, or because they got demoted. That is some evil stuff: traitors and betrayers.

So Isaiah 61 is proclaimed to the ones whose ears the oppression has opened: liberty to the captives, “the opening of the prison to them that are bound”, because we are yet this day in captivity and we fill the prison houses. What is there to hope for outside of the body of Christ? Only the ones who know who they are can look for “the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of vengeance of our God”.

The bottle says, take another drink. You can handle it; drink some more. The Bible says, “And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit.”

The bottle wants to fill you: drink me and be filled with my love. It says, you're alone, nobody understands us, I love you more than anybody. I love you more than water. You don't need to eat today; I'll make the food taste better. You can't sleep; I can put you to sleep so fast you won't even realize it. The bottle starts talking like scripture: I am that I am, the comfort of them all.

That is excess, and it destroys the body too. Alcohol builds fat around your organs and your belly, raises your risk of heart disease, high blood pressure and type two diabetes, makes you hungrier and drives you to fast food. Four or five shots a drink every day is thousands of calories a week, and then you wonder why you can't lose weight or climb a flight of stairs.

The command is to be filled with something else: the Spirit. Cast your burden on the Lord and be filled with his Spirit, not with the bottle.

The bottle says, forget your pain; the Bible says, “Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee.” The bottle says, numb your sorrow. Christ answers that lie: “Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.”

The bottle offers to carry your burden for you. It talks to you like scripture in a dark room with one light over the table: drink me, I can take away thy sorrows; you're depressed, don't worry about it; you're stressed out, put the kids to bed early and drink me. That is a spirit having a conversation with you.

Christ is the one who actually takes the weight. The labouring and heavy laden are told to come to him, not to the liquor store, and he gives rest. The bottle only numbs the sorrow until tomorrow; casting the burden on the Lord is how he sustains you and keeps the righteous from being moved.

The bottle says, you can't change. You're the same; you're going to be that same person. The Bible says, “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul.”

The law of the Lord converts the soul: it changes a man. So the lie that you can't change is answered by the perfect law of God. You can repent and become a new man.

That is the other side of casting your burden on the Lord. You don't just hand him the weight; you take on his law, and his law turns you into somebody different. The bottle keeps you drunk and stupid, the way the enemy wants it, with a liquor store in every black neighborhood and weed stores everywhere to keep you high, drunk and stupid. The law of the Lord makes the simple wise and converts the soul out of that.

The bottle says, you are a failure. You ain't nothing. You're going to be the same person you always were. The Bible says: “There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.”

Guess what? You can repent. The bottle says you're a failure; the Bible says you can repent and become a new man.

But it starts with acknowledging it: I'm an alcoholic. I'm a fornicator, an adulterer, a liar, a thief; I deal with envy, covetousness, idolatry. That is where the change happens. And acknowledging it is not enough; you have to work on fixing those things. You can't say, I'm an alcoholic, and keep going out drinking.

No condemnation belongs to those who walk after the Spirit and not after the flesh. The man chained to the bottle is walking after the flesh; the man who casts his burden on the Lord and walks in the Spirit is free of the condemnation the bottle keeps whispering over him.

“The burden of Moab. Because in the night Ar of Moab is laid waste, and brought to silence; because in the night Kir of Moab is laid waste.” Ar and Kir are cities of Moab. This took place under Nebuchadnezzar, when Babylon came in smiting Moab. But there is more to it, and we go to Revelation to see it.

“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city.” The dead bodies are the spiritually dead bodies of the Israelites. And the great city is Babylon the great. That is the point to hold: Revelation speaks of a great city, a Babylon, in the last days, where our people lie spiritually dead in the street.

So Babylon is not only the kingdom of Nebuchadnezzar. There is a Babylon of the last days as well, and Revelation 14:8 names it: “Babylon is fallen, is fallen, that great city.” When Isaiah shows Babylon laying Moab waste in the night, bringing its cities to silence, and Moab howling over Nebo and Medeba with baldness on every head and every beard cut off, it carries a dual meaning. Moab, which today is China, the Vietnamese and the Mongolians, will be laid waste again, and the great city where our people lie spiritually dead is the Babylon of today.

Revelation 11:8 speaks of “the great city.” Revelation 14 proves which city that is: “And there followed another angel, saying, Babylon is fallen, is fallen, that great city, because she made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication.”

The great city is Babylon, the one that made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication. This place, America, is a spiritual Babylon. It is not the actual Babylon under Nebuchadnezzar, but this place God calls Babylon the great.

That is why we went there from Isaiah 15. Isaiah’s burden of Moab took place when Babylon under Nebuchadnezzar smote Moab: Ar of Moab and Kir of Moab, cities of Moab, “laid waste, and brought to silence” in the night. Moab went up to the high places to weep and howled over Nebo and Medeba, and “on all their heads shall be baldness, and every beard cut off”, because Moab shaves off its hair in great sorrow and mourning, a custom that remains in their religions to this day, in the head shaving of the monks and nuns of Chinese religion.

So when Babylon under Nebuchadnezzar smote Moab, know that there is dual significance behind it. There is a Babylon the great today, and Moab today is China, who with the Vietnamese and the Mongolians will be laid waste once again.

“And in mercy shall the throne be established: and he shall sit upon it in truth in the tabernacle of David.” The throne that is going to be established is the throne of Christ, and Isaiah 9 shows it: “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder.” The government shall be upon the shoulders of Christ.

“and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.” A lot of people don’t understand why he is called the everlasting Father. It is because the one you think is the heavenly Father in the Old Testament was actually Christ. That is why there is a lot of confusion in the Israelite community.

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Don’t just read by that word increase; the mustard seed of Matthew 13 shows it. We are at the mustard seed stage now, and this is the beginning of God’s government.

“upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever.” To order it and establish it with judgment and justice: that is law and order. That is why we establish law, order and rank, and teach brothers and sisters the laws, commandments and statutes of the Holy Bible.

Some don’t like law because they like adultery better; they don’t like order because they like disorder, chaos, a toxic marriage and a chaotic life, married today and divorced tomorrow. That is genetic encoding from slavery, and it is in all of us. But the Bible can break that spirit, only if you let it. Only God can cleanse that from you, and his throne, established in mercy, is judging and “hasting righteousness.”

Isaiah tells Moab, “hide the outcasts; bewray not him that wandereth”, and “Let mine outcasts dwell with thee, Moab; be thou a covert to them from the face of the spoiler.” The outcast is us, the Israelites; that is why verse 1 speaks of “the mount of the daughter of Zion.” During the time of Nebuchadnezzar many Israelites fled and hid amongst Moab, and the spoiler they hid from was Nebuchadnezzar.

Jeremiah is the proof of where our people fled: “Likewise when all the Jews that were in Moab, and among the Ammonites, and in Edom, and that were in all the countries, heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant of Judah, and that he had set over them Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan.”

Where were they? In Moab, among the Ammonites, and in Edom. When the king of Babylon came through, Judah scattered into those lands and hid there, just as Isaiah told Moab to hide them. And “Sela” in verse 1 is Petra, which is Edom; they call Edom Petra today.

There is a dual meaning behind these scriptures. What happened with our people and Moab in the time of Nebuchadnezzar speaks again to the last days, when Moab is China and our people are outcasts among the nations, until “the extortioner is at an end, the spoiler ceaseth, the oppressors are consumed out of the land” and the throne of Christ is established.

Isaiah 9:7 says, “Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Why does it say the increase of his government? Christ answers in a parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: Which indeed is the least of all seeds.”

And their thoughts are the white man's thoughts. Our people follow all these man-made religions, and they don't teach God's laws, his commandments, his statutes. We ain't got to keep no laws, because that is what all these white people were teaching: don't keep no laws.

So what do you get? Those vipers hatch eggs, and what comes out? Little vipers, little snakes. Your son, little Tyrone, is a snake, and your daughter, little Chenique, was a snake too. That is what God is saying in Isaiah 59:5, and it is why verse 7 says “their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity”: a rebellious people walking after their own thoughts.

Isaiah 59 says they “weave the spider’s web” and “Their webs shall not become garments”. Job explains the spider's web. “So are the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrite’s hope shall perish: Whose hope shall be cut off”, because they are hypocrites, “and whose trust shall be a spider’s web.”

Their trust shall be as a spider's web: you get tangled up in that thing, and that spider comes out and bites you and eats you up.

“He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: he shall hold it fast, but it shall not endure.” Your house won't stand. A people who forget God weave their webs and lean on what they built, but it cannot cover them or hold them up. That is why Isaiah 59:6 goes on, “neither shall they cover themselves with their works: their works are works of iniquity, and the act of violence is in their hands.”

Now Christ is speaking to them: “O generation of vipers”. That goes back to Isaiah 59, the cockatrice' eggs that break out into a viper. Christ called them vipers, and John the Baptist called them vipers. And their children are little snakes too.

“how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.” What is in the heart comes out of the mouth. A generation of vipers cannot speak good things, because what fills their heart is evil.

That is Isaiah 59 again. Before verse 5, verse 3 said our lips have spoken lies and our tongue perverseness. The lips speak lies and the tongue perverseness because the heart is full of iniquity, and the eggs they hatch are the same kind as the ones who laid them.

Isaiah 59:5 says “They hatch cockatrice’ eggs”, and a cockatrice is like a poisonous snake. Put together everything from verses two to four, the iniquities that separated us from our God, the hands defiled with blood, the lips that have spoken lies, and this is what comes of it: “he that eateth of their eggs dieth, and that which is crushed breaketh out into a viper.” The eggs that are crushed are the kids that come out: a little baby snake. They produce evil followers.

Many years ago at a community meeting a black woman screamed at the police that they were selling drugs in her building and nobody was doing anything. The police set up a sting and locked up two dudes putting drugs in the mailboxes: her own sons. Then she came back saying it was false, with them on video. These are the eggs, the snake eggs coming out.

John the Baptist saw the same thing: “But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers”. That is the same thing Isaiah was talking about. “who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance”.

A generation of vipers cannot just say it repents. You have to bring forth God's commandments in application; that is what proves your repentance.

“But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The great house is the nation of Israel; think of it as whatever IUIC school you come from. Every camp leader, the head of the sanctuary, must be able to identify the gold brothers and the silver brothers, the gold sisters and silver sisters, and also look through the school and say, this brother and this sister is earth, this one is wood.

If you can't discern that, you'll have problems in the school, putting people in positions that don't fit them. Marcus Garvey had his ships and put his best friends over them, and they didn't know how to run a ship: one crashed, one went to his girlfriend's house, and he lost it all because of friendship. Shake the friendship appointments. Who is best qualified? Who knows what they're doing? A dummy who doesn't study set up as a school leader, and all hell breaks loose. If sanctuary leaders have no discernment, they are spiritually blind and destined for ruin.

Some brothers and sisters are just slow and need more time to grow. Fine; don't put them in that position yet if others are better qualified. “If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use, and prepared unto every good work.” Purge yourself from the wood and earth spirits. They see this truth not as a government, not as the mustard seed of a government, but as a social club, dancing every new moon and confused when it comes to God's work. That is how a people groping like the blind becomes vessels unto honour.

“Yea, truth faileth; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey.” If you depart from evil by repenting, you make yourself a prey to everybody around you; everybody around you hates your guts now. Amos says the same thing: “They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly.”

That includes some of your own mothers and fathers, sisters and brothers. They hate the one who rebukes and abhor the one who speaks uprightly, because “truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter.”

“and the Lord saw it, and it displeased him that there was no judgment.” There was no true judgment in the earth. The one who departs from evil is hated for it, and the Lord sees it.

“We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes: we stumble at noonday as in the night; we are in desolate places as dead men.” We got eyes, but we act like we ain't got none. We act like what we just saw didn't happen. The curse said it would be so: “And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.”

We are like blind people, but we have eyes. We see we're not prospering as a people. We see we're under constant oppression as a people. But we act like we don't see it, because oppression has become so normal to us; it's our everyday life.

It's high noon, but in our minds we are so spiritually blind it is like night for us. “we are in desolate places as dead men”: that's the black and brown community, desolate places, our people like the walking dead. Isaiah 59 is Deuteronomy 28:29 in real time.

That is why verse 9 says, “Therefore is judgment far from us, neither doth justice overtake us.” We want to live filthy lives, evil lives, violent lives, and then expect justice from God. It don't work like that. Oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.

There is a difference between being spiritually slow and being spiritually dead. “we are in desolate places as dead men,” but Sirach shows what the nation needs: “Again, there is another that is slow, and hath need of help, wanting ability, and full of poverty.” We usually read it as an individual, but think about it on a bigger scale. You might say this is Joe or Bob. No, this is us.

Slow, needing help, lacking ability, full of poverty: that is our people. “yet the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good, and set him up from his low estate,” and lifted up his head from misery, so that many that saw it marvelled at him.

The nations are going to marvel when God raises us up. It will be such a shock that this low, degenerate race of people is now going to rule the earth. We lack the ability now; it is the Lord's eye that sets us up from our low estate.

The voices of our people conceive and utter from the heart words of falsehood, lies on top of lies. Christ answers: “He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.” If you believe on the black Messiah, you are not condemned; if you believe not, you're not even keeping commandment one.

“And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Christ is that light that came into the world, and men love darkness, sin, rather than light, Christ and keeping the commandments. It didn't change from Isaiah to John; it's the same thing: “we wait for light, but behold obscurity.”

“For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved.” They hate Christ, they hate keeping the laws, they hate the commandments, because if you come to Christ your deeds will be reproved: have no other gods before me, bow down to no graven image, remember the Sabbath, honour your father and your mama, thou shalt not kill. They don't want to hear that.

“But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.” We want Christ, the word of God, to make our deeds manifest. What am I? Lord, show me.

Isaiah says the government shall be upon his shoulder, “upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice.” Jeremiah says the same: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch.” That righteous Branch is Christ.

“and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.” See what he is going to do: execute judgment and justice in the earth. The nations don’t want that. Some of us in here may not want that either: I don’t want no justice and judgment, hell no. Yes, it is coming anyway.

“In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.”

So the throne of David in Isaiah 9 is the reign of this King, the Branch raised unto David. The increase of his government is a kingdom of judgment and justice, of law and order, and in his days Judah is saved and Israel dwells safely. That is why we learn God’s laws now: it is the government we are going to live under.

Isaiah calls the son that is given “The everlasting Father.” Most Christians, and even some Israelites, cannot explain that, because they have not figured out that the everlasting Father in the Old Testament was Christ. They say we always spoke to the Father. No, you did not speak to the Father; you spoke to Christ. That is why he is called the everlasting Father. John 14 is a precept for it.

“Philip saith unto him, Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us.” See Christ’s response: “Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Shew us the Father?”

Yes, Christ looks like his Father. But what is he actually telling Philip? I created you. I am your Father, your everlasting Father. You were brought forth through me.

Remember, Christ is the only begotten of the Father. That means the Father created only Christ, and then told Christ to create everything else. So when Isaiah names the child born unto us “The mighty God, The everlasting Father”, it is because everything that exists was brought forth through him. That is why Philip, who had been with him so long, should have known him.

In case anyone is still confused about why Christ is called “The everlasting Father”, John 1 settles it. We have to shake the Christian thoughts.

“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” Christ was in the beginning with God, and he was God. “The same was in the beginning with God.” God is a plural there.

Then the part that matters: “All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” All things were made by Christ, and without Christ was not any thing made that was made. The Father only begat Christ, and through Christ everything else was created.

That is why he said to Philip, “Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip?” I created all of this. That is too heavy for a Negro, because you have Baptist on your mind and Catholic in your head. It was hard for us in the beginning too, but the Most High has shown us. Let it marinate.

So the child born and the son given in Isaiah 9:6, with the government upon his shoulder, is the same one who made all things: the Word, the mighty God, the everlasting Father.

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Christ explains that increase in Matthew 13: “The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: Which indeed is the least of all seeds.” If you grew up in the city you may not know what a mustard seed looks like; it is one of the smallest of all seeds.

“but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs.” When it is grown: that is the increase of his government. It starts small. What we have here is small. We may think we have a lot, but this is nothing yet; we are still at the mustard seed stage.

And the kingdom of heaven is a government, not a church group. That is why it behooves us to learn God’s laws, commandments and statutes: to set up a government you need everything that makes a community, and God’s laws are going to filter everything for us. Right now we think small. God says think bigger. A house? Bigger. Property? Bigger. The world is ours, and for the world to be ours we have to be able to set all of that up.

Think how the Most High uses something as small as the human mind. As a man thinketh, so is he. Everything you lay your eyes on, every object and invention, was a thought first. We shortchange ourselves with doubt, but that is not what God made. Untapped greatness is waiting to bud; remove the doubt and the fear and let the Lord work on that head.

The mustard seed government is small now, and we think small. Compare what God did for Solomon with where we are today.

“I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches.” Solomon learned wisdom and gave it out freely, and that is what we are doing today: we don’t hide the riches of the wisdom of God. “For she is a treasure unto men that never faileth: which they that use become the friends of God, being commended for the gifts that come from learning.” If we use this wisdom we become the friends of God. And it comes from learning, not once but daily; that is what the classes every day are about.

“For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements.” You might say you know how the world was made. You don’t: what elements make the air, what elements were made for the sun? Solomon understood that. He knew “The beginning, ending, and midst of the times”, from Adam to the second coming of Christ. He knew “the alterations of the turning of the sun, and the change of seasons”, “The circuits of years, and the positions of stars.”

“The natures of living creatures”: Esau puts cameras on animals, even in their butts, to learn how they defecate, trying to get on Solomon’s level with all that freakiness. Solomon knew “the furies of wild beasts”, “the violence of winds”, the tornadoes and storms, “the reasonings of men”, “the diversities of plants and the virtues of roots”, which herb is for what, and “all such things as are either secret or manifest, them I know.”

We are not even on Solomon’s level yet. We need the Lord to open our minds up to get there, and when he does we will be on that level and greater. That is what the mustard seed is about: we start small and it grows. This is the beginning of that government.

Leviticus 26 says that even “when they be in the land of their enemies”, like today here in America, “I will not cast them away, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly”. Then: “But I will for their sakes remember the covenant of their ancestors”. Who said bloodline ain’t important? The Bible says he will remember the covenant of your ancestors. Luke 1 is saying the same thing in the New Testament.

“Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David”. The horn of salvation is Christ. He is the king, out of the house of David. “As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us”. That is what Leviticus 26 is saying: in the land of their enemies he will not cast them away.

“To perform the mercy promised to our fathers”, our ancestors, “and to remember his holy covenant; The oath which he sware to our father Abraham”. That is the covenant of the ancestors in Leviticus 26:45, remembered for their sakes and brought to pass through Christ.

And what is it for? “that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear”. The God who brought our fathers out of Egypt in the sight of the heathen has not broken his covenant with us. He will deliver us out of the hand of our enemies so that we serve him without fear.

A critic was played mocking the Israelites, quoting “Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest” as if Christ said it to everybody: come unto me all ye, not you that accept that I'm black. That is what Edom is doing now, hiring black people, dumb Africans, to use Zionist talking points against the truth. We didn't say it; a black man said it. So here is the precept he does not know.

“And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve.” Rest from what? From thy sorrow. From thy fear. From the hard bondage: that's slavery. Wherein thou wast made to serve. The man on the screen don't know what the hell he's talking about.

The rest Christ promises the labouring and heavy laden is rest from the sorrow, the fear and the hard bondage of Israel's captivity. The ones heavy laden are the people who were made to serve. That is who “come unto me” is addressed to.

Isaiah opens the chapter by saying who gets that rest: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel.” We are messed up as a people, not in our right minds yet, but because of the covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob he will yet choose us. That's mercy, and we need that mercy.

“For through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half”. If it took us a year and a half to get from one area to another, don’t you think we were making stops? Maritime means things connected with the sea, oceans and navigation: shipping, commerce, naval operations. We were running those ports, and even where it was not us particularly, we had understanding with the nations we passed by. The Red Sea and the Indian Ocean connected Africa to the wider world as early as the third century BCE, with trade to Arabia, India, Persia and China.

Solomon had a navy of ships: “And king Solomon made a navy of ships in Ezion–geber, which is beside Eloth, on the shore of the Red sea, in the land of Edom. And Hiram sent in the navy his servants, shipmen that had knowledge of the sea, with the servants of Solomon.” Shipmen that had knowledge of the sea: those are the maritime men.

Ezion-geber is at the northern tip of the Red Sea’s Gulf of Aqaba, by modern-day Aqaba in Jordan and Eilat. That is very near the region where the brothers entered into the Euphrates. “And they came to Ophir, and fetched from thence gold, four hundred and twenty talents, and brought it to king Solomon.” Ophir is not far from those same areas.

So we had maritime trade going on even in Solomon’s time. It was no mystery for us to make it from where we were, out of Persia, over to the Americas, because those ports were there. That is how the journey took a year and a half, stopping at the ports, until we came into the region called Arsareth, the land Columbus identified with America.

Between verse 40 and verse 41 of 2 Esdras 13 there is a whole lot of history. Verse 40 is Assyria: “whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive”, before Babylon and before the Persians. Then Babylon took down Assyria and took her captives, and moved down and took Judah. Then the Persians came in. None of that is mentioned in the two verses; it jumps from Assyria to Persia, under Cyrus. So when verse 41 says “But they took this counsel among themselves”, what is the counsel? Ezra shows it.

“Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the Lord God of Israel, (he is the God,) which is in Jerusalem.” It is Cyrus speaking: the proclamation between the Most High and him, allowing Israel to go back and build in exchange for being able to take down Babylon.

“And whosoever remaineth in any place where he sojourneth, let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts, beside the freewill offering for the house of God that is in Jerusalem.” That was what was charged to Israel to go and do.

But the counsel the tribes took among themselves was different: “that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt”. The bulk of them said, we are not staying; we are not going back to build in Jerusalem; we are going to a further country. Ezra and Nehemiah are the first two books of Ezra, and 1 Esdras and 2 Esdras are the third and fourth, and together they detail this history.

Solomon’s ships “came to Ophir, and fetched from thence gold”. Isaiah uses that same gold: “I will make a man more precious than fine gold; even a man than the golden wedge of Ophir.”

We often read this and keep going, and some will say it is the best gold, but we don’t go deeper into what the gold of Ophir is. The gold of Ophir is an exceptionally fine, pure gold, prized in the ancient world, famous as what King Solomon and King Hiram of Tyre brought in, and its exact location remains one of history’s greatest archaeological mysteries.

That is what the Most High is going to make you men: that pure fine gold. The same tribes who crossed the waters on those old maritime routes, whose record the historians call mythical, are the men the Most High will make more precious than the golden wedge of Ophir.

Moses said “thy life shall hang in doubt before thee”. When we got emancipated we thought we were free. Juneteenth. Then the white man took the sheet out of the closet, cut two holes in it, put on the white robe, and it was time for the KKK, patterned after the capirotes of Spain from the Inquisition. Spain was in this country, and what they had over there they brought here. As soon as we thought we were free, they gave us hell.

The Most High speaks to that in Zechariah: “And I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease: for I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction.” God was a little displeased with us, because we broke his laws and his commandments. But the heathen afflicted us more and more and more. That is what God is saying right there.

Then back to Moses: “thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life”. Imagine building your own town because white folks don't want you drinking their water or going to their school: your own cab company, your own hospital, your own bank. Then you hear a noise, and they are dropping dynamite on the city from planes and murdering a lot of us. That is the heathen helping forward the affliction, far beyond the little displeasure God had with us.

So the curses of Deuteronomy 28 came on us for our sins, but the nations went further than God sent them, and he is very sore displeased with them for it. The heathen that are at ease today are the ones who will answer for what they added to our affliction.

Cain said, “Behold, thou hast driven me out this day from the face of the earth; and from thy face shall I be hid”: God was not dealing with him anymore. “and I shall be a fugitive and a vagabond in the earth.” A fugitive is somebody always on the run, someone who never pays for his crimes. A vagabond is in everybody's land and everybody's home.

But Cain did not escape forever. Wisdom shows he was put to death: “But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.” Cain murdered Abel, and Cain was killed the same way. The judgment caught up with him.

So what did it mean, I shall be a fugitive and a vagabond? It speaks of his descendants. Has America paid for its crimes? Have the whites in South Africa paid? In Australia? None of them has paid for their crimes yet. They have been on the run from justice, living in everybody's land.

That goes with Job 20, read in the same class: “His bones are full of the sin of his youth.” The fugitive has never paid, but as Cain perished in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother, judgment will come on his children. As Job said, “he shall vomit them up again”: everything taken will be restored.

God will “purely purge away thy dross.” Paul uses that same word, purge. “But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver.” The great house is the nation of Israel, the twelve tribes. We are not speaking for the other camps, with their cookouts on the Sabbath, their raping of girls, their stealing money for Maseratis and beating the baby mothers; we speak for Israel United in Christ. In every IUIC school, Philly, DC, Virginia, New York, Atlanta, Connecticut, OKC, there are men and women who are gold and silver, and it is up to you to discern and identify who they are.

“but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” In every school there are also brothers and sisters of wood and of earth: they are not right. This is not about new brothers and sisters who just walked through the door; we all walk in not right. It is about men and women in this truth for years who have not changed: still murmurers and gossipers, putting forth no work and no effort to study and improve. To them it is a social club, a place to hang out with the homeboys, drink a little wine, then go home and play dominoes. The vessels of dishonor are here to try you, and every bird clings to its like; see who groups together.

“If a man therefore purge himself from these”: you have to know your circle. When the Bishop came into the truth he had a circle of five or six brothers he was always getting in trouble around, down to jumping the turnstile with them and getting a ticket. He had to change his circle and get around leadership and the elders to get his mind right. Don’t worry about hurting feelings; if you know they are not right, separate from them.

“he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.” Then God can use you. Then we can send that brother to a city or a state and he can grow a whole congregation, like Isaiah telling the Lord, send me.

And this is why we cannot join with the other camps: it is based on what we just read. Only a fool would do that. The same purging God does in Isaiah, we must do ourselves.

“And I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin.” Dross is waste, refuse, any worthless matter, and the tin goes with the dross. God will turn his hand upon us, the Israelites, and purge away everything within us that is wasteful and useless. What is that? Christ lists it.

“For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts”: from within, out of the mind of men. Evil thoughts: that is dross and tin. “adulteries, fornications, murders, Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness”: every one of them is dross and tin. Add the rest we carry: lying, stealing, child molestation, masturbation, pornography, bestiality, anger, malice. All of it.

“All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” The dross is not outside of us; it is in us, and that is what God is purging.

So that one verse speaks volumes. The “thee” God turns his hand upon is you and me, and what he purges away is everything that proceeds out of our own hearts and defiles us, so that afterward Israel can be called “The city of righteousness, the faithful city.”

For the dross to be purged away, we have to go through some things. Paul shows it: “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also.” When you read Paul in Hebrews 12 he tells you nobody rejoices in tribulation, but here he gives you the after effect. Why glory in tribulation? “knowing that tribulation worketh patience.” That tribulation goes back to Ecclesiasticus 2: when you come to serve the Lord, prepare your soul for temptation, the hard times. When you go through hell, you learn patience.

“And patience, experience.” Patience gives you experience. A lot of us come into this truth at 30, 40, 50 with experience in the world, but in the truth of God we have no experience. That is the experience we need.

“and experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed.” Experience teaches us hope, and hope makes us not ashamed, because we endure to the end, “because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.”

So the purging of Isaiah 1:25 is done through tribulation. God turns his hand upon us, and what we go through works patience, experience and hope in us, until the dross and the tin are gone.

Isaiah tells the virgin daughter of Babylon, “Stand now with thine enchantments, and with the multitude of thy sorceries, wherein thou hast laboured from thy youth.” God is telling you straight that this Babylon deals in witchcraft. Some might think they are clever and say there are two different Babylons. No: Revelation 18 shows it is the same Babylon the great.

“And a mighty angel took up a stone like a great millstone, and cast it into the sea, saying, Thus with violence shall that great city Babylon be thrown down, and shall be found no more at all.” That is the same end Isaiah gives: “desolation shall come upon thee suddenly.”

“And the light of a candle shall shine no more at all in thee; and the voice of the bridegroom and of the bride shall be heard no more at all in thee: for thy merchants were the great men of the earth.” The merchants are their corporations, the same merchants Isaiah names: “even thy merchants, from thy youth: they shall wander every one to his quarter; none shall save thee.”

“for by thy sorceries were all nations deceived.” By her sorceries all nations were deceived. That is imagery: what they put out in television and movies to manipulate the people, the way the Huxtables were an example. A film about the young George Washington dropped in theaters just this week, and it is not a coincidence: they want to bring the patriot spirit back for the 250th anniversary. It is witchcraft.

And she has laboured in it from her youth: 1776 is her youth, one of the youngest nations on the planet, with Washington DC laid out by the Freemasons in an upside down pentagram, the White House at the bottom point. That is the star some of our people wear while barbecuing on the Fourth of July, and they should be ashamed. Her astrologers and stargazers “shall be as stubble; the fire shall burn them”, and Babylon is thrown down with violence.

Isaiah says “Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net”. That is why our young men hang on the corners: uncontrollable, like wild bulls in a net. “I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: my judgment was as a robe and a diadem.” That shows you how Job used to dress. The way he dressed, that is how his righteousness reflected.

Eliphaz the Temanite, one of Job's friends, tells him, “Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.” You were the one that strengthened men and women when they were weak; your words upheld those that fell down in grief and in sin. “But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.” Now judgment has come upon you, Job, and now you have given up, you have lost the spirit. Where is that mighty man that helped all the people? Now you're upset, your lips stuck out, you got an attitude.

In a clip shown in class, an Arab man said plainly that everybody is anti-black, not just the Arabs. Reflect back on this verse: he didn't lie. Christ said everybody is against us. Everybody.

Paul writes: “As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.” That is prophecy right there. And where is it written? “And this is the blessing of Judah: and he said, Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah”. Judah is going to be the teachers. “and bring him unto his people”: Judah is the one the spirit comes on first, to go and gather the tribes. “let his hands be sufficient for him; and be thou an help to him from his enemies.”

God will shake his hand upon the nations, and the nations shall be a spoil to their servants. The wording might be difficult for some of us, so here is a precept to explain it further.

“Therefore as I live, saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, even the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation”. The nations that made us serve are going to be spoiled by us and possessed by us. America is described as Babylon, the land of the north, and the day is coming when the ones who served there will spoil it.

“For the most High then shewed signs for them, and held still the flood, till they were passed over.” The tribes that left the heathen went into the Euphrates “by the narrow places of the river” and down into the ocean, and the Most High was with them. He showed them signs, and there were men among them able to read those signs.

“And of the children of Issachar, which were men that had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do; the heads of them were two hundred; and all their brethren were at their commandment.” Issachar could read the stars. That is how they were the navigators: they had understanding of the times, they knew what Israel ought to do, and so they were able to lead the ships as the tribes came over. They knew how to navigate the waters.

They understood the winds and the currents, the Atlantic drift routes from Africa to America. Solomon understood all of this too, with the navy he had going out; the same ports Solomon’s navy knew were the stops along the route, because “through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half”. African boatmen from Lake Chad later built a papyrus boat on the pattern of the ancient Egyptians and sailed it from North Africa as far as Barbados, proving such a drift journey on the Africa-to-America currents could be done, because the currents were understood.

So the ten tribes did not wander blindly into “a further country, where never mankind dwelt”. After Christ dealt with Judah, “he must needs go through Samaria.” There the woman said, “How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” The southern kingdom did not deal with the northern kingdom. Zebulun and Naphtali were carried away, and their land became Galilee of the nations, of the Gentiles.

Then Isaiah says what would come to them: “The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.” Matthew gives it back as “The people which sat in darkness saw great light.” Isaiah is prophesying and Matthew is revealing what it is really talking about.

“From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” Christ was that great light spoken of, shining on the scattered tribes of Israel that had been made Gentiles.

David says, “Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: they shall prosper that love thee.” Some of y'all are busy praying for Haiti, praying for Puerto Rico, praying for Mexico, praying for America. But the Bible said pray for Jerusalem.

Isaiah says how to pray for it: “And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.” Give the Lord no rest until he establishes Jerusalem and makes it a praise in the earth.

Remember, Jerusalem is a people before it is a place. We are Jerusalem; pray for us. We are not supposed to be praying, stop the war over there. No: they have to be moved out of our land so that we can go back home. That is the peace of Jerusalem, and that is the prayer that gives God no rest until it is done.

The psalm says that in Jerusalem “there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” Christ tells his apostles who sits on them and whom they judge: “And I appoint unto you a kingdom, as my Father hath appointed unto me; That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”

Sit on thrones doing what? Judging the twelve tribes of Israel. The thrones of judgment are for Israel, just as the tribes that go up to Jerusalem are “the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel.”

So don't read all this and try to throw the Chinese and the Japanese and everybody in there. Stop it. The kingdom, the table, the thrones and the judgment all belong to the twelve tribes.

David says of Jerusalem, “For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” John saw those thrones: “And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them.”

Thrones set, people sitting on them, and judgment given to them. And who are they? The souls “beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.”

The thrones of judgment in the psalm are real thrones in the kingdom, where the faithful reign with Christ. That is the Jerusalem the tribes go up to, and that is why we pray for its peace: it is a people before it is a place, and those thrones belong to us.

David says, “Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together: Whither the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel.” Other nations aren't there; they are not mentioned here. Why does it say the city is compact together? Revelation shows the city.

It “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.” This is our book. The kingdom is ours. The names on the gates are the tribes that go up.

“And the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal.” So it is 1,500 miles, the length, the breadth and the height all equal, like a square, like a box. That is a city compact together.

“And he measured the wall thereof, an hundred and forty and four cubits, according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel.” A hundred and forty-four cubits is approximately 216 feet by a man's measure, but it is the measure of the angel, so it is actually larger. That is the Jerusalem the tribes of the Lord go up to.
