Ezra says that after Adam transgressed, death came “in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number.” Genesis 4 shows one of those lines: Cain's. And in Cain's line, “Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and organ.”

Cain's line handled the music. They were behind all the music back then, and music is very influential, very powerful when it is in the wrong hands. Is it in the wrong hands today? Yes, it is.

Then Tubal-cain was “an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”, and brass and iron mean weapons. So Cain had power over entertainment and power over weaponry and warfare. Remember Esau was a man of war; that was Esau's blessing, and it was Cain's blessing too. There is nothing new under the sun.

This is how “every people walked after their own will, and did wonderful things before thee, and despised thy commandments.” Wonderful there means evil; they started to mess around with the daughters of men. And they despised the commandments, which shows the commandments were around back then; that is how Noah knew clean from unclean. The wicked had the music and the weapons then, the same as they do now, and it ended in the flood that destroyed them.

After Cain slew Abel, “Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel.” Seth was Abel's replacement, the replacement of righteousness in the earth.

“And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the Lord.” Ezra says the nations that came out of Adam “despised thy commandments.” When the sons of God despised God's commandments, God stopped dealing with us. But once Seth had Enos, that line began to call upon the name of the Lord, and God started dealing with us again.

Those tribes back then were called the sons of God. Tribes, sons of God: that sounds like the Israelites. Nothing new under the sun. The tribes of the sons of God were around back then and they are around now; wicked, evil leaders were around back then, and the righteous are around now. The wickedness is always around, and the righteous are always born within the evil.

That line carries straight to the flood. Ezra says God brought the flood on those that dwelt in the world, “Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely, Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men.” That goes back to Shem's line: not Ham's line, not Japheth's line, but Shem's, the line that came down from Seth.

Solomon says it again in chapter 3: “That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath already been; and God requireth that which is past.”

It is the same as “The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be”. One generation comes and another goes; the old die and the young are born. The sun has its cycle, the wind has its circuits, and the rivers run into the sea and return again. Generations have their circuits and cycles the same way.

So what is to be has already been. Before our generation it was already in the past, only “There is no remembrance of former things”. That is why a man can stand in a moment and feel, I remember this.

What is the thing that hath been? Solomon names it: “That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man”. So he explains it himself: the thing that have been is man.

Just like the wind, the sun, the moon and the rivers have a flow, likewise man: we come and we go. You and I have been here before, in different cycles of life. That is why it is called deja vu, a French term that literally means already seen: the sensation of having already experienced a situation even though you know it is happening for the first time.

Already seen, because you are already meant to be there. The prophets saw things that came to pass. When the prophets saw us going on slave ships, we had to live out what they saw. So when John saw America in flames, we have to live out what John already saw. We are catching up to the prophecies, and what leads up to them is already set in motion. You can't change it.

“Who is as the wise man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing?” The wise man knows the interpretation of the thing. And “a man’s wisdom maketh his face to shine”.

The thing that hath been, in Ecclesiastes 1, is talking about man. Man has been around before, but “There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after.” It takes wisdom to interpret that thing.

So the wise man understands the cycle: the generations pass and come again, and what the prophets already saw is what we are living out now. The wise man knows it is man that hath been, and that is why there is no new thing under the sun.

Isaac told Esau, “And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother.” That goes right back to Cain being a fugitive and a vagabond: wandering all around, in lands that don't belong to him, acquiring them by the sword, killing and massacring and holding himself unaccountable. Some say they did not steal the Native Americans' land, they conquered it. What is the difference? After you conquered it, did you give it back? You kept it and gave it to your children, and then gave land to the Irish and British who came afterward and conquered nothing. That is stealing.

“and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck”: once David's lineage went off, Esau broke free of our rule and began to conquer. “And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing,” and said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” What did Cain do to Abel? He slew him. Nothing new under the sun: the same people doing the same exact thing. Rebekah told Jacob, “thy brother Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee”: how evil, to find comfort in killing your own brother.

Wisdom tells what became of Cain: “But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.” The unrighteous is Cain. When he killed Abel it was not a tap on the back of the head; he brutally killed him in his fury. And Cain was killed too, the same violent way he killed Abel.

That is why Rebekah said, “why should I be deprived also of you both in one day?” She knew: if Esau killed Jacob, God would kill Esau. You kill your brother, and you are going to die too.

Rebekah told Jacob to flee to her brother Laban's house because Esau wanted him dead, so he ran to Laban, and “Jacob fed the rest of Laban’s flocks.” He took rods of green poplar, hazel and chesnut, “pilled white strakes in them,” and set them before the flocks at the watering troughs. The stronger cattle conceived among the rods, “so the feebler were Laban’s, and the stronger Jacob’s.” “And the man increased exceedingly.”

So Jacob was Laban's shepherd; he took care of the sheep and the cattle. He was a shepherd just as Abel was a shepherd, and Esau was the man of the field just as Cain was a man of the field. The same two lines keep repeating.

And Jacob tells what that shepherding cost him: “This twenty years have I been with thee;” “That which was torn of beasts I brought not unto thee; I bare the loss of it.” “Thus I was; in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep departed from mine eyes.” “I served thee fourteen years for thy two daughters, and six years for thy cattle: and thou hast changed my wages ten times.”

Laban was a grimy man. He did Jacob dirty: Jacob took care of his cattle day and night, bore the losses himself, and Laban kept lowering his pay. Yet God increased Jacob exceedingly in spite of it.

“Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly.” “So look upon all the works of the most High; and there are two and two, one against another.” There is always a good side and a bad side.

Genesis 5 shows it. “Jared lived an hundred sixty and two years, and he begat Enoch.” Wait a minute: didn't Cain have a son named Enoch too? He did. Seth's Enoch “walked with God: and he was not; for God took him,” taken up the way Elijah was, walking with God just as Noah walked with God. You had a righteous Enoch and a wicked Enoch.

It goes on down the line. Seth's line had Methuselah, who lived “nine hundred sixty and nine years,” the longest of any man, and Lamech, who named his son Noah, “saying, This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which the Lord hath cursed,” the ground cursed when Adam sinned. Cain's line had its own Lamech. Two and two, one against another.

Genesis 5 keeps saying each father “begat sons and daughters,” yet it names specific sons, because those particular children were significant: they birthed prophets. Among the other sons and daughters there was wickedness. That is why Noah is named and found perfect: he had siblings, but he was the righteous one out of all the sons of God of his time dealing with the daughters of men.

Sirach names the righteous line: “Sem and Seth were in great honour among men, and so was Adam above every living thing in creation.” Adam had his righteous child, Seth, born “in his own likeness, after his image,” and Noah had his righteous child, Shem: “Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.”

And out of Shem's line came us. The line God honoured runs from Adam through Seth to Noah and on through Shem to Israel.

These are Cain's children: “And unto Enoch was born Irad: and Irad begat Mehujael: and Mehujael begat Methusael: and Methusael begat Lamech.” So Cain had a son named Enoch, a descendant named Methusael, and one named Lamech.

Now set that beside Genesis 5, Seth's line: Jared begat Enoch, Enoch begat Methuselah, Methuselah begat Lamech, and Lamech begat Noah. The same names on both sides. It is always two: the left hand side of wickedness and the righteous side. Cain had his Lamech and his Enoch; Seth's line had its Lamech and its Enoch. Righteous Enoch, evil Enoch.

That is Ecclesiasticus 33 lived out in the generations before the flood: “there are two and two, one against another.” And the righteous line, the one named in Genesis 5, is the line of prophets that led to Noah, “a just man and perfect in his generations.”

“But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.” “Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God.” Noah was also a son of God, and out of all the sons of God in that time who were doing wickedness with Cain's daughters, Noah did not. There is always that light shining in the darkness all throughout time.

What does perfect mean, and what does it mean to walk with God? God told Abram, “I am the Almighty God; walk before me, and be thou perfect.” Meaning what? Keep his commandments. When it says Noah walked with God, it does not mean he went on long walks and talks on the beach with God. It means he walked in his ways.

Righteous, perfect and just all mean keeping God's commandments. The commandments that Seth kept, Noah was keeping also, while all flesh around him corrupted its way upon the earth.

God said of Abraham, “Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.” That is what it means to walk before God and be perfect.

Abraham kept the laws, statutes and commandments just as Noah did. “Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God”: he kept the commandments that Seth kept, and that is why he found grace in the eyes of the Lord when the rest of the earth was corrupt and filled with violence.

So the law was not new at Sinai. Noah kept it, Abraham kept it, and those who keep it are the ones God preserves when “The end of all flesh is come before me.”

“the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.” Who are the men here? Eve said of Cain that she had gotten a man from the Lord, so the daughters of men are Cain's children. The sons of God came out of Adam's line through Seth. And the sons of God started messing around with Cain's daughters.

Genesis 5 shows why Seth's line is called the sons of God: “In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him.” God made Adam in his likeness, so Adam was the son of God. “And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth.”

Was Cain made in Adam's image? No. Everyone is not made in God's image. Seth was, and Abel was, but Cain was not. Cain was a man of the Lord, a regular man; God made him, but he was not God's son. He was somebody else's son: of that wicked one.

So when the sons of God, made in God's likeness through Seth, took the daughters of Cain, the line that was in God's image mixed with the line that was not. The children “became mighty men which were of old, men of renown”: powerful, famous, fierce fighters, but wicked as hell, because they intermingled with Cain. Cain had built a city, and the sons of God began dwelling in it and following his ways, just as the sons of God today dwell in Esau's city and learn his ways.

Luke traces Christ's line all the way back: “Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.” There it is written plainly. Adam was the son of God, and that line, Seth's line, were the sons of God of Genesis 6.

Abel was one of them, but Cain killed him. Then Adam and Eve had Seth, who replaced Abel, and the line of the sons of God continued through him.

So “the sons of God saw the daughters of men” is Seth's line looking upon Cain's daughters. What followed is why “it repented the Lord that he had made man on the earth.” The sons of God started to behave like Cain and his daughters, and God said, “I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth”: destroy everything and start over. “The earth also was corrupt before God,” because the sons of God mingled with Cain's children; Cain gained dominion, “and the earth was filled with violence,” just as Cain was violent.

Genesis 7 ends with four words: “and the Lord shut him in.” Noah did not close that door; God did. Revelation 3:7 shows who holds that power: “he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth.” That is Christ, the one “that hath the key of David.”

Why did God close the door himself? Because of what Noah would hear outside. Noah was a man, and a man has a soft spot. There were babies out there, people begging for their babies, screaming and crying. Noah's own kin were out there too, his siblings and relatives, crying out, why are you doing this? If the door were left to Noah, he might have opened it. So God said, get back, I'll close the door. Noah had to sit inside and hear the screaming, the crying and the begging until there was nothing to hear anymore. That is a terrible thing to live through.

The door was shut only after a long season of mercy. Noah was a hundred years building that boat, and the people were warned the whole time: repent, stop following Cain, keep these laws. They said, we good. God was longsuffering with them. Noah was found righteous “in this generation” because he kept the commandments; that is how he knew the clean beasts from the unclean and how he walked with God. When the fountains of the great deep broke up and the windows of heaven opened, only the eight souls on that boat lived.

It is the same today. Right now the door of repentance is open, and Christ is longsuffering with our people. This is the time to get it right. Once that door is closed, that is it; no one can open it, the way the great gulf is fixed. As it was in the days of Noah, so it is now.

Christ said to his own people, “Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning”. Those same Jews wanted Christ dead; they were plotting to kill him. Did Satan murder anybody? No. Who killed in the beginning? Cain. Christ is calling him the devil. The Lord said to Cain he would hide his face from him, and Cain's father became the devil.

John says what Christ said in John 8:44: “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Cain was Satan's baby, spiritually obviously. “And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.” And he killed Abel savagely; it wasn't like he just cut his throat, it was very bad.

So “the lusts of your father ye will do” means the same way Cain killed his brother, you are going to kill me: the same spirit that was in Cain is in you. “and abode not in the truth”: in process of time Cain offered up fruit, when he was supposed to offer up animals. It is not talking about Satan, who was always a liar; that's his job. It's talking about Cain. When the Lord asked for his brother, Cain said I don't know. Was he lying? Yes: “he is a liar, and the father of it.”

The commentaries on Genesis 4:7 all tap dance around this and don't want to be honest about it. Be very careful about modern scholarship, because they hide things; older scholars are more upfront, and there is a movement set up to censor any biblical truth that can be substantiated.

The evil man and the violent man of Psalms 140 has a name, and Malachi gives it. “I have loved you, saith the Lord.” Israel asks, “Wherein hast thou loved us?” And the answer: “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” He loved Jacob just like he loved Abel, and he hated Esau. Laying his mountains and his heritage waste means God allowed him to be overthrown.

“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished”: we lost all, we are going back to being vagabonds. “but we will return and build the desolate places”: build themselves back up as an empire, just like Cain built that city. And the Lord answers, “They shall build, but I will throw down.”

“and they shall call them, The border of wickedness”: the beginning and the end of wickedness. “and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever”: no repentance, no salvation, no kingdom, ever. Not even the good ones, so some of you coons out there.

So when David prays “Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man” and “Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked”, this is who he is praying against: Esau, Edom, the people the Lord hated and against whom he hath indignation for ever.

“And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.” The kingdom of heaven, that's Israel, and Israel suffereth violence. The violent that take it by force are the Romans, and Esau is the Romans.

That puts a name on the man of Psalms 140. The Bible calls the evil man, the violent man, the wicked, and Esau is the violent man, the wicked man. “They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent; adders’ poison is under their lips”: they are liars. And they “have purposed to overthrow my goings.”

So David's cry, “preserve me from the violent man”, is Israel's cry to be kept from the hands of Esau, the Romans, who have done violence to the kingdom of heaven from the days of John the Baptist until now.

Holy, and beloved. Baruch shows who the beloved is: “He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.” Israel is his beloved, and it is to Israel he gave all the way of knowledge.

So the “holy and beloved” of Colossians 3:12 are the children of Israel: holy because he severed them from other people, beloved because he calls Israel his beloved.

That is why the Lord, through the apostle Paul, instructs the Colossians on how to deal with one another: “bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering; Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another”. Why? Because we are the same people. We are the sons and daughters of the living God, and there is a way we have to govern ourselves and treat each other.

In verse 11 Paul references us as the Greeks, the Barbarians and the Scythians. Then in verse 12 he says it one more time, plainly: “Put on therefore, as the elect of God”. He is speaking in a language we can understand, not for the heathens to understand. Isaiah tells us who the elect of God is: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect”.

Israel is his elect. So the elect of God that Paul is instructing in Colossians 3:12 are Israelites.

They know good and well this Bible don’t belong to them. But in slavery they played on our ignorance. We couldn’t read or write; they taught it to us by oral tradition, wouldn’t let us read the Bible, and gave us the slave Bible where the majority of the Bible wasn’t even there. They wanted to keep us docile, ignorant and misinformed. But there is a God, the God of Israel, who has poured his spirit upon his people in these last days, and now we know what the Bible is talking about: Israel mine elect.

Colossians 3:12 calls the elect of God “holy and beloved”. Leviticus tells us how to be holy, and who it is for: “And ye shall be holy unto me: for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine.”

Holy means severed, separated from all other nations on the face of the earth. He has severed us from other people, “that ye should be mine”: that ye, you Israelites, should be his people.

So right there in Colossians 3:12 the Lord is saying it ain’t all nations. Just in case anyone was confused by what Paul was saying in verse 11, he clears it up in verse 12. The ones told to put on mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness and longsuffering are the holy people, the ones severed from the other nations to be his.

Servants ruling over us happened with Assyria, Babylon, Persia, Greece, Rome, and America present day. The Lord explains it to Ezra: “And he said unto me, I will liken my judgment unto a ring”.

A ring is a circular motion. You see this curse? It comes right back around, empire after empire, and it keeps happening because we are the people of God. But this is the last time. All praise to the Most High.

So the slavery in America where Colossians 3:22 was used against us is one more turn of that ring of judgment on Israel. It was not the Lord making the white man our rightful master; it was his judgment coming back around on his own people, and it ends with this last time.

In 1673 Mr. Baxter published his Christian Directory with directions to masters in foreign plantations who have negroes and other slaves, a rubric to follow. In their evil minds they really believed they were masters. Did the Lord allow this to happen? Absolutely. But that is not what Colossians 3:22 is talking about. The first direction: remember that they have immortal souls and are equally capable of salvation with yourselves. That is where the false sense of equality comes from. It comes from slavery; it comes from Christianity.

Who is salvation for? “Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.” A savior brings salvation, and that salvation is only for the children of Israel.

They believed they could be saved and then us; they are the people, and we come after. That is not how it goes. The same directions said that they and you are equally under the government and laws of God, and that is incorrect: we are not equal with these people. Christ was exalted to give repentance to Israel, so the servants of Colossians and the salvation preached to them belong to Israel.

The slave masters' directions said that God is their reconciled tender father. God is our reconciled father, but that reconciliation is not for everybody. What does re mean? To do again: repeat, redo. Reconcile means to do it again. So if they wrote that reconciliation was for the slaves, that means they knew who we are.

Reconciliation cannot apply to the other nations, because they were never a people close or near to God. The Israelites are the only ones that have been close or near to God. Daniel shows it: “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.”

That is determined upon Daniel's people and holy city, and the most Holy anointed is Christ. Through Christ we get our reconciliation. So the very masters who twisted Colossians 3:22 wrote down, in their own directions, that their slaves were the people God reconciles: Israel.

The third direction to the masters: serve your necessities by your slaves so as to prefer God's interest and their spiritual and everlasting happiness; teach them the way to heaven. So in want of all things we wanted food, clothing, housing, shelter, and we also got that old time religion from them too.

“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”. In want of all things: even our religion had to come from the enemy we were serving.

The next page shows what that religion was for. They wrote that we were redeemed with them by Christ from the slavery of Satan and may live with them in the liberty of the saints in glory. They want us to go to heaven with them and live with them. That's called hell. That mind was beaten into us: a brother on the street asked if the Edomite could be saved, and said if he goes to hell, so will I, because he doesn't want to go anywhere without his master. That is the want of all things the curse brought, and why the master's reading of Colossians 3:22 still holds our people.

“Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh”. Going precept upon precept and in context, these servants would have to be Israelites, and these masters would have to be Israelites. It is a scripture they cherry-picked to fit their evil narrative. In The Religious Instruction of the Negroes in the United States they wrote of us, the 697,697 slaves of the 1790 census, as the original stock, in a state of absolute heathenism. They inserted themselves as the people and made us the heathens.

But the Lord did say this would happen: “Thus saith the Lord God; Because that Moab and Seir do say, Behold, the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen”. Moab and Seir look at the house of Judah and call us heathen.

How did we become like the heathen? By following after the heathen: celebrating their pagan rituals, Christmas, Thanksgiving; eating crab, shrimp, pork, lobster; praying to a white man. That is what makes us heathenistic. So the servants of Colossians 3:22 are Israel, and the enemy calling Judah heathen is only what the Lord already said Moab and Seir would say.

Our enemies would like to think God cast us away because we became like the heathen, and that he isn't going to redeem us. Even with us becoming heathens, this is what the Lord says: “Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham. And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed.”

The scripture foreseeing: the Lord already knew we were going to become heathens. He saw that this would happen to us, and he would justify us through faith, through Christ. They may be mad all over again; it doesn't matter. We are still God's chosen people.

So the heathen Galatians speaks of justifying is Israel fallen into heathenism, the same servants Colossians 3:22 speaks to. That justification is only for one people, as Isaiah 45:25 shows.

The masters' book called us the most needy of any people in their country. It does say needy, and the Bible says it too: “The instruments also of the churl are evil: he deviseth wicked devices to destroy the poor with lying words, even when the needy speaketh right.”

The needy in that book is us. The churl devised wicked devices with lying words: cherry-picking “Servants, obey in all things your masters”, writing directions for masters to bring slaves to their religion, forbidding our meetings and our reading.

And even when we speak straight out of the Bible, going precept upon precept, they call it hate speech. That is the needy speaking right and the churl answering with lying words to destroy the poor. So when Colossians 3:22 is read in context, it speaks of Israelite servants and Israelite masters, and the lying words that turned it against us are the churl's devices.

Galatians says God would “justify the heathen through faith”. Who is that justification for? “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.” Shall the seed of what be justified? Israel.

So it is what it is. Yes, we became heathen, following after the heathen in their holidays, their foods and their white image; but we are still going to be justified through Christ, and we shall glory. The justification is for one people, the seed of Israel.

That is why the servants of Colossians 3:22 are Israelites and not the slave master's property to be taught his religion. The masters' books called us heathens in need of their instruction, but the Lord had already written that all the seed of Israel, heathen as we became, would be justified in him.

The masters' own book says of us: they are in the eye of the law property. In the eyes of their laws, we were their property. The Lord told us why: “And it shall come to pass, when ye shall say, Wherefore doeth the Lord our God all these things unto us? then shalt thou answer them, Like as ye have forsaken me, and served strange gods in your land, so shall ye serve strangers in a land that is not yours.”

We are serving strangers in a land that is not ours, a land we are not familiar with. That is the servitude the Lord allowed because we forsook him.

So the slavery here was the curse on Israel for serving strange gods, not the obedience Colossians 3:22 teaches between Israelite servants and Israelite masters. They took the scripture and used it to hold us as property, but the Lord had already told us we would serve strangers.

Jeremiah said we would serve strangers in a land that is not ours. The Lamentations goes further: “Servants have ruled over us: there is none that doth deliver us out of their hand.” Servants have ruled over us. This is Bible prophecy.

It happened in the time of Assyria, Babylon, Persia, Greece, Rome, and America in the present day. It keeps happening over and over again. Why? Because we are the people of God. But this is the last time.

So the masters who took Colossians 3:22 and told us “Servants, obey in all things your masters” were themselves the servants ruling over Israel, just as the prophets lamented, with none to deliver us out of their hand.

We were their property, and they still view us as that. They may have said we were equal in salvation, but while we were here they treated us like beasts: chattel slavery, three-fifths of a man. They never looked at us as their equals.

Nehemiah prayed it: “And it yieldeth much increase unto the kings whom thou hast set over us because of our sins”. This is happening because we sinned against our God. “also they have dominion over our bodies, and over our cattle, at their pleasure, and we are in great distress.” Dominion over our bodies, to look at us as their property, at their pleasure.

Their own book says it plainly: they are in the eye of the law property over which there is an absolute control; and by law or custom we were excluded from education, and by consequence from the reading of the word of God. If we were equal, why were we excluded from education? Because they don't want us to know the truth of the Bible, that servants obey your masters isn't talking about them. They want to keep us docile and uneducated.

Their book says we may, according to the power lodged in our hands, forbid religious meetings, and no independent churches were allowed, so we depended on them alone. It went on during the Inquisition too, when they changed Christianity into the all-inclusive Catholic system and went around killing us, the real Jews, tearing up our safe houses and taking our book. The same thing is going to happen again, because now we know the truth. The only way the lie could hold strong was to destroy anybody who did not get down with it.

Revelation shows it: he “deceiveth them that dwell on the earth by the means of those miracles which he had power to do in the sight of the beast; saying to them that dwell on the earth, that they should make an image to the beast”. “And he had power to give life unto the image of the beast”: that is the false image of Christ. “that the image of the beast should both speak, and cause that as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed.”

If we did not agree to it, we were killed. Over time our people knew it wasn't true, but they didn't want to be killed, so they went with the lie, generation after generation. But it's a new generation on the earth, and we aren't accepting the lies any more. We know we are the people, and we know what comes with the territory.

Paul elaborates on the masters: “Let as many servants as are under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed.” The servants are under the yoke, the yoke of bondage. If you had a master who still believed in the law of sacrifice, but you believed on Christ, you still honoured him. He follows sacrifice, but you still treat him with respect.

“And they that have believing masters, let them not despise them, because they are brethren”. Now you have Israelite masters who believe on Christ. Don’t despise a master, your brother, that believes on Christ, because they are brethren.

Not one time has the Lord ever said we are brothers with the other nations. So that is showing you those masters are Israelites. When Colossians 4:1 tells masters to give their servants what is just and equal, it is speaking to Israelite masters over Israelite servants, their brethren.

Colossians 3:22, read in context, says “Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh; not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God”. Why? Your master was taking care of your clothes, your raiment, your housing, your food. So why would you disrespect him? Number one, that is your brother. Number two, he is doing this for you: as you do your duties and work, he takes care of you.

Sirach says it: “If a servant say to his master, I will not do as it pleaseth thee; though afterward he do it, he angereth him that nourisheth him.” The master nourishes the servant, and a servant who refuses him angers the one that feeds him.

And you are not just angering the master. You are also angering the Lord that nourisheth us. That is the order Colossians 4:1 completes from the other side: the servant honours the master, and the master gives the servant “that which is just and equal; knowing that ye also have a Master in heaven.”

“Masters, give unto your servants that which is just and equal”. They said that they were the masters. Did they do that? No. They were living in the big house; we were living in the outhouse, and when we got emancipated, did they ever give us the forty acres and the mule? No. So they are showing that they are hypocrites. They are impostors. They’re the damn devil that the Bible speaks of.

Remember, Colossians, Ephesians and Philemon were all written generally at the same time, to the same region. Ephesians says the same thing Colossians does: “Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh, with fear and trembling, in singleness of your heart, as unto Christ; Not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart”.

The servants are serving “as unto Christ”, as “the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart.” This is instruction to one people serving under Christ, not a charter for the slave masters of America, and the verse ends by reminding the masters they “also have a Master in heaven.”

Now this makes more sense: “There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.”

Neither Jew nor Greek we already understand from Colossians 3:11: the Greek-speaking Jews and the Jews. Neither bond nor free: the Israelite servant and the Israelite master. Neither male nor female: the manservant and the maidservant, the Israelite man and the Israelite woman.

“for ye are all one”: we are all one nation, under Christ. That is all it is talking about. So the servants and masters of Colossians 4:1 are one people in Christ, and that is why the master must give the servant what is just and equal.

To go a little deeper into who these servants are, Jeremiah says: “That every man should let his manservant, and every man his maidservant, being an Hebrew or an Hebrewess, go free; that none should serve himself of them, to wit, of a Jew his brother.”

Being a what? An Hebrew, or an Hebrewess. So these servants are Israelites. And the one they served was “a Jew his brother.”

That is the servant and master of Colossians 3:22 and 4:1: Israelite servants and Israelite masters, brothers. Christianity took a scripture about brethren and cherry-picked it to fit its evil narrative over us.

More on these servants: “For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.”

The children of Israel are servants, and they are his servants, the ones he brought out of Egypt. That is who the servants of Colossians are, and why the masters must remember they “also have a Master in heaven”: the servants belong to the Lord.

They changed the narrative and flipped the script, inserting themselves into the scriptures where they are not. Where they are, Leviticus shows it right after: “Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you”, and “they shall be your bondmen for ever”. They were originally our possession, but we sinned against our God and became their possession. Don’t worry: it is going to go back to the way it is supposed to be.

When we read precept upon precept, in the context of the scriptures, we see how we have been lied to as a people. Paul asks: “Who art thou that judgest another man’s servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth.”

Who are you to judge another man’s servant? To his own master he stands or falls. So our real master is Christ. That is the “Master in heaven” of Colossians 4:1, the one both servants and masters answer to.

And the servant is not left alone: “Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand.” There it is. For God is able to make him stand.

“But Pharaoh shall not hearken unto you, that I may lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth mine armies, and my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.” Mine armies. We have been marching since Egypt, and we marched around the walls of Jericho.

Israel came out of Egypt as the armies of the Lord, by great judgments on the ones who held them. That is why our marching troubles our oppressors.

“Thou didst strike through with his staves the head of his villages: they came out as a whirlwind to scatter me”. When Christ returns, these same people who had us in slavery, and have us in slavery, are going to try to fight against Christ.

“their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly.” These same slave owners rejoice to devour the poor, and they do it secretly. Even though slavery supposedly ended with the emancipation proclamation in 1863, then what? You had the school to prison pipeline. Redlining. Sundown towns. Sharecropping. Look at us now, and why? Because he is setting up all these traps. That is why he is still oppressing us to this day, and that is the “yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” But Tatum cannot see that.

Habakkuk said their rejoicing is “to devour the poor secretly.” Who are the poor? “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

The poor of his people. We are the poor that they are devouring secretly. The poor are Israel, and it is Zion that the Lord founded for them to trust in.

Tatum blames the murders, the violent crime and the abortions in the inner cities on our people alone. But who legalized abortion? The white people. Either the cultic ministries are right or Jesus is right; somebody is wrong. It’s you, Pam.

“But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

“and in the time of their trouble, when they cried unto thee, thou heardest them from heaven”. That is what is happening now. The Lord is starting to hear our cry. We are supposed to pray unto the Lord until he brings vengeance; that is what the Bible tells us to do.

“and according to thy manifold mercies thou gavest them saviours, who saved them out of the hand of their enemies.” How is that happening? By the purple and gold going to this city and that city, this country and that country, teaching the word of God. These are the saviours, and the saviours showed up in Ocean Springs, Mississippi.

So when we see these things happen to our people, yes, we are going to be there, and no, we are not going to stop. We don’t care if we have coons among our own people; we are going to rise up and save the day, because that is how God ordained it. Tatum is mad about it. Get mad. You hate your people and you hate your God.

They do not like when we stand up on our feet with confidence as the nation of Israel, not as blacks, but as the nation of Israel.

“And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.”

Great fear falls on them when they see us rise up as the children of God, as the army of the living God. That is what the man in Cicero feared when he said he could not stand the ones who march, and it is what puts fear in our oppressors when the brothers show up in a town like Ocean Springs. The yoke of iron destroyed us, but the Spirit of life from God stands us back on our feet.

The holy city “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel”.

Praises to the Most High for that. The kingdom is only for God’s people. The gates of the city carry the names of the twelve tribes, and no other nation’s name is written there.

That settles what Pam called heresy. Christ was not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and the city he brings has twelve gates for the twelve tribes. The same people the Lord sent into bondage with a yoke of iron upon their neck are the people whose names are on the gates.

Isaiah said the wicked shall see and be ashamed for their envy at the people. Who are those people? God's chosen people. Ezra says it: “The heathen shall envy thee, but they shall be able to do nothing against thee, saith the Lord.”

The heathen shall envy the Israelites. But they shall be able to do nothing. They can't stop it, because they ain't going to be in rulership any more. They are not going to have ownership any more.

That is the end of the man who ruleth over another to his own hurt: the time of his rule runs out, and all his envy cannot stop what the Lord has spoken for Israel.

“Let favour be shewed to the wicked, yet will he not learn righteousness”. If favour was shown to Esau, he still wouldn't change his wicked ways. It does not pay to be wicked.

“in the land of uprightness will he deal unjustly, and will not behold the majesty of the Lord.” Where is the land of uprightness? The land of Israel. And what did he do there? He stole it. Lord, thou wilt ordain peace for us”, like we read earlier in Ephesians 2: he is going to ordain peace for us and destruction for our enemies.

In all our affliction he was afflicted. So when he comes back, he is going to feel all of that pain and all of that suffering they did to the children of Israel, and he is going to wreak havoc on these nations.

“the angel of his presence saved them”. Salvation is not for the oppressors. Salvation is for those who have been afflicted. The man that ruled over another did it to his own hurt, because the one he afflicted is the one the Lord saves.

Sirach said vengeance, as a lion, shall lie in wait for the proud. Jeremiah shows the lion: “The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way; he is gone forth from his place to make thy land desolate; and thy cities shall be laid waste, without an inhabitant.”

The destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way, to make the land desolate, without an inhabitant.

And that is twofold. It is talking about Nebuchadnezzar, and it is talking about Christ. The lion that came up against the land in the days of Jeremiah is a picture of the Lion that is coming for the nations that ruled over Israel to their own hurt.

Who are the proud that digged the pits? “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?”

And who is he speaking to? Verse 1: “The vision of Obadiah. Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom”. Concerning Edom: Esau, your friendly neighborhood white man, your Europeans, and the Americans.

When you have forsaken the way, being corrected is grievous to you. You keep having to be told the same thing over and over, and the one who doesn't want to hear it gets pissed off; he doesn't want to hear it no more. That was Solomon, the old and foolish king who would no more be admonished.

Moses said it: “I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. The Most High scattered us and made our remembrance cease. That goes with Deuteronomy 28:64, where we are scattered and serve gods of wood and stone. When we were serving gods of wood and stone, we were spotted.

So James is writing to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, ones that were living as sinners. Count it joy when God starts showing you who you are. To live an unspotted life, we have to learn what we were doing wrong so we can fix it. So why are you mad? That is the whole purpose. God sends teachers to show us how to get right; we get cleansed because we are swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath.

And once we are unspotted, we go out and help others the same way: to visit “the fatherless and widows in their affliction”, the ones with no guide, no hedge, nobody to lead them, so they can become unspotted too. The scattered, forgotten tribes are the firstfruits God begat with the word of truth, and the good and perfect gift from above is the wisdom that makes us clean again.

“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God.” How do we ask of God? Do you think wisdom just floats down from heaven? No. You have to study; you have to open the book. And how do you know unless you have a teacher? Somebody has to teach you. As you grow in understanding you realize, like Paul, an expert in the law, that you had not known sin but by the law: I didn't know this was covetousness. Now you know what you have to fix in you.

Ecclesiasticus shows the man who asked: “When I was yet young, or ever I went abroad, I desired wisdom openly in my prayer. I prayed for her before the temple, and will seek her out even to the end.” He seeks wisdom to the end because wisdom will direct your path. “For thou savedst me from destruction, and deliveredst me from the evil time: therefore will I give thanks, and praise thee”: I will thank you because you will deliver me from that evil path.

“I directed my soul unto her, and I found her in pureness.” I redirected what I was doing and directed my soul to wisdom, because wisdom in its pureness will direct my path and save me. You want to be tethered to wisdom because with wisdom you avoid the punishment. That's what we all want: to get ourselves right, to be a better servant, a better husband, a better father. Teach me, God. Well, somebody has to teach you.

“I have had my heart joined with her from the beginning, therefore shall I not be forsaken. My heart was troubled in seeking her: therefore have I gotten a good possession.” As you seek her, you start realizing all the issues you have, and the severity of what God is talking about: eternal damnation, some learning it after death by pain. I can't get past this porn, I can't get past lying. At first it sounds good: I put on fringes, we keep the feast days, we turn up. But now I'm learning, damn, I'm a hateful ass brother, I'm a murmurer, I'm a backbiter. My heart is troubled.

Then: “Draw near unto me, ye unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.” You come to the house of learning, and somebody is going to teach you how to direct yourself. So now they're teaching you, and now you're mad? Do we understand what we signed up for? You said you wanted wisdom; here it is. No, you don't really want wisdom. You want church.

If any man lack wisdom, let him ask of God: you pray, you ask of God, then you go to a house of learning and you learn. And what are you asking for? “Search me, O God, and know my heart”: know what I think, how I process your information. “try me, and know my thoughts”: I'm asking God to measure me against his word.

“And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.” Tell me, Lord, if there's any wicked way in me, and lead me in the right way. That's what we are all asking God to do: show us. So when you ask God for wisdom and he starts showing you your errors, that is the prayer being answered.

That's why James says, “My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations.” You count it joy because you asked, show me all my wicked ways so I can fix them. “But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” You ask God to show you, the scripture comes correcting you, and now you're wavering. What are you doing when you waver? Trying to dodge correction.

So when it comes, take your medicine like a big boy and move on like a big girl. It's not the sin a person commits so much as what they do afterwards that shows who they are, because none of us is right. Do they take their medicine, the scriptures? Big talk, and as soon as correction comes, they ghost and make excuses. Blessed is the man that endures it: just listen, learn, and live.

James 4:1 asks, “From whence come wars and fightings among you?” When you are told something you are doing wrong and something in you is adverse to correction, right is coming in and wrong is warring against it. Captains who have sat in counsel know the look: you tell somebody they don't listen, and they squint like they are confused and repeat back what you just said. It ain't their sight that went bad. It is the battle in the mind, manifesting in the face.

James shows where that confusion comes from: “For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.” The word of God is pure; there is no variableness in it, and there should be no confusion in what is being said. If you were sincere, you would say, show me the lie, help me understand, maybe I am in error. Instead you are confused, because you are warring with what is right and don't want to accept it. You have strife in your heart.

“This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish.” It is deceiving you, the same deceiving we read in chapter one.

Then you wonder why good things are withheld from you and why you can't move forward. You are a liar, a thief, a murderer, an adulterer, it is being identified to you, and you cannot reason with yourself. You are struggling with yourself, and that is the war in your members.

When a brother starts to correct you and you don't like it, what do brothers start doing? They get mad, they pull away, they hold a grudge, and then they start speaking evil of the ones who corrected them. James says: “Speak not evil one of another, brethren.”

What are you supposed to do instead? “Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord.” You are supposed to humble yourself in the sight of the Lord, because you know to do good, but you don't want to do it.

That is the war and the fighting of James 4:1, coming out of the lusts that war in your members. The correction comes in, the wrong inside wars against it, and instead of humbling yourself, the war turns outward into speaking evil of your brother. The one who humbles himself stops the war where it starts.

“Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.” You know that what is being said is right, but you don't want to do it, because you are struggling. What is sin for you? Your sin is what you are struggling with. That is where the war is: you don't want to accept the prophet telling you.

That is all the people in the streets right now. You tell them what they are doing wrong and they are ready to kill you; they want to fight you for teaching the Bible. What's wrong with you? You hate to hear it because it convicts you. It is letting you know your life is in shambles, that you are evil, that you are the devil.

So the wars and fightings of James 4:1 come from knowing to do good and not doing it. The lust you are holding on to wars against the good you already know.

Part of deceiving yourself is justifying yourself. “If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me”. You are condemning yourself. The word of God, which comes from the teachers, is supposed to cleanse you, and the margin gives justify as cleanse, or clear self. So justifying yourself is deceiving yourself into thinking, I'm already cleansed, I'm already clear. Whatever the teachers have to say, the reproof and the instruction I'm receiving, I'm already clean.

When that happens, teachers, sometimes you have to let people suffer. Most people don't make the same mistake twice by accident; they choose, ignore the warnings, repeat the patterns, and expect someone else to absorb the consequences. Rescue delays the learning, and growth delayed by rescue is growth denied. David said it was good that he was afflicted. We can't carry everybody.

But teachers and instructors cannot weaponize the scriptures either, using them to correct everybody else and never our own lives. Then you are the brother that is wise and teacheth many, yet is unprofitable to himself, holding brothers to a higher accountability than you are willing to hold yourself, expecting perfection while you have hidden sins. The justified self is the one the mouth condemns, whether it is the one being corrected or the one correcting.

God said, “Behold, I send my messenger before thy face”: John, sent to teach the people and get them right to prepare for Christ. That is the job of the prophet, the apostle and every teacher: to show you. Then Christ called Simon and Andrew, James and John, from their nets. These men came in to get right, and do you think that walking with him he was not showing them all their errors? Luke shows him doing it with Peter.

“And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.” When you get right, then go strengthen your brethren. Christ is showing Peter he still has things to work on. You want to walk with me? I'm going to show you what your problems are.

Peter answered, “Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death.” And Christ said, “I tell thee, Peter”, didn't you just hear what I said to you? “the cock shall not crow this day, before that thou shalt thrice deny that thou knowest me.” Peter, you ain't there yet. Your mind ain't right yet. Get converted first.

Peter did become the head of the church afterwards, but first there were things he had to reconcile within himself. God opens his book and we behold ourselves in it; he sends prophets to show us how to get right. The worst thing to do is deny it. It don't feel good when you're going through it, but it's good for you. Medicine hurts sometimes, but if you are sincere you take your medicine and you get better. If you don't, you become an example of what not to do.

And those who teach must turn it on themselves too: don't weaponize the scriptures to correct everybody else while you can't see your own flaws, or hold brothers to a perfection you yourself are far from.

“O my God, I trust in thee: let me not be ashamed, let not mine enemies triumph over me.” Then: “Lead me in thy truth, and teach me: for thou art the God of my salvation; on thee do I wait all the day.” Look at what David is asking for: lead me and teach me.

Isaiah shows how God answers that: “Thus saith the Lord, thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel; I am the Lord thy God which teacheth thee to profit, which leadeth thee by the way that thou shouldest go.” He leads you by the way, in the direction you should go.

And God leads through the prophets he sends, and many of them were killed. People hate the word of God so much that they want to kill us. That's why it says be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath. The brothers go out to teach and get guns pulled on them, just for reading the Bible, while dudes drive by selling crack, fentanyl, whatever they sell. Guns pulled on us by Christian folk. That's why the church can't be stood: church is full of crap.

So are we the enemies because we tell the people the truth? No. You're just simple and you don't want correction. We are going to do our job and teach you the good and the right way, and keep our hands clean. What you do with it is on you. Either repent, or die in your sins.

The wicked of Psalms 50 hates instruction and casts God's words behind him, and “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.” Sirach shows the right way to deal with a brother or friend: “Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more.”

“Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again. Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.”

So why do we sit and speak against our brother? Because sometimes a brother admonishes you, and now you are angry behind it. Why are you mad? Why is it bothering you? Admonishing is what a friend is supposed to do. The one who hates instruction turns the admonishment around and slanders the brother who gave it.

God says to that man, “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee”. Just because he didn't do anything right away, don't think you are going to get away with it.

Why is a friend's admonishment the same matter as speaking against your brother? Because friend and brother are synonymous. Proverbs explains it: “A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.”

There are some friends that are closer than a brother. So when Psalms 50:20 says “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son”, the slander lands on the friend who admonished you as much as on your own blood.

A man that has friends must show himself friendly, not turn on the friend who corrects him. And God will not keep silence forever: “Now consider this, ye that forget God, lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver.” That is Israel, because the other nations never knew God to forget him. “and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God”, and the salvation is only to Israel.

“The belly devoureth all meats, yet is one meat better than another.” Why is one meat better than another? Because you can taste it. You have a palate, and you can say, I like this one better than that one.

“As the palate tasteth divers kinds of venison: so doth an heart of understanding false speeches.” The same way your palate can taste which meat is better, a heart of understanding can discern false speech. You listen to somebody and you know: this is BS. It happened recently, around Passover, talking to a brother: listening for a while, it didn't add up, it started to sound like murmuring. You would have been better off keeping quiet, but being that you want to talk, go ahead and embarrass yourself.

That is what Wisdom of Solomon 7 is describing. Wisdom is “Kind to man, steadfast, sure, free from care, having all power, overseeing all things, and going through all understanding, pure, and most subtil, spirits.” If those are the attributes of wisdom, you want to be tethered to wisdom, so you can discern and understand why people do the things they do: the defense mechanism, the gaslighting, the one in error trying to tug on your heart and make you feel guilty so you will chase him. That's not how this goes. He is supposed to wear down the footsteps.

Wisdom “is the breath of the power of God.” The power of God is the word of God, and the word of God is wisdom. They're all synonymous; they all mean the same thing. The word of God is this book, and the word of God is Christ. It is one pureness, one avenue, with no variableness in what it means. That is why the Christian church has destroyed the minds of a people, making them believe you can separate Christ from the commandments. He is the word. You can't believe on Christ and not keep the commandments, and you can't keep the commandments and not believe on Christ. It's an oxymoron. Yet the witchcraft called Christianity has separated them to the point that it has been said that if you keep the commandments, you're sinning. Your church made you dumb as hell.

“For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.” Quick means alive. This word is alive; it's not like a textbook. It will affect you to the deepest part of your thought process. It cuts, until you feel sick to your stomach, an emptiness like hunger. If you have never felt that cut in class, examine yourself.

“Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.” If you are tethered to Christ, you have to be tethered to wisdom, and if you are tethered to Christ and to wisdom, you know BS when you hear it. You know the intention of the heart of a person when they speak. You hear the pity party you've heard a thousand times before. You tell a man, stop talking, and he keeps talking, explaining, digging the ditch deeper, thinking he's making sense and embarrassing himself. A spiritual man discerneth all things. We could be wrong, we're not 100% with everything, we're learning ourselves; but for the most part, tethered to wisdom, you understand false speech.

Converting comes through trial, error and correction, and you're supposed to be happy about the correction. “Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness”: when that person is telling you what you're doing wrong, it's a kindness that he does it. “and let him reprove me; it shall be an excellent oil”: it's going to be a blessing.

“which shall not break my head.” It isn't going to kill you. Somebody telling you that you are doing evil is not going to kill you. It's supposed to kill the old man in you, not you physically. And people don't want to hear that; they don't want to know the errors of their ways.

When you come to this truth, prepare your soul for temptations, for trials, for tribulation. People come in with rose-colored glasses, thinking everything's going to be perfect. No: it's going to start unmasking who you are, who I am, and what we have to fix to get right. It's sweet until you start dealing with who you really are. That is the wisdom that leadeth and directeth the wise, as Solomon says: God directs you away from evil and shows you how to avoid it, and his reproof is how he does it.

Wisdom is “a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.” That is the breath that was breathed into us in Genesis 2; it was wisdom, so that we should know better. And what is pure? “The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.” It will enlighten your spiritual eye to see things clearly, to understand false speech, to know when you're going in the wrong direction. It's supposed to light your path.

“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” “The fear of the Lord is clean, enduring for ever: the judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether. More to be desired are they than gold, yea, than much fine gold: sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb.” It is sweet, but then it gets bitter, because now you start to learn about yourself. That's all right, because the law of God converts the soul. It's only a problem when your soul isn't getting converted.

“Moreover by them is thy servant warned: and in keeping of them there is great reward.” The Lord does not ask us to keep the laws with nothing in return; he is a just and fair God. And converting doesn't just happen; you don't close your eyes and wake up different. It comes through trial, error and correction.

“Who can understand his errors? cleanse thou me from secret faults”: things people don't know I'm dealing with. Sometimes a class comes out talking right about you. You said you wanted wisdom. And if it comes in English and you speak Spanish, don't worry: “There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.” We'll translate it, even into sign language. If it's for you, you'll get it. But you need to be cleansed.

“Keep back thy servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me.” This is a prayer we ask God for, and then he sends the prophets to tell you. So why are you upset? Don't ask for rain and get mad when it's muddy. You asked God to cleanse you; he has to show you what needs to be cleansed. The first key is listening. The greatest gift a young person can have is to listen: be neutral, hear what's being said, examine yourself whether it's true, and if it is, fix it. Stop lying to yourself.

“then shall I be upright, and I shall be innocent from the great transgression. Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O Lord, my strength, and my redeemer.” If you want your words and your thoughts to be acceptable, open this book, learn what the will of God is, and when the word comes to you, accept it for what it says.

“Then beware lest thou forget the Lord, which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.”

That's why you do it: why you teach the laws diligently to the children, talk of them in the house and by the way, and sing the psalms and spiritual songs over and over. The repetition keeps the house from forgetting the Lord who brought us out of the house of bondage.

Now if you forget the Lord, guess what? You're going to be tempted. Forgetting the Lord leaves the armour off, and the wiles of the devil find a way in. Remembering him is how the family puts on the whole armour of God and stands.

“Ye shall not tempt the Lord your God, as ye tempted him in Massah. Ye shall diligently keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and his testimonies, and his statutes, which he hath commanded thee.”

Well, how don't you tempt him? Teach them diligently. Husband in order, wife in order, redeeming the time. Diligently keeping the commandments, testimonies and statutes: that's how you do it, by instructing them.

So all these scriptures go together. Do half of them and you have only pieces of the armour. Do them all, in the house, with the children, and the family has put on the whole armour of God, “that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.”

“And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children”. Teach them what? The laws of God. “and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.”

It is a routine of the word. It's repetition: sitting in the house, walking by the way, lying down, rising up. Children are not mature enough to make that cognitive decision on their own; the parent has to put the law in them diligently, over and over.

That is how the children put on the whole armour of God. The husband in order, the wife in order, the time redeemed, and the laws taught diligently at every part of the day, so the house can “stand against the wiles of the devil.”

“See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.”

This is another piece of the whole armour. If you are not redeeming the time because the days are evil, you are not going to teach your children to learn how to fear God. Walking circumspectly, not as fools but as wise, is how a parent sets the example the children follow.

The days are evil: the social media zaps our young out, and Esau sets it up so they can be taken for sweat equity. Redeeming the time means using it for the Lord and for teaching the house, so the family can put on the whole armour of God and “stand against the wiles of the devil.”

“Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord”.

Over and over you sing these songs, you read these words. It's repetition, the same routine of the word Moses commanded when he said to teach the laws diligently in the house, by the way, lying down and rising up. It is there to mold the children's minds concerning the laws of God.

The world molds them with its music and its social media; the psalms, hymns and spiritual songs mold them with the law. That repetition in the house is part of putting on the whole armour of God, so they can “stand against the wiles of the devil.”

“Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body.”

The whole armour of God is not put on in pieces. If we want to strengthen our families: one, the husband in order; the wife in order; and the children will learn how to obey the Lord by your behavior. The husband is the head as Christ is the head, and the wife submits as unto the Lord.

If the husband and wife are not in order, you can't expect the children to be in order. So the order of the house, the husband as head and the wife submitting, is part of the armour that lets the family “stand against the wiles of the devil.”

“Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;) That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth.” “And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.”

These scriptures are put together with “Put on the whole armour of God” for a reason. If you do half of these things, you are not putting on the whole armour of God; you are putting on pieces. It begins at home. Husbands in order, wives in order; if they are not in order, you can't expect the children to be in order.

Children learn how to obey the Lord by the behavior of their parents, and in turn they are putting on the whole armour of God. The father brings them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord, and that is how a family stands against the wiles of the devil.

Isaiah says, “As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them.” These same kids become the neighborhood oppressors, running around with Glocks and taped-up mags and all that foolishness, and there is no man anywhere in the picture: no man with authority, no dignity, no order, no structure. Ecclesiasticus gives the charge that was missing: “Give him no liberty in his youth, and wink not at his follies.”

You have to hold those children in. You have to take that by the reins, because you are the one who is going to form their thoughts, their shape and their identity. Don’t give them liberty in their youth, and don’t wink at their follies.

Look at what happens when that is not done. They wanted to kill Julio Foolio over a rap battle: young, dumb, stupid people, wise to do evil. They used a girl’s phone to track him, bought AR-15 type weapons with brass catchers so the shells would not be left at the scene, and shot up his birthday party at a hotel. They thought they got away, but the police got every camera, the house cameras, the phone records, the tag readers and the Flock cameras, and the investigators took their time and put the pieces together. Lock, seal, smack, boom, you’re going down. Your ass is in jail and your mind is still a child. When the enticement wears off, reality seeps back in, and it usually comes with the arrest.

We have children in our nation too, some disrespectful to their parents, some who won’t listen. You don’t know what your parents are trying to save you from, and once you learn it, it may be too late to turn around. That behavior is not normal, not for our people, the royalty, and not period. And the eighth head knows this. They don’t care if it touches some of theirs; that is collateral damage. Their elite make sure their own children get the lessons they need to not fall into it. We are the only ones who eat this stuff up.

The Lord told Ezekiel, “set thy face against mount Seir, and prophesy against it.” Who or what is mount Seir? Genesis 36 answers: “Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.” Esau's dwelling is Seir, so when the Bible prophesies against Seir, it is prophesying against Esau, the nation of Edom. Now there is context, and no one can say we are making it up. We don't need a cosigner; the Bible says what it says.

With that key, Ezekiel 35 opens up. “Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred”: a hatred that has gone on for centuries, from Esau their father to his children toward us. It is in their blood to hate us; their hatred is damn near biological, from the womb to the tomb. That is why they do such terrible things to us: eating us, hanging us, castrating us, raping us, mutilating us. A sister whose husband was murdered sought justice in court; they hung her from a tree, shot her full of holes, cut the unborn baby out of her, stepped on its head and set it on fire. Damn! That is a perfect hatred. There's no record of black folks ever doing that to white folks. What we did to the French in Haiti was retaliation, and they deserved it; she was innocent.

They shed our blood “in the time that their iniquity had an end”: after the Emancipation Proclamation came the KKK, Black Codes, Jim Crow, convict leasing and redlining. That envy goes back to the birthright. Esau was the firstborn and felt it was not fair that God chose Jacob, and the Lord says he will do “according to thine anger, and according to thine envy.”

Edom said, “These two nations and these two countries shall be mine, and we will possess it.” The two nations are Judah and Israel; the two countries were Judea and Samaria and later Israel and the Americas. They took one as Romans and later as Israelis, and the other as Christians, as conquistadors. “I have heard all thy blasphemies”: this is a direct precept to Revelation 2:9 and 3:9, the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews and are not, possessing the land and professing to be the people that belong there. They have said it to our faces: yes, you are the real Jews, but the land is ours now. They know; the world does not.

“When the whole earth rejoiceth, I will make thee desolate.” As long as that nation is on the earth, there can be no peace; when there is no more Edom, the earth rejoices. “thou shalt be desolate, O mount Seir, and all Idumea, even all of it.” The judgment on Edom is complete, with no exceptions, and they shall know that he is the Lord.

Isaiah says the terrible one, Edom, is brought to nought: the one that does terrible things to the nations behind the cloak, behind the scenes, to maintain power and authority on the earth, destroyed as Ezekiel 35 said. The scorner is consumed, and all that watch for iniquity are cut off, those “That make a man an offender for a word, and lay a snare for him that reproveth in the gate.” Who is the one that reproveth in the gate? Amos answers: “They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly.”

They hate him that rebukes in the gate, in the streets. They abhor him that speaks uprightly. That is the one teaching in the streets, and that is who they lay the snares for, in the legal system, in their music and their media.

So they will pass laws to make those of us who reprove offenders for our words. Say certain things and you face jail time, imprisonment, exile, banishment; they are even trying to pass laws where you can be put to death, talking about bringing back beheadings and the guillotine. They will call it hate speech, terrorism, treason, being unpatriotic. You are anti-MAGA, against abortion, against same-sex, against white supremacy? Lock that brother up, lock that sister up. You say you are an Israelite, that they are fake Jews? Hate speech; five years; fire them from their job; fine them thousands; put a lien on their house.

They will do it because they can, and they will. But the most frightening one to them is the one they cannot kill, the righteous one they cannot pay off, bribe, drug, slander, poison or shoot. And Isaiah’s end is sure: the terrible one is brought to nought, and all that lay snares for him that reproveth in the gate are cut off.

The man of God out of Judah was charged by the word of the Lord, “Eat no bread, nor drink water, nor turn again by the same way that thou camest.” The Lord told him what not to do and what to do. He refused the king, even for half his house. Then an old prophet in Bethel came after him: “I am a prophet also as thou art; and an angel spake unto me by the word of the Lord, saying, Bring him back with thee into thine house, that he may eat bread and drink water. But he lied unto him.”

This dude was lying. God said the only one he speaks with mouth to mouth is Moses; everybody else he speaks to with dreams and visions, and this man said an angel came to him. The man of God went back, ate and drank, and “a lion met him by the way, and slew him”: “It is the man of God, who was disobedient unto the word of the Lord”.

That is why the Lord said, “Take ye heed every one of his neighbour, and trust ye not in any brother: for every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders.” That is why you have to be mindful with brothers.
