Some people are in your life for blessings, some are in your life for cursings; but ultimately it is to try us, each and every one of us.

“Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently.” Unfeigned: don't be fake, don't be phony.

Some brothers can fake it real good. If a sister asks us, what about this brother, we can only tell her what you show us. Is he really like that? She's got to talk to him more in depth, more personally, to find out how he truly is.

That is why the love of the brethren has to be unfeigned, out of a pure heart. Only you and God know whether you are walking feignedly; we only see what you show us.

Feign is a verb that means to pretend, to fake, to give a false show of something. It includes pretending an illness: a lot of sisters get Sabbath sick. It includes faking an emotion, or making up an excuse. Remember the brother who used to go around teaching fake it till you make it? Don't raise that man up; he isn't right. To feign means to pretend: you are a fake brother, you are pretending.

Paul sets the opposite: “Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned.” Unfeigned faith: not feigned, not folly.

The whole end of the commandment is charity from a pure heart and a faith that is not pretended. That is the walk Ezra asks God to remember, and the feigned walk is the one he asks God to think not upon.

“Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him.” That was the guy who put the talent in the napkin: he drew back.

As we're doing the restructuring, certain captains get asked, why did you move this brother from this position to that position? Oh, he's not the same any more. When he came in, he was on fire; we didn't have to tell him what to do. Now you've got to yell at him, you've got to force him. So drop him down and move him to the side, like we read in 1 Corinthians 6 today.

The Lord has no pleasure in the one who draws back. That is walking feignedly before him, and Ezra asks God to think not upon those, but to remember them that according to his will have known his fear.

“Think not upon those that have walked feignedly before thee.” To feign means to pretend, to fake, to give a false show of something. And Luke shows feigning in action: “And they watched him, and sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words.” They pretended to be just men so they could catch Christ in his words.

During the time of Christ there were a lot of fake brothers among them, so we expect that to be true today. There is going to be an explosion, a spiritual explosion, an influx of believers, especially from the Christian church: 3,000 one day, 5,000 another day. It's going to happen, because the scriptures say it.

But we have to be mindful: there will be feigned people among them. Ezra asks God not to think upon those, “but remember them, which according to thy will have known thy fear.”

“And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?” When those scriptures come out, your heart is supposed to be burning for this.

How do I get this word out? What ideas do I have? I want to give my time to this truth; everything else outside of this doesn't matter. If your heart is not burning with the word of God, if you don't have the desire to learn, to teach, to better yourself, to better the nation of Israel, you are going to fade away. You're a hireling.

You could be in 5 years, 10 years, 20 years, but this word is supposed to make your heart burn to get it out. The hireling walks feignedly; the one whose heart burns is the one who has known God's fear.

“And Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.” That's a hireling: he put his hand to the work and then looked back. Some of y'all are sitting here right now. There is a God; remember that.

This is where you self-examine. Am I being a phony, a hypocrite among the brethren? Am I walking feignedly? Only you can answer that. You and God know the answer; we don't.

Ezra prays that God would think not upon those that walked feignedly, but remember them that have known his fear. The one who looks back from the plough is not fit for the kingdom.

Against the hireling who puts his hand to the plough and looks back, and the man who draws back, stands Israel's confession: “Our heart is not turned back, neither have our steps declined from thy way.” That's how you've got to be. That's how we have to be.

The heart that does not turn back and the steps that do not decline are what it means to walk before God unfeignedly. Those are the ones Ezra asks God to remember: “remember them, which according to thy will have known thy fear.”

So examine yourself. Has your heart turned back? Have your steps declined from his way since you first came in on fire? You and God know the answer.

“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another.” That is the unfeigned love of the brethren, real and not put on.

“Not slothful in business”: not lazy concerning God's work. “fervent in spirit”: be on fire in your spirit. “serving the Lord.”

This is the opposite of walking feignedly. The feigned brother came in on fire and now has to be yelled at and forced; the hireling looked back from the plough. The one Ezra asks God to remember, one “which according to thy will have known thy fear”, is kindly affectioned to the brethren, not slothful in God's business, and on fire in spirit, serving the Lord.

Who are the elect the angels gather in Matthew 24? Isaiah answers: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name.” Israel is God's elect.

So there's no contradiction between the New Testament and the Old Testament. Christ was sent to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, the angels gather the elect, and the elect is Israel. Ezekiel's sheep, Matthew's elect and Isaiah's elect are the same people.

The contradiction comes from these false pastors, these hireling pastors, who tell the people it is everybody. The Lord said: “I will seek that which was lost, and bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken, and will strengthen that which was sick.” That's our people: we were broken, we're the sick ones. “but I will destroy the fat and the strong”: he is going to destroy the nations. “I will feed them with judgment.”

“For thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I, even I, will both search my sheep, and seek them out.” Who is that I? Christ. And Christ said who he came for: “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

That is what Christ was doing, seeking out the lost sheep of Israel, and that is what Paul and the apostles were doing after him. That was the great commission in Matthew 28:19.

So when Ezekiel says “I will seek that which was lost”, that's our people. The lost sheep Christ was sent to are the same sheep God promised to search out and deliver “out of all places where they have been scattered in the cloudy and dark day”: all places, countries and lands.

“And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” These are the angels of Psalms 50, called from the heavens to gather.

Did he say gather everybody, all people? No. They gather his elect, and his elect are Israel. It's the same gathering Ezekiel spoke of: “so will I seek out my sheep, and will deliver them out of all places where they have been scattered in the cloudy and dark day.” The four winds are all the places, countries and lands where our people were scattered.

The prophets gather on the earth, the angels gather from the heavens, and it is the elect, the sheep of the house of Israel, who are gathered.

“Praise ye the Lord. Sing unto the Lord a new song, and his praise in the congregation of saints.” The saints are the twelve tribes God gathers.

“Let Israel rejoice in him that made him”: because we have not been rejoicing in our creator, we've been rejoicing in the white man. “let the children of Zion be joyful in their King”: for so long we've been joyful in the white man.

“For the Lord taketh pleasure in his people: he will beautify the meek with salvation.” He doesn't take pleasure in all races on the planet, only in his people.

“Let the saints be joyful in glory: let them sing aloud upon their beds.” That's the rest right there. It is what Ezekiel promised the gathered sheep: “there shall they lie in a good fold, and in a fat pasture shall they feed upon the mountains of Israel. I will feed my flock, and I will cause them to lie down, saith the Lord God.”

Ezekiel says God will search his sheep and gather them from the countries. Who does the gathering? “He shall call to the heavens from above, and to the earth, that he may judge his people.” He calls to the heavens from above: those are the angels he's calling to. And to the earth: the earth are the prophets, you and me on the earth.

“Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” Those are the twelve tribes of Israel. So he's telling the prophets, gather the twelve tribes, and he's telling the angels, gather the twelve tribes.

That is the promise of Ezekiel 34: “I will bring them out from the people, and gather them from the countries, and will bring them to their own land, and feed them upon the mountains of Israel.” The good pasture is the kingdom.

“Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith the Lord.” Jeremiah 23 really talks about the essence of hirelings. How do they scatter the sheep? In Christianity they scatter them into the Baptist church, the Catholic church, the holiness church, whatever denomination. We are being divided rather than united as the twelve tribes of Israel. Even in the time of Christ there were the Sadducees, the Pharisees, the Stoics, the Epicureans and the Herodians; we were being scattered then, and it's happening today.

Moses said where it would lead: “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.” Under these wood gods, like Christianity with the old wooden cross, and the many denominations under Islam, our people are scattered everywhere in those false religions, even in Judaism.

Remember, this is about Israelites; it is not so much talking about Esau. “Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away”: driven them away from the truth that they are the Israelites of the twelve tribes. But the Lord says “I will gather the remnant of my flock out of all countries whither I have driven them”.

Against the hirelings who scatter the flock, the Lord promises “I will set up shepherds over them which shall feed them: and they shall fear no more, nor be dismayed, neither shall they be lacking”. Jeremiah shows what they will feed us with: “And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding.”

Knowledge and understanding of what? God's laws. It isn't talking about feeding them with jumping up and down, screaming and foaming at the mouth.

Right now we are lacking as a race, as a people. We are lacking knowledge, wisdom and understanding; and when you break it down, we are lacking rulership, dominion of the earth, our own country, a fortified family, a nation. We are lacking everything. Pastors after God's heart, feeding us the laws, are the shepherds who end that lack.

“For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” The elder world was during the time of Adam. Ezra says “the righteous should inherit these things, but that the ungodly should perish. Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer strait things, and hope for wide”. Strait things is tribulation.

“They say still unto them that despise me, The Lord hath said, Ye shall have peace”. They are speaking to people who really hate God. At the sit down, the man with the hat kept saying that when tribulation comes, we're not going to be here; the church won't be here. Christians just lie and tell you there's going to be peace.

But Paul and Barnabas were “Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.” The only way we're entering the kingdom of God is through much tribulation. So what Bible are these Christians reading?

That is why Jeremiah says “Hearken not unto the words of the prophets that prophesy unto you: they make you vain: they speak a vision of their own heart, and not out of the mouth of the Lord.” A vision of their own heart is their own mind, what they feel at that moment: I don't know who this is for, but God has a message for you. It is not coming from the Bible, and the Bible says tribulation.

“And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you. And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men’s hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.”

In all the lands we were scattered, “if from thence thou shalt seek the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him, if thou seek him with all thy heart and with all thy soul”, meaning do everything God says to do. “When thou art in tribulation, and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days, if thou turn to the Lord thy God, and shalt be obedient unto his voice; (For the Lord thy God is a merciful God;) he will not forsake thee”.

We say we are Christians, we serve the same God, and the white man doesn't give a damn about that. “I have not sent these prophets, yet they ran: I have not spoken to them, yet they prophesied.” He did not send these pastors, these Christian reverends. Jeremiah says the Lord will lead “the seed of the house of Israel out of the north country, and from all countries whither I had driven them”. “for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the Lord”. We are not just in North America. That is why Jeremiah says “from all countries whither I had driven them”: the 12 tribes were scattered to every corner, and the gathering is from all of them.

“Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” Who is that? Judah. That is the “Judah shall be saved” of Jeremiah 23, where in the days of the righteous Branch, Christ, Judah is saved and Israel dwells safely; remember we were split into two kingdoms.

“for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.” Meaning we are his favorite. We are God's favorite. And the end of it is “they shall dwell in their own land”. The Lord who brought Israel out of Egypt will be known as the Lord who brought his favorite people out of the north country and set them in their own land.

“and thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.” The rust represents his wickedness. It's still there, kept still within his mouth, just as Job says.

“Set him not by thee, lest, when he hath overthrown thee, he stand up in thy place”. That is what happened historically. “Wherefore then gavest not thou my money into the bank, that at my coming I might have required mine own with usury?” This is the bank: the congregation. Usury means interest. So when Christ comes back, he wants interest on what he gave each of us.

Paul shows the great house: “But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The bank is his great house. Your work, your love, your zeal, your understanding: bring it into the bank, the congregation.

“Take from him the pound, and give it to him that hath ten pounds.” Imagine the order, like the king in Game of Thrones giving orders to the men next to the throne. You're the same grimy person you were five years back; there's no change in you, no transformation. It goes for men and women: the same gossiper, murmurer, complainer you were five years ago, just here with fringes and a border of blue. He taketh away means he takes you away and kills you.

“and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit.” You've got to be purged to bring forth more fruit. There are things in us that have to be cut: cut this off, cut that person off from you, cut this out of your soul and your spirit, so you can bear more fruit.

We've seen it. Brothers came among us with certain skills and did not expand on them, so the Most High, like musical chairs, moved them out of the way. “But his citizens hated him, and sent a message after him, saying, We will not have this man to reign over us.” Who hated him? Rejected is the word to highlight. The elders, the chief priests and the scribes rejected him: back then it was the scribes and Pharisees and those that followed them who said, we will not have this man to reign over us.

Today there are no groups called scribes and Pharisees, but the same spirit is here. They are the Christians, they are the Muslims; they fall into this. They reject his reign, and at the end of the parable the King says what becomes of them: “But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.”

“And another came, saying, Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin.” See that? Hirelings. I kept it laid up; I didn't do anything with the knowledge you bestowed on me, the faith you gave me.

“Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.” Many will say they prophesied and did many wonderful works in his name, “And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.” That goes back to this servant: he was in the truth, and he took his talent and hid it in a napkin. I'm not helping them any more; I did it full time, but I don't want to do it any more.

And the end of the parable: “But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.” Churches don't read that; they will look at it and say, no, we're not reading that in Sunday school. It means you are not just going to be able to do what you want to do. You were put on this earth to do what the Most High and Christ said, and if you don't do that, there's no reason for you to live. If you don't want to do what you were created for, bring him before me and end his existence.

“And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.” What are the pounds? God's word.

David says: “Therefore I love thy commandments above gold; yea, above fine gold.” The commandments are more precious than gold, so the money the nobleman hands his servants is his word: the knowledge, the understanding, the faith he bestowed on each of us.

Occupy till I come means do something with it until he returns. When he comes back he wants to know “how much every man had gained by trading”: how much each one went out and taught the word. The servant who laid his pound up in a napkin kept the word to himself, and that is how he is judged.

“Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.” That's what we all want: dominion. Revelation says the same: “And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers.”

We're not going to play with the nations. We've got to teach them to honor the King of kings. We've got to teach them the civil law, the ceremonial law, the dietary law, the moral law, and the history of Israel too. They are not going to be glorifying China any more, or the white man; they are going to glorify the history of Israel.

Just one city is too much to handle in this body and mind we have now. That's why it's exciting to read this: the Lord is going to have to change this. Some of you have problems dealing with that one black woman you've got right now, and you're talking about being lord over five cities. Being faithful in a very little now is what earns the authority then.

The nobleman gave the pounds “that he might know how much every man had gained by trading.” The trading is going out teaching the word. It is business: “Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord.”

This is talking about God's business. If it were the white man's business, you wouldn't be slothful, because you've got to eat, you've got to have a place to live. But in God's business people get slothful. Be fervent in spirit, on fire in spirit, serving the Lord.

The first servant's pound gained ten pounds and the second's gained five, and they were rewarded with cities. The servant who was slothful in the Lord's business laid his pound up in a napkin and gained nothing.

When he came, the people loved him so much that they wanted to “take him by force, to make him a king”, and “he departed again into a mountain himself alone.” By the prophets, there would be no more king until Christ returns: the sceptre waits for Shiloh.

In the Persian captivity there was Joshua the high priest, of the tribe of Levi, and Zerubbabel the governor, of the tribe of Judah. The Lord speaks to Joshua and his fellows, “for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.” The Branch is Christ, and Jeremiah 23 shows it.

“Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.” The righteous Branch raised unto David is Christ, the King who will reign and execute justice.

“In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.” That is the same day Zechariah speaks of. The stone laid before Joshua with its seven eyes, and those eyes are the angels. “I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day”: that is Christ dying on the cross. And “In that day”, every man shall call his neighbour “under the vine and under the fig tree”: that is in the kingdom, when Israel dwells safely under the Branch.

The Branch appears again in Zechariah 6: “Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the Lord.” That is not the second temple; it is about the third and the fourth.

“Even he shall build the temple of the Lord; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both.” Both is the priesthood and the kingship. He sits and rules on his throne as a king, and he is a priest on that same throne.

That is why Zechariah 3 speaks to Joshua the high priest, and why Zerubbabel the governor stands alongside him: the priest from Levi and the ruler from Judah. Christ fulfilled both offices, the priesthood and the kingship, in one man, the Branch.

Zechariah says Zerubbabel “shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it.” Who is the headstone? Christ. Why are they crying grace, grace? Isaiah shows it, and shows that Zerubbabel is in these last days as well: “In that day shall five cities in the land of Egypt speak the language of Canaan, and swear to the Lord of hosts; one shall be called, The city of destruction.”

The language of Canaan is the scriptures, and one city shall be destroyed. “In that day shall there be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar at the border thereof to the Lord.” An altar is for sacrifice, and this is talking about where the Israelites are: here in Babylon the great.

“And it shall be for a sign and for a witness unto the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt: for they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors, and he shall send them a saviour, and a great one, and he shall deliver them.” Who is that saviour? Christ.

So Zechariah is saying the same thing. The headstone is that saviour we just read about in Isaiah, and the crying of grace, grace is because of the oppressor. The great mountain, Babylon the great, becomes a plain before him, and he delivers his people out of the land where they cried.

Zechariah asks, “Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain”. Zerubbabel was in the Persian captivity, and Babylon was already destroyed by Persia. So who is this great mountain? Jeremiah shows where the mountain is: “And I will render unto Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldea all their evil that they have done in Zion in your sight, saith the Lord.”

Watch what he calls Babylon: “Behold, I am against thee, O destroying mountain, saith the Lord, which destroyest all the earth: and I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and roll thee down from the rocks, and will make thee a burnt mountain.” The great mountain is Babylon.

“And they shall not take of thee a stone for a corner, nor a stone for foundations; but thou shalt be desolate for ever, saith the Lord.” That lets you know it is not Iraq. Are people still living in Iraq today? Yes. This says “thou shalt be desolate for ever”, so it is not talking about ancient Babylon.

So the great mountain before Zerubbabel is Babylon to come: Babylon the great. Before him it becomes a plain, flattened and destroyed, and it is done “Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.” Everything we do must be according to the spirit of the Most High God; it has nothing to do with our physical powers and our skills.

Zerubbabel is the branch in the line of Christ: Matthew's genealogy runs from Zerubbabel through Abiud, Eliakim, Azor, Sadoc, Achim, Eliud, Eleazar, Matthan and Jacob to “Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” So when the Lord speaks to Zerubbabel, he is speaking to the father of Christ's line.

“Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.” Zerubbabel was of the king's bodyguard, one of the top fighters. The Lord is telling him, no, this has nothing to do with your fighting skills; we know you can break bones, but that's not what is going to overcome everything. The spirit of the Lord is what's going to do it.

“Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain.” The great mountain is Babylon the great, and it shall become a plain: flattened, destroyed. “and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it”: crying mercy, mercy unto it.

What is the headstone? “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.” Who is that? Christ. He is the headstone. Not only would Christ come from Zerubbabel's lineage; Zerubbabel shall bring forth the headstone.

“The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house; his hands shall also finish it.” His hands started the foundation of the temple, and he did finish the temple. But this goes deeper than that: because of verse 7, verses 6 through 9 are going into the last days as well, when the great mountain, Babylon the great, is brought down to a plain and the headstone, Christ, is brought forth.

“A wise son heareth his father’s instruction”. When you first come in as a brother, you are still attached to the life you are coming out of; somebody has to instruct you. Acts shows it. The eunuch “Was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet. Then the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot. And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest?”

We study and we get certain instructions, but is there a follow-up? When we give an instruction, do we follow up and ask, did you understand what I'm telling you to do? Or is it, boy, I said do it, do it, until the kid is intimidated and afraid to do it? Are we checking whether the person is actually ascertaining the instructions, or just repeating what they see and trying to make it?

Black people will buy something that has to be put together, dump all the pieces out, look at the picture on the box and put it together like that instead of reading the instructions. That is what we do with the scriptures. We read and study, but are we challenging ourselves on what we study? Are we asking the questions and going back to say, I'm reading this, but I don't understand any of it? And as leaders, are we giving the instructions to the people?

“And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me? And he desired Philip that he would come up and sit with him.” We all have to be guided in the instruction we are getting. You can't just tell a person to go do something. We are all instructed until it becomes habit, and that is how a son learns to hear his father's instruction instead of becoming the scorner who hears not rebuke.

“He that walketh with wise men shall be wise”: broaden your circle to wise men, men that keep the commandments, and you'll have righteous success. Speaking of that: “The blessing of the Lord, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it.” When the Lord blesses you, there is not going to be any sorrow with it. You are going to get gains.

Think of lifting weights. When you exercise, the muscles are being broken down; an acid releases in your body and breaks them down. But when it regroups, it builds more muscle and makes you look stronger, and when you look stronger you feel stronger and sit up a little more. Shout out to the Greensmen and the brothers that got necks: they were fat and their neck sat down in their shoulders, then they slimmed down and now you can see they've got a neck. People start praising you: bro, what are you doing? Something about you changed.

That is what being around wise men does. Everybody knew the men who walked with Christ: you sound like him, you talk like him, you've got a spirit about you that looks like Christ. It bigs you up and makes you feel and be somebody.

Evil success is different. Some kids think making money on OnlyFans or social media content is success; it's not, and it's nothing to glory in. It seems good and brings profit, so it is “abomination to fools to depart from evil”. That's why rappers and entertainers keep selling digital crack and the prostitute lifestyle to the community but not to their own kids. Evil success comes with sorrow; the blessing of the Lord adds none.
blog/2026/2026-08-08-2026-08-08-stay-in-:
“And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots: And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding.” Who is that stem coming out of Jesse? Christ. The spirit of the Lord rests upon Christ; the spirit of wisdom and understanding rests upon Christ. Paul says it plainly: “But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.”

Christ is the wisdom of God. And wisdom makes all things new. That is why 2 Corinthians 5:17 says, “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature”: any man in Christ is a new creature because the power and the wisdom of God makes all things new.

Isaiah shows what is contained in the Holy Spirit that rested on him: “the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord.” It made him “of quick understanding in the fear of the Lord”, the way King Solomon said he was a witty child, and the way John leaped in Elizabeth’s womb when Mary visited: there is a spirit in the womb.

Christ is also the power of God, and Isaiah shows that power too: “he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked.” And when you have that spirit, you will not judge after the sight of your eyes; “with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth.” Reproving with equity means you are not partial. With the spirit of the Lord you are not going to be in partiality; you will have knowledge and understanding, and you will obtain the wisdom, retain it and apply it.

“Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature.” Christ is the firstborn of every single creature, the first created. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him.”

By Christ were all things created in heaven and in earth. What is in heaven? All the angels, the host of heaven. Would Satan be a part of that? So who created those evil angels too? Christ did. So in the wilderness the creation is trying to tempt the creator. Think about that.

Satan knew that was the creator. But look at the time he came: “when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was afterward an hungred.” He came after the forty days of fasting, in a weakened state while in the flesh, and said, oh, I can surely tempt him; this is what he created me to do. Christ answered him with the word: “It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone.”

The same thing applies among brothers and sisters. There is a time when you are in a weak state, spiritually, or physically from surgery or pain, and Satan comes: nobody called to check on you, but here I am; they don't know you like I know you. You argue with your spouse and go for a drive, and guess who is in the passenger seat. He whispers memories you haven't thought of in years, like Cleopus Jenkins back in 73 with that Studebaker and the eight-track tape, and you think it is your own thought. He knows everything about you, from before you met your husband, because you were his employee.

If Satan tried to tempt his own creator, how much more is he going to tempt us? That is why we stay in the spirit and answer him the way Christ did.

“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul.” The law of God is perfect, it is pure, there is nothing wrong with it, and converting means to change. Only the law can change you. I used to be a murderer; the law said thou shalt not murder. I used to be a thief; the law said thou shalt not steal. I used to be an abuser. Once I know the Lord, I repent. Same thing, brother. Same thing, sister, with your trauma. Stop using your trauma as a crutch. It happened when you were 14, 15, 16, and now you're 46, 50, in your third marriage, still using it, and you can't keep a man or a woman because you cannot cope.

We never grew up around order, structure and unity. So when we come around it now, we begin to feel uncomfortable, because we realize we are the problem: the reason environments become toxic, the reason people bicker and fight, the instigating spirit we grew up seeing. Now, in a body and a truth where the light shines on that, you are forced to change, and brothers and sisters do not want to.

“Whoso feareth the Lord shall direct his friendship aright: for as he is, so shall his neighbour be also.” If you fear the Lord, you are going to direct your friendships aright, because as you are, so shall your neighbour be. But if you are constantly having issues, constantly having problems, who is the issue? Who is causing these troubles? With the laws of God and all the examples in the scriptures, you should be able to direct your friendship aright. So why is your name always in something?

“My son, gather instruction from thy youth up: so shalt thou find wisdom till thine old age.” We didn't have the opportunity to gather instruction from our youth up. But coming into this truth we have to be born again and begin to do so. You can't drag in all the ways your grandmama and your auntie and them used to deal with each other. It's a new day.

“She is very unpleasant to the unlearned.” Wisdom is very unpleasant to the unlearned. You didn't learn about yourself. All you ever did was point out other people's problems. You never examined yourself; you never looked in the mirror. So now that wisdom finally reveals who you are, it is very unpleasant.

“he that is without understanding will not remain with her.” That's why people have to find a reason to leave. They get offended, they find a reason to be mad, and then they go. What is the root cause? They don't want to change once that wisdom is revealed. And the law, which is perfect, converts only the soul that will be changed.

Destructive attitudes begin internally before they become visible externally. A person may still attend services, teach, lead, pray or serve while harboring the wrong spirit, an evil spirit. You look at the fringes and think, he's good, she's good; you would be surprised how many have an evil spirit in the midst of us. Some come here to destroy the unity of the brotherhood, because in the world it's always chaos: you never see a room full of black people with no fight, no argument, breaking bread together. Whatever you were going through in the world, you had better get over it, and quick, because that thing will destroy you. Those who carry that spirit will find themselves outside these doors.
blog/2026/2026-08-15-2026-08-15-give-dil:
Romans 10 asks, how shall they hear except they be sent? We have been sent to the four corners of the earth, sent from the beginning to be saviours, to “raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel.” And Paul shows the way God chose to do it: “For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.”

Our people may see what we do as foolishness. Someone may say, I’ve just been called to do this to fold. No. God says it pleased him by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.

That is our purpose. Preach God’s word. To be sent to preach God’s word, to save the believers, to save the elect. That is our goal and our mission, and you have to take pride in it.

So when Isaiah says the servant shall be “my salvation unto the end of the earth”, this is how: not by the wisdom of the world, which never knew God, but by the preaching of the prophets whom God formed from the womb and sent. Standing on the corner looking like a fool preaching his word is exactly what pleases him, and it is how Jacob is brought again to him.

Isaiah says the Lord formed his servant from the womb “to bring Jacob again to him”, “to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel”, “that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.” That you may be a saviour. A lot of times we, the prophets, don’t understand the magnitude of our calling. The Lord said he would send us as saviours, and our people’s salvation will come no other way than by the prophets, the saviours God sent, and through his word. Paul shows why.

“How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard?” This shows the importance of the prophets, the saviours: there is no way for the people to be saved unless the saviours are sent. “and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent?”

We have been sent, throughout the four corners of the earth, and from the beginning, to be saviours. By going forth and teaching God’s word, salvation comes here on earth. “as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace.”

That is why the prophets of God are “glorious in the eyes of the Lord.” There is no higher calling than being a prophet of the Most High God, once he has revealed his son in you at the appointed time. Some of us used to be athletes, and once Christ was awakened in us we let all that go. None of it compares to what we do now in these last days as watchmen of Israel. This is the true glory, glorious not to man but to God, and our God is our strength to raise up the tribes of Jacob.

Micah says, “Arise ye, and depart; for this is not your rest: because it is polluted, it shall destroy you, even with a sore destruction.” America, Babylon the great, all the lands we have been enslaved and colonised in, are not our rest. Isaiah shows why staying in them destroys us: “Wherefore thus saith the Holy One of Israel, Because ye despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and stay thereon”.

We despise God's word and trust in oppression. It was a sin for us to trust in this oppression and to stay and believe in it. “Therefore this iniquity shall be to you as a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking cometh suddenly at an instant.” There is no comfort and no protective covering in this society, in assimilating into America, Babylon the great. Our brothers and sisters that love this society and this world, it is our downfall as a people.

That is the pollution Micah speaks of. When you forget where you come from and get comfortable in the land of your captivity, it destroys you, because you begin to take on the attributes of your oppressor. That is not for us. We are God's children, and trying to make the oppressor's ways work for us always backfires. The white man has had the sword and the power to rule the world, but God will not let his children follow after him like the rest of the world and prosper.

So the wall breaks suddenly. In every place we have been, oppression, death and destruction follow behind us, and there is no peace there. Look at the families of Nolan Wales, of Kendrick Johnson, of the young woman found hanging from a tree in Mississippi: they never have rest again. And look at how we think as a people on social media and in all these podcasts: from the aged man and aged woman down to the children, we are in a sore destruction, because we have gotten comfortable in our captivity, “forgotten their restingplace”, and do not even want to go back to our homeland.

Why is it that when our iniquity had an end, Esau refused to let us go and kept shedding our blood? Solomon speaks of the ancient Egyptians, and this is modern Egypt today: “not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.” Their malice is bred in them: God made them that way. They will never change as a race of people. That's why it has been a perpetual hatred from Cain to Abel, Jacob to Esau, blacks and whites, playing itself out over and over, while Christianity blinds us from accepting what God is telling us.

Name a century that black people have had pure peace around this white man. Not we-got-the-vote peace: you still get jailed, racially profiled, shot down, and you can't do what white people do when they get pulled over. The record lists it: the transatlantic slave trade and child slavery from 1619 to 1865, racial terror after emancipation, massacres in Memphis, Colfax, Wilmington, Atlanta, East St. Louis, the Red Summer, Arkansas, Tulsa, Rosewood. And that is only what was reported; imagine what was not documented.

As a result of all this enslavement and all these massacres, Esau is thinking a certain way now. He thinks he's getting away with it: “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence.” Oh, wait a minute, we just enslaved the Lord's people and he didn't do anything.

“thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself.” That is what Esau is thinking to this day. That's why they don't hold themselves accountable for anything. They hold themselves not guilty when they slay us, when they kill us, when they put us into slavery, when they don't give us reparations. Esau thinks he is God.

“but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.” There will be a judgment for these things. So don't think that smiling white man in your face means to do you good.
blog/2026/2026-08-15-2026-08-15-prison-h:
To prove who the congregation is, one more: “All the congregation of Israel shall keep it.”

That is it right there. The congregation is Israel. Not the church, not the Baptist church, not the Catholic church: the congregation of Israel, the ones commanded to keep the passover.

So read Isaiah again: “I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation”: that is Israel. “in the sides of the north”: that is North America. “I will ascend above the heights of the clouds”: that is airplanes and helicopters. “I will be like the most High”: I will be like God. “Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit.” Regardless of all the technological power they have, America, Babylon, Lucifer is going to be brought down to hell.

And he is the one “that opened not the house of his prisoners”. We are the prisoners, the congregation he sat on, but our people believe they are free.

“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!” God has not changed the subject from Babylon; he changed the metaphor. Babylon, Lucifer, America: the same thing. America weakens all the nations.

“I will exalt my throne above the stars of God”: that is space travel. “I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north”: that is slavery. When you are sitting on somebody, you have conquered them, you beat them. Well, who is the congregation? Is it the church, the Baptist church, the Catholic church?

“Remember thy congregation, which thou hast purchased of old; the rod of thine inheritance, which thou hast redeemed; this mount Zion, wherein thou hast dwelt.”

The congregation is the people God purchased of old, the rod of his inheritance, the people he redeemed, mount Zion where he dwelt. That is Israel. So when Lucifer says he will sit upon the mount of the congregation, he is saying he will sit on God’s own inheritance, and that is what was done to us in the sides of the north, North America.

“Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement.” The word covenant means agreement, and our people made one. The same thing happened before, in the time of the Greeks: “In those days went there out of Israel wicked men, who persuaded many, saying, Let us go and make a covenant with the heathen that are round about us: for since we departed from them we have had much sorrow.”

See that? Wicked men went out of Israel saying, let us go and make a covenant, an agreement, with the heathen, meaning the other nations, the Greeks in this context. They told the people that since they had departed from the nations they had had much sorrow.

People often say the Bible has no relevance today. What we just read has all the relevance in the world for today, because the same thing they did back then, making a covenant with the Greeks, our people are doing today, making a covenant with every white man or woman they can find. They join MAGA, the Republican party, the Democratic party.

That is the covenant with death: agreement with the white man and his philosophies. The hell is our people held in a low state. That is why people like Brandon Tatum, Jason Whitlock and Candace Owens, the ball players and the rappers, say I am not oppressed, because they make millions. You are oppressed: what they do to the masses of your people they will do to you if you step out of line.

And God’s word to all our people who join with Esau and the Arabs is this: “your covenant with death shall be disannulled, and your agreement with hell shall not stand; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, then ye shall be trodden down by it.” God is going to judge them.

Against the covenant with death, the Lord God lays something else: “Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste.” This stone is Christ, and Ephesians proves it: “And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone.”

Christ himself is the chief corner stone. That means he is the leader; he is the commander. Read on: “In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord.” The whole building, fitly framed together on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, grows into a holy temple in him.

So “he that believeth shall not make haste” means the one who builds on that stone will not be confounded. You will be delivered. You will be saved.

Everyone else has built on something else. Our people made a covenant with death, the white man and his philosophies, and an agreement with hell, keeping our people in a low state. They made lies their refuge, Christianity and democracy, and hid themselves under falsehood, thinking the overflowing scourge of judgment will not come to them. But the Lord lays judgment to the line and righteousness to the plummet; the hail sweeps away the refuge of lies at the second coming, at Armageddon, and the covenant with death is disannulled. Only what is built on the corner stone, Christ, stands.

“for he was cut off out of the land of the living”: that is when he was crucified. Daniel prophesied it: “And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself.” Messiah, that's Christ, is cut off, but not for himself. He didn't die for himself; Isaiah says, “for the transgression of my people was he stricken.”

“and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary; and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and unto the end of the war desolations are determined.” The people of the prince that shall come is Rome.

So the same Rome that dominated Israel when Christ was cut off came and destroyed the city and the sanctuary. Christ was cut off for the transgression of his people, and desolations were determined upon the city by the hand of Rome.

We might think that Christ doesn't understand what we are going through. Isaiah 53 shows that Christ knows perfectly well what we are going through. The whole chapter is talking about Christ, and verse 8 says: “He was taken from prison and from judgment.” How?

John shows it. “And from thenceforth Pilate sought to release him: but the Jews cried out, saying, If thou let this man go, thou art not Cesar’s friend.” Pilate “brought Jesus forth, and sat down in the judgment seat in a place that is called the Pavement, but in the Hebrew, Gabbatha.”

“And it was the preparation of the passover, and about the sixth hour: and he saith unto the Jews, Behold your King! But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Cesar. Then delivered he him therefore unto them to be crucified. And they took Jesus, and led him away.”

That is how he was taken from prison and from judgment: bound, set before the judgment seat, rejected by his own for Caesar, and led away. The one who was taken from prison is the one who comes to preach to our people, who are in the prison house today.

“and who shall declare his generation?” David answers: “A seed shall serve him; it shall be accounted to the Lord for a generation. They shall come, and shall declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done this.”

To declare means to teach. To declare means to preach. They shall come and shall declare his righteousness: that's us, you and me. Unto a people that shall be born: that's us too.

So the question Isaiah asks is answered by a seed that serves him and is accounted to the Lord for a generation. Christ was cut off out of the land of the living, but his generation is declared by those who come after, teaching and preaching his righteousness to our people that he hath done this.

Jeremiah says, “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.” Paul is talking about the same thing: “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.” That examine yourselves is the same thing Jeremiah said: let us search and try our ways.

This is a lot of times what we as a people do not want to do: examine ourselves. What is wrong with me? What is wrong with you? Who raised you? Why do you act that way? Why do you do the things that you do?

“Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?” You have to prove your own self, whether Christ is in you or not. And that is where turning again to the Lord starts. Jeremiah goes on, “We have transgressed and have rebelled: thou hast not pardoned”, and that is why we are in this state, the condition we are in now. A people who will not examine themselves will never see why the Lord has covered himself with a cloud, and will never turn again to him.

Paul says: “And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed.” Salvation is near. It is high time that we wake up from our sleep.

In order to wake up, we must start by examining ourselves, which is what Jeremiah calls for: “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.” What is wrong with me? What is wrong with you? Who raised you? Why do you act that way? Why do you do the things that you do?

Waking up is not only knowing who we are. It is searching our own ways, seeing that “We have transgressed and have rebelled”, and turning again to the Lord, lifting up our heart with our hands unto God in the heavens. The time is short and salvation is nearer than when we first believed, so there is no time left to stay asleep in the condition we are in.

How do we search and try our ways? Paul shows it: “What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. “How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground.” Who is Lucifer, and what heaven did he fall from? In the scriptures there are the heavens where the Lord is, which is paradise; there is heaven that is the sky and space; and there are heavens that are a place of authority. Lamentations shows that last one.

“How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel.” The beauty of Israel was cast down from heaven to the earth. That means we were brought down low: brought into captivity, no longer on top, no longer ruling. It is a good analogy showing that heaven also goes into rulership.

So Lucifer falling from heaven is a ruler falling from his place of authority, not an angel falling out of the sky. Read on in Isaiah 14 and he is named: Israel will “take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” Lucifer is the king of Babylon, the oppressor, the golden city, because America is rich. And “They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms”: Lucifer is a man, the man of sin, the fourth beast, the white man.

The same Lord who cast Israel down from heaven to the earth will cut this ruler down to the ground. It is a future prophecy of America being destroyed.

“That thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” In the day the Lord gives us rest from our sorrow, our fear and the hard bondage we were made to serve in, we are going to be speaking against America. The king of Babylon here is America, and this is how we know Lucifer is not an angel: Lucifer is called the king of Babylon, the oppressor, the golden city. In Revelation it is mystery Babylon the great, and Revelation 18 explains that city.

“Standing afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come.” Remember what we read in Isaiah 14: the king of Babylon. Here it is that great city Babylon, that mighty city, and her judgment comes in one hour.

So Lucifer is a city, a country, rulers, a government. “The Lord hath broken the staff of the wicked, and the sceptre of the rulers.” It is not talking about a fallen angel; it is talking about America, the king of Babylon, whose ceasing Israel will proclaim when the Lord gives us rest from the hard bondage.

Isaiah calls the king of Babylon “the golden city”: “How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” Why does it say golden city? Revelation 18 explains it: “For in one hour so great riches is come to nought.”

So great riches: that is the golden city. It is called golden because America is rich. Lucifer is talking about America. And all those riches come to nothing in one hour, the same hour of judgment in verse 10, when they stand afar off crying, “Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city!”

The golden city ceasing in Isaiah is the great riches coming to nought in Revelation. It is not an angel that falls; it is a rich nation, a government, the oppressor that made us serve in hard bondage, and in the day the Lord gives us rest, we will take up this proverb against it.

They were called what? Niger means black. The white man uses that term as a derogatory word, but the prophets were called black right through history. So if the prophets were black, what does that mean Christ was? Black too.

And the same way they were called that then, we are called that today. Nothing has changed. The people of the Bible were black, which is why the false Christ of Christianity, the white Jesus, is a deception. “Then shalt thou call, and the Lord shall answer; thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am. If thou take away from the midst of thee the yoke, the putting forth of the finger, and speaking vanity.”

What is the putting forth of the finger? That is blaming. Saul blamed the people right after saying he had kept Agag alive. He blamed the people for keeping the sheep and the best of the flocks, but did not take accountability for keeping Agag the Amalekite alive. So what does the Lord say? He is not going to hear any of us until we stop playing the blame game. The Lord answers, “Here I am”, when the finger is taken away.

Stop blaming others. How are you dealing with that situation? I am bitter against this person because they did this to me; I have hatred towards this person because of this. The Lord does not care about your reasoning or your justification, because every one of us will be judged according to our ways. The Lord sees how that person is treating you, and the same way he sees how you are reacting to that treatment. If you trust in the Lord, you act according to how God commanded you to deal with that situation, and then let the Lord deal with that person.

That is a building block of bitterness. Disobedience, then justifying yourself, then blaming others: the bitterness is compounded on sins that were already there. As 1 Samuel 15:22 says, “to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.”

Mark 7:22 names “an evil eye” among the evil things that come “from within, out of the heart of men”, and “All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” 1 Samuel 18:9 says “Saul eyed David from that day and forward.” Was it with the looks of righteousness, or with an evil eye? “But the Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord troubled him.” Saul was already battling some things. The Lord had rejected him, and an evil spirit from the Lord had taken him.

“And Saul’s servants said unto him, Behold now, an evil spirit from God troubleth thee. Let our lord now command thy servants, which are before thee, to seek out a man, who is a cunning player on an harp: and it shall come to pass, when the evil spirit from God is upon thee, that he shall play with his hand, and thou shalt be well.” They told him: find someone who plays cunningly on a harp, and that spirit will leave you.

There are building blocks of bitterness. Bitterness doesn’t just come about; there are other things first. Saul rejected the word of the Lord, and the Spirit of the Lord departed from him. That was the ground the evil eye grew in. And don’t think, because you are not battling that spirit right now, that it won’t come. Satan says, hold my cup. Wait until you get the new job offer, the promotion, the demotion, the transfer to another school or another city, where you are dealing with different spirits and different circumstances, and you wonder why you are being troubled in the spirit. If it had not been for the Lord, we would all be as Sodom.

“And it came to pass, when the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, that David took an harp, and played with his hand: so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.”

So David did a good thing by playing the music to have that spirit depart from King Saul. Saul did what the servants said, the spirit left him, and he was refreshed. He was like, man, I needed that. He was back in the spirit again. David was sent for Saul’s benefit, and Saul could not see it.

Now fast forward to chapter 18. “And he will destroy in this mountain the face of the covering cast over all people, and the vail that is spread over all nations.” He is going to destroy all the lies this white man cast over all people: that God is white, Jesus is white, the angels are white, the Jews are white. Isaiah 60 is a precept for that verse.

“For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth.” Covered with what? Sin, lies and deceit. That darkness is the covering cast over all people and the vail spread over all nations.

“and gross darkness the people.” The people is talking about the twelve tribes. We are in the worst type of darkness, because the lies were cast over us first and deepest.

“but the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.” When the Lord arises upon Israel, the covering is destroyed and his glory is seen on his people. That is the feast in the mountain of Isaiah 25:6: the lies are taken away, the vail is removed, and the people who sat in gross darkness are the ones his glory rests upon.

How was the covering cast over all people and the vail spread over all nations? Revelation 13 is another precept for it. “And he opened his mouth in blasphemy against God.” That is this white man, beginning with the Roman Catholic Church during the time of the Renaissance. The blasphemy is lies, wicked lies. “to blaspheme his name”: the Roman Catholic Church, Christianity, blasphemed the name of God. “and his tabernacle”: that is the Israelites. “and them that dwell in heaven”: the angels.

“And it was given unto him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them.” It was the Roman Catholic Church, under Pope Nicholas out of Rome, that commanded Spain and Portugal to make war with the saints of God, and the saints of God are the twelve tribes of Israel.
