“and power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations. And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him.” How so? Through the blasphemy of verse 6: all the lies, the deceit and the deception he taught when he conquered us and the nations. He taught Christianity; he taught Eurocentric lies and white supremacy. “whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.”

That is the covering cast over all people, and it is why a woman on the street will say she saw Jesus and he was white with long hair, just like the pictures. Colonization starts in the mind. As long as you worship a white Jesus you are not ruling anything. But in this mountain the Lord will destroy that covering, and the lies he spread over all nations with it.

“Sing, O barren, thou that didst not bear”: that is our foremother Sarah, the wife of Abraham. She was desolate and could not have children, yet “more are the children of the desolate than the children of the married wife”, Hagar, the mother of Ishmael. Israel numbers as the sand of the sea; we outnumber all nations on this planet. Then Isaiah says, “Enlarge the place of thy tent.” Why? Isaiah 49 shows it.

“For thy waste and thy desolate places, and the land of thy destruction”: we got destroyed. “shall even now be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants.” The land of Israel, whose capital is Jerusalem, is not going to be enough to hold all twelve tribes. “and they that swallowed thee up shall be far away.”

“The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other”: after the two thirds that were destroyed. They “shall say again in thine ears, The place is too strait for me”: it is too narrow for us. “give place to me that I may dwell”: give us enough room so that we can all live.

That is why the tent has to be enlarged. Isaiah gives the analogy of a tent, a tabernacle, where we will dwell in Jerusalem: “let them stretch forth the curtains of thine habitations: spare not, lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes.” The cords hold the tent up and the stakes keep it from falling down. So many children are coming home that the land of our destruction will be too narrow, and we will “break forth on the right hand and on the left.”

And when they say we are thirteen percent of the population, that is propaganda. They may be counting only American blacks, but they are not counting the Jamaicans, Haitians, Puerto Ricans or Mexicans.

“For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face.” The glass is talking about the Bible. We do not understand everything in it. Even in saying that, there are different levels, and there are double meanings to many scriptures.

“now I know in part”: we know partially. “but then shall I know”: when the Lord returns, then shall we know. That is the face to face of Ezekiel 20:35, when he pleads with us face to face, and it is how “all thy children shall be taught of the Lord.”

“even as also I am known.” What does that part mean? He created us from the beginning. Before the earth was made, he created us. He already knows us fully; when he returns we will know as we are known, and the children of Israel will be taught of the Lord himself.

Isaiah says, “And all thy children shall be taught of the Lord; and great shall be the peace of thy children.” Ezekiel shows how that teaching will happen: “And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people, and there will I plead with you face to face.”

When the Lord pleads with us face to face, that is when all the children of Israel shall be taught of the Lord. He brings the twelve tribes out and teaches them himself.

And the peace that follows is the rest of Isaiah’s promise: “In righteousness shalt thou be established: thou shalt be far from oppression; for thou shalt not fear: and from terror; for it shall not come near thee.” The twelve tribes shall be established, far from oppression, and terror shall no more come near us. Today our people are still terrorized, hanged from trees and called suicides, but the day of being taught face to face by the Lord is the day that ends.

Isaiah says to the afflicted, “I will lay thy stones with fair colours, and lay thy foundations with sapphires.” That is the kingdom. The Lord will lay our foundations with stones and rubies and emeralds; we are going to have a crown.

John saw that same kingdom: “And the foundations of the wall of the city were garnished with all manner of precious stones.” He names them one by one: “The first foundation was jasper; the second, sapphire; the third, a chalcedony; the fourth, an emerald; The fifth, sardonyx; the sixth, sardius; the seventh, chrysolite; the eighth, beryl; the ninth, a topaz; the tenth, a chrysoprasus; the eleventh, a jacinth; the twelfth, an amethyst.” The sapphire Isaiah promised is right there in the second foundation.

Then Isaiah goes on: “I will make thy windows of agates, and thy gates of carbuncles, and all thy borders of pleasant stones.” These are more precious stones, rubies and diamonds. The twelve tribes of Israel are the afflicted, “tossed with tempest, and not comforted”, and we have not been comforted. But the mountains shall depart, meaning destruction, while the Lord’s kindness does not depart from Israel. The city garnished with precious stones is what he is building for the people he has mercy on.

What does it mean to inherit the Gentiles? “And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls.” That's what it means: we shall own and possess them. “and their kings shall minister unto thee.”

“for in my wrath I smote thee”: that's slavery. In his wrath God smote us, meaning he allowed us to go into slavery. “but in my favour have I had mercy on thee”: that's Christ dying on the cross and delivering us.

“Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night.” The gates of New Jerusalem shall be open continually. Why? “that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles”: the wealth, the riches of the Gentiles. Why? Because it's ours. It has always been ours. “and that their kings may be brought”: brought as what? Slaves.

“For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.” Any nation that will not serve the Lord shall perish. It starts with Christ first. He is our king; his orders are our orders. He gives us an order, and we carry it out to the nations. Whoever does not obey shall perish. That is the seed of Isaiah 54 inheriting the Gentiles and making the desolate cities to be inhabited.

The land of Israel is not going to be enough to hold all twelve tribes. The children left after the two-thirds were destroyed will say, “The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell.” So Isaiah says, “Enlarge the place of thy tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of thine habitations: spare not, lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes; For thou shalt break forth on the right hand and on the left.” We are going to be so large we break out on the right hand and on the left.

“and thy seed shall inherit the Gentiles.” To inherit the Gentiles means to own them, to possess them. It starts with Christ first: “I will declare the decree: the Lord hath said unto me, Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee.” That's Christ.

“Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.” See that? Heathen and Gentiles have the same meaning. The Father gives the heathen to Christ for an inheritance, and Israel's seed inherits the Gentiles with him. Why don't churches ever read this kind of stuff? Why don't apologists ever read it?

“For a small moment have I forsaken thee; but with great mercies will I gather thee.” When you ponder on that, for a small moment have I forsaken thee, it seems like forever and ever to you and me. But to the Lord it is only a small moment. Only a small moment.

Peter shows why: “But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.” One day with the Lord is as a thousand years. So to us it has been thousands of years of being forsaken, but the Lord says, listen, it is only a small moment. It has been one day in the Lord’s time.

And the small moment ends in a gathering: “with great mercies will I gather thee.” He is going to gather us. That is what Christ dying on the cross is about, gathering us back together again.

“For thy Maker is thine husband”. That Maker is Christ: “the Lord of hosts is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel”. So the Lord was never married to all nations on the earth. He was only married to Israel, and Jeremiah says so: “Turn, O backsliding children, saith the Lord; for I am married unto you: and I will take you one of a city, and two of a family, and I will bring you to Zion”.

He is married to the backsliding children of Israel, and he calls them to turn. That is why Isaiah 54:6 speaks of “a wife of youth, when thou wast refused”: refused because we were sinning. He said return, for I am married unto you, and we did not want to return, so the Most High refused us.

And that goes with the marriage supper of the Lamb, where Christians say, oh, we are going to be in the marriage feast. No, you are not. None of you Catholics, you Baptists, you Episcopalians, you Anglicans, you Muslims and Mormons, you are not going to be there. The Lord is married to Israel, and it is Israel he takes, one of a city and two of a family, and brings to Zion.

“In a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment”. That is called slavery. When he hid his face, that is the chains. That is the ships. That is poverty, sickness, death, destruction. That is what all of that sums up right there. Leviticus shows what the little wrath looks like: “And I will set my face against you, and ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you.”

That is a little wrath: slain before our enemies, ruled by them that hate us. And while he hid his face, Psalm 50 shows he kept silence over the wicked who took his covenant in their mouth: “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself”. God is not intervening in some things. He stays silent, because this is the time for us to get our lives together and repent, to put the pieces of the puzzle in the Bible together. So the so-called white man thought God was like him. “but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes”, and that is what is happening now.

But the little wrath is only for a moment. Isaiah 54:8 ends: “but with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith the Lord thy Redeemer.”

In the parable “there was a widow in that city; and she came unto him, saying, Avenge me of mine adversary.” We are that widow. The Lord said he was married unto us, but because we sinned, he refused us. Jeremiah shows the same widow: “How doth the city sit solitary, that was full of people! how is she become as a widow!”

“she that was great among the nations, and princess among the provinces, how is she become tributary”! That is Israel: once full of people, great among the nations, a princess among the provinces, now alone, cast off like a widow, and paying tribute to others. Christ is making reference back to that in Luke 18.

So the widow crying “Avenge me of mine adversary” is us, the twelve tribes, crying for vengeance on our enemies. We want revenge. “he would not for a while”, just as the Lord kept silence for a time, but “because this widow troubleth me, I will avenge her, lest by her continual coming she weary me.” Because the twelve tribes trouble him, he will avenge her. That is the key: pray for vengeance and don't stop.

“And shall not God avenge his own elect, which cry day and night unto him”? We are the elect, crying day and night, three times a day. Some of our people call it unjust that God put us in slavery and punished us, and ask why an all-loving God would do that. It is not unjust: you punish your kids when they go off, and likewise the Lord. “I tell you that he will avenge them speedily.” The question Christ asks is whether, when he comes, he will find that faith: will the widow still be praying for vengeance?

Christ said “Watch therefore” and “Therefore be ye also ready: for in such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh.” Brothers and sisters, we have to be ready. Ezra gives the Lord's word to those who are: “Hear, O ye my beloved, saith the Lord: behold, the days of trouble are at hand, but I will deliver you from the same.”

The days of trouble are at hand, but the Lord will deliver his beloved from them. “Be ye not afraid neither doubt; for God is your guide, And the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts, saith the Lord God: let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves.” God is the guide of those who keep his commandments and precepts; they are the ones left when the others are taken to destruction.

This is the same thing Noah was preaching back then, but nobody listened; everybody mocked him. The message is the same now: keep the commandments, don't let your sins weigh you down, and be ready, because the day comes in an hour you think not.

Christ said “as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.” Noe is the Greek; it is still Noah. In his days they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, “until the day that Noe entered into the ark.” So what was Noah doing all that time? Peter tells us.

God “spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly.” Noah was a preacher of righteousness: a preacher of God's laws, because that is what righteous means, his laws. He was warning the people to repent and change their ways, and the people mocked him and laughed at him.

Then they “knew not until the flood came, and took them all away.” Took them away into what? Not the kingdom of heaven: destruction, death. Took is the past tense of take. So when Christ says “the one shall be taken, and the other left”, the one taken is taken to destruction, like the ungodly in the flood, and the one left is the righteous, like Noah.

So it shall be at Christ's coming: nations eating and drinking and carrying on, while those preaching God's laws are mocked, until the destruction comes on the world of the ungodly. “Therefore be ye also ready.”

“Though thou hast sore broken us in the place of dragons, and covered us with the shadow of death.” The place of dragons is the seven heads: the great red dragon with seven heads and their lands, Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Great Britain, and the eighth head is America. Why has he covered us with the shadow of death? He has allowed these dragons to teach us lies, as a punishment for us disobeying his commandments. “If we have forgotten the name of our God, or stretched out our hands to a strange god”: see that part?

Daniel shows the strange god: “Thus shall he do in the most strong holds with a strange god, whom he shall acknowledge and increase with glory.” That is the white man, starting with the Greeks all the way up to today. Here in our captivity we have stretched out our hands to their strange god, the one you think is Jesus. He acknowledged him and increased him with glory, and robbed everything.

“and he shall cause them to rule over many, and shall divide the land for gain.” He caused his European allies to rule over many. They divided the land of Israel and the land of Africa at the Berlin Conference for gain. That's what they did.

So now we stretch out our hands to a strange god: white Jesus. Like the black woman in the video: Jesus is white, he's the white man, you look like Jesus, long hair, you are Jesus. We have stretched out our hands to a strange god and forgotten the name of our God. “They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods, with abominations provoked they him to anger.” White Jesus is a strange god; Allah is a strange god. “If ye forsake the Lord, and serve strange gods, then he will turn and do you hurt, and consume you, after that he hath done you good.” Have we not been hurt, in slavery, captivity, oppression and poverty? “There shall no strange god be in thee; neither shalt thou worship any strange god.” Yet we worship a god that doesn't look like us, act like us or talk like us, and want that strange god to bless us when he has done nothing but hurt us. Some of your mothers and fathers have that damn crucifix around their necks and on the walls of their houses.

“Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.” We have envied the oppressor and chosen his strange god and his strange religion. “Be not thou envious against evil men, neither desire to be with them.” We want into their politics, their religions, their schools; we want to look like them. The churches have done us a disservice. And the Lord knows it: “Shall not God search this out? for he knoweth the secrets of the heart.” We cry, “Awake, why sleepest thou, O Lord?”, and want him to intervene now, but he says, y'all have got to get yourselves together, men and women, and get right according to my word.

“The righteous shall rejoice when he seeth the vengeance.” Christianity will make you think you are not supposed to read this, but the Bible has it in there for you to rejoice. When you get to see your enemies get it, the people who have been oppressing us and doing all kinds of terrorist acts, and you get to see them get that justice, that's rejuvenation. It revitalizes your bones. “he shall wash his feet in the blood of the wicked”: that means smashing skulls and vertebrae and rib cages with your feet. That's a good thing. That's therapy.

The Bible names the great things we should look for, and one is joy of children: “There be nine things which I have judged in mine heart to be happy, and the tenth I will utter with my tongue: A man that hath joy of his children.” Our brothers and sisters who have lost their husbands and their sons don't get the joy of their children. Their children are hanging on trees; their daughters are hung on trees; lives extinguished. You are supposed to have joy of your children, but because an enemy has taken them from you, hung them on trees, murdered them, you don't get that joy.

“and he that liveth to see the fall of his enemy.” To see the fall of your enemies is therapy, God's therapy. People don't like it; give a damn. We talk about people with trauma; God has given us therapy right there.

That's why verse 11 begins with so: it gives the reason the vengeance of verse 10 is necessary. “So that a man shall say, Verily there is a reward for the righteous: verily he is a God that judgeth in the earth.” Surely there is a reward for our trauma, for the evils that have happened to us, and God is going to give it to us. When he beautifies the meek with salvation, it is us putting our enemies in chains and taking vengeance on them. Christianity isn't going to teach you that; these lying pastors and this Christianity garbage will completely destroy our people if we don't pull our heads out of it. And understand, if you teach that you want justice and vengeance, the enemy will call you hateful, and affliction comes with it. Program your mind for that. Don't think you can teach that the white man is the wicked of the earth and he'll leave you alone.

David, chosen out of Judah and out of his father’s house, hands the building of the house to the son the Lord chose to sit on the throne: “Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father.” “Moreover I will establish his kingdom for ever”. Solomon’s kingdom, not Solomon and his brethren’s. Then David charges him: “Take heed now; for the Lord hath chosen thee to build an house for the sanctuary: be strong, and do it.”

“Then David gave to Solomon his son the pattern of the porch”. The blueprints to the temple: guess who gave them to Solomon? David. Solomon did not come up with the design; David came up with it, and Solomon fulfilled his father’s wishes. That porch is why the feast of dedication is kept at Solomon’s porch. It took Solomon seven years to build the temple and thirteen years to build his own house, so the temple was done before his house was finished.

David gave him the pattern “of the houses thereof, and of the treasuries thereof, and of the upper chambers thereof”, the floors and levels, “and of the inner parlours thereof, and of the place of the mercy seat”, the holy of holies. “And the pattern of all that he had by the spirit”: the spirit moved David to design the temple. The courses of the priests, which priest for burning incense and which for each service, David was behind all of that too. Gold by weight for the things of gold, “refined gold by weight” for the altar of incense, everything gold, “and gold for the pattern of the chariot of the cherubims, that spread out their wings, and covered the ark of the covenant of the Lord.”

“All this, said David, the Lord made me understand in writing by his hand upon me, even all the works of this pattern.” David did not write it off the top of his head. The Lord moved his hand on what to write, and David drew out the temple through his hands. So the house Solomon built on the throne of the kingdom of the Lord was the Lord’s own pattern, given through David to the son chosen to sit on David’s throne.

Abram, childless, was going to leave his house to Eliezer of Damascus, the eldest servant born in his house: “Behold, to me thou hast given no seed: and, lo, one born in my house is mine heir.” The Lord said no: “This shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir.” Not a heathen servant, but his own seed. An heir and an inheritance are the same word, like a family heirloom passed down the line.

That is the key to 1 Chronicles 2: “Now Sheshan had no sons, but daughters. And Sheshan had a servant, an Egyptian, whose name was Jarha. And Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant to wife.” This was while Israel was in Egypt, when we had no land of inheritance allotted to us. People read it and say the Egyptian married into the tribe and became Judah. No.

The record follows that line for generation after generation so that it is known. When Israel came out of Egypt and inherited the land, that line could not receive land, because the land passes by the paternal bloodline and that line goes back to an Egyptian servant. They were among us in the land, but they did not inherit. It is written there to exclude, not to include. Sheshan's brothers had sons and received land; his line did not. It does not mean the Egyptian became a Jew. When we came back under the Persians and the Medes, a man who could not show from his father's house who he came from was given no inheritance, and a Levite could not serve in his office. Zerubbabel could show he came from King David's line.

The daughters of Zelophehad show the law when a man has only daughters. They asked, “Why should the name of our father be done away from among his family, because he hath no son?” The Lord said, “If a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter”, then to his brother, then his father's brethren, then the next kinsman: the law Boaz was fulfilling. But those daughters had to marry “only to the family of the tribe of their father”, “So shall not the inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe.” The inheritance of Israel is paternal. There is no sin in marrying a woman of another tribe; Aaron did it. The command there was only to keep the land in the tribe. We have no land in captivity now, so marry within your nation and stay with your people.

Judah had five sons: Er, Onan and Shelah by the daughter of Shua the Canaanitess, and the twins Pharez and Zerah by Tamar. “The sons of Pharez; Hezron, and Hamul. And the sons of Zerah; Zimri, and Ethan, and Heman, and Calcol, and Dara: five of them in all.” Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Dara became very famous. They were very wise.

How wise? Solomon’s wisdom is measured against them: “For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all nations round about.”

Those same sons of Judah were so wise that many men were named after them, and Solomon surpassed even them. He was wiser than the wise men of his own tribe.

That is the house this genealogy runs through. Hezron, the oldest son of Pharez, begat Ram, and from Ram comes Amminadab, Nahshon, Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse: a tribe of wise men, princes and kings.

Now a tie-in regarding family ties: “And Aaron took him Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Naashon, to wife; and she bare him Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.”

Aaron is Moses’ brother, of Levi. He took Elisheba, Amminadab’s daughter and Nahshon’s sister, to wife. Aaron’s wife was of the tribe of Judah. Those families intermarried, priests and kings marrying together. It is no coincidence; that is why John the Baptist and Christ are cousins.

Nadab and Abihu were the two who offered strange fire and were killed; Eleazar and Ithamar were spared. Eleazar became the high priest in the days of Joshua, the mediator before the Lord. So Eleazar’s mama was Judah. That is why some Levites don’t have the big heads; their mama is Judah. And don’t forget the big nose, too.

So Amminadab begat Nahshon and a daughter Elisheba. Aaron married Elisheba and had the four sons, the high priests, which makes Nahshon Aaron’s brother-in-law. And from Nahshon came Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse: the priesthood and the royal line of Judah bound together in one family.

“And Ram begat Amminadab; and Amminadab begat Nahshon, prince of the children of Judah”. Nahshon was of the elite princes of Judah, a prince family, a royal family. The census confirms the same man: “Of Judah; Nahshon the son of Amminadab.”

And in the camp: “And on the east side toward the rising of the sun shall they of the standard of the camp of Judah pitch throughout their armies: and Nahshon the son of Amminadab shall be captain of the children of Judah.”

So Nahshon was a captain. These men had serious status: princes and captains, leaders. They were warriors; they were not regular men.

“And Nahshon begat Salma, and Salma begat Boaz, And Boaz begat Obed, and Obed begat Jesse”. Boaz came from that line, the line of Pharez, the twin that breached, not the one whose hand came out first with the scarlet thread. And Jesse had eight sons, and one of those sons is David.

Zedekiah rebelled like his brother and his nephew did. He tried to run away and got caught in the plains of Jericho, and they killed his kids in front of him first, then took his eyes out, bound him and locked him up in Babylon. At this point there are no more kings of Judah; Zedekiah was the last one. His sons are gone, his heirs are gone. So who's left?

Read on: “in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah”, “Evil–merodach king of Babylon in the year that he began to reign did lift up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison; And he spake kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon”. Jehoiachin had been locked up between 36 and 37 years. Then he “changed his prison garments: and he did eat bread continually before him all the days of his life.” His allowance was a continual allowance, a daily rate for every day: Babylon gave him a job and status.

Jehoiachin is Jeconiah, and he is the Jechonias of Matthew 1:11. He got some mercy in captivity, but was he a king anymore at this point? No. He was a king, but now he was a captive in Babylon, receiving wages and some status.

And in Babylon he had children: “the sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son”. Salathiel is Shealtiel, the father of Zerubbabel, whose name means born in Babylon. That is where the line of the kings of Judah went on after Zedekiah's sons were slain: through a captive king in Babylon.

About three months after Judah went in to Tamar, she began to show, and word came to Judah that his daughter-in-law had played the harlot and was with child by whoredom. Her husband was dead and she was living in her father's house, so Judah said, “Bring her forth, and let her be burnt”: that was the law for a harlot. But she sent him his own signet, bracelets and staff, and “Judah acknowledged them, and said, She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son.” The child was his, and he was the one in the wrong.

Deuteronomy 25 shows what Judah and Onan owed her. Moses recites this law later, but our forefathers already had knowledge of it through oral tradition passed down from Adam. “If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger: her husband’s brother shall go in unto her.” That is why it was wrong when Onan spilled his seed on the ground.

“the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel.” To succeed in the name of the dead brother does not mean the child takes his actual name. It means the child inherits the dead man's possession, his land and his things, because he left no seed to inherit for him. The brother raises up a surrogate seed in honor of his dead brother, so the land stays in his brother's name and is not lost.

A brother who refuses is brought before the elders. His brother's wife shall “loose his shoe from off his foot, and spit in his face”, saying, “So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother’s house.” And “his name shall be called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.” He carries that humiliation forever, because he would not love his neighbor as himself. That is why the history of Ruth is so important. It is not about Ruth, the Moabite heathen woman; y'all make it about her because y'all love heathens.

So Tamar was more righteous than Judah: she kept her dead husband's name alive when Judah withheld Shelah. From her came twins. Zarah put out his hand first and the midwife bound a scarlet thread on it, but he drew it back and his brother broke forth: “this breach be upon thee: therefore his name was called Pharez.” Pharez means a breach, and the line of the kings runs through him.

The Lord told Ezekiel to bear his stuff on his shoulders in their sight and carry it forth in the twilight, covering his face “that thou see not the ground: for I have set thee for a sign unto the house of Israel.” God made Ezekiel himself a sign unto the house of Israel.

Read on to verse 11 and Ezekiel is told to say it to Israel plainly: “Say, I am your sign: like as I have done, so shall it be done unto them: they shall remove and go into captivity.” What the prophet did, Israel would go through.

This lines up with Isaiah 8. When the Lord gives a sign, it is the man and the child he gives, not the woman. Isaiah and his children were signs and wonders in Israel, and Ezekiel was set for a sign to the house of Israel, which is why the sign of Isaiah 7:14 is the child born to Isaiah and the prophetess.

“Thus Ezekiel is unto you a sign.” What is he? A sign. Not his wife: Ezekiel. “according to all that he hath done shall ye do: and when this cometh, ye shall know that I am the Lord God.”

The Lord told Ezekiel to eat dung, and what did we end up doing? Eating dung. He was a sign, and what he did came upon Israel.

Read on to verse 27: “thou shalt be a sign unto them; and they shall know that I am the Lord.” Again and again the man is the sign. So when Isaiah says “I and the children whom the Lord hath given me are for signs”, it fits the pattern of the prophets: the sign given to Ahaz was the child Isaiah's wife bare, Maher-shalal-hash-baz, not a virgin.

Isaiah had just told Ahaz, “the Lord himself shall give you a sign”. Then in chapter 8 the Lord has Isaiah write the name Maher-shalal-hash-baz, quick to the plunder, swift to the spoil, and Isaiah goes unto the prophetess, his wife, and “she conceived, and bare a son.” The child was named before he was conceived, the same way Gabriel named John and named Christ before they were conceived.

Then Isaiah says who the sign is: “Behold, I and the children whom the Lord hath given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel from the Lord of hosts, which dwelleth in mount Zion.” Behold who? I, Isaiah, and the children. Not his wife. He never counts the woman.

So the sign of Isaiah 7:14 was not the virgin; it was the child. The virgin birth was garbage. The birth of Isaiah's son was the sign that Ephraim and Syria banding together against Judah would fail. Before the child could cry “My father, and my mother,” the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria were taken away before the king of Assyria. Assyria would pass through Judah and “reach even to the neck”, coming close to conquering but failing, because of Immanuel: “Take counsel together, and it shall come to nought; speak the word, and it shall not stand: for God is with us.” Once Isaiah's son was born, the two kings could not succeed against Judah.

When the people were gathered thick together, Christ said, “This is an evil generation: they seek a sign; and there shall no sign be given it, but the sign of Jonas the prophet.” Then: “For as Jonas was a sign unto the Ninevites, so shall also the Son of man be to this generation.”

Jonas was a sign. The Son of man was a sign. Men were always the signs. There is no scripture where the women were signs. Hosea was also a sign, and his marriage was a sign, but the woman by herself was never a sign.

That settles Isaiah 7 and 8. The Lord said he would give Ahaz a sign, and Isaiah tells us who it was: himself and the children the Lord gave him. The son born to Isaiah and the prophetess was the sign that God was with Judah, Immanuel, and that the two kings coming against Judah would come to nought.

Baruch gives another one. Overshadow does not mean that it got her impregnated. It means to guide her to where she had to go. “For God hath appointed that every high hill, and banks of long continuance, should be cast down, and valleys filled up, to make even the ground, that Israel may go safely in the glory of God”.

“Moreover even the woods and every sweetsmelling tree shall overshadow Israel by the commandment of God. For God shall lead Israel with joy in the light of his glory”. The trees shall overshadow Israel, for God shall lead Israel. To overshadow is to lead, guide or defend.

So in Luke 1:35 the Lord would lead Mary to Joseph. When it says overshadow thee, it means he will guide and lead her, like he led Zacharias home to his wife to lay with her. That is what it is talking about, not him overshadowing her into pregnancy.

The law shows what conceiving is: “Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, If a woman have conceived seed, and born a man child: then she shall be unclean seven days”. She conceived what? Seed.

A woman conceives seed through intercourse. That is the same seed Onan spilled on the ground in Genesis 38, knowing the inheritance would not be his. It is the same exact thing.

So Luke 1:31, “thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son”, is a woman conceiving seed and bearing a man child. It is said to Mary in the same form of words as to Zacharias about Elisabeth: “thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John,” and “shalt call his name JESUS.” The same thing being done, the same thing being said.

This goes with overshadow: the Lord guided Mary, and she went and came together with her husband. “Man’s goings are of the Lord; how can a man then understand his own way?”

A man’s goings are of the Lord because the Lord guides us and overshadows us in everyday life. Sometimes you are walking in the street, something tells you to pick something up off the ground, and a car goes right by where you would have been. Why? The Lord was there guiding you.

“how can a man then understand his own way?” Remember, Mary did not understand. She said, “How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?” She was espoused to Joseph but had not yet come together with him. The Lord said, don’t worry, you are going to fulfil the scriptures; I am going to guide you. She could not understand her way, but the Most High had plans for her, and he guided her, the same way he guided every one of us here.

Gabriel tells Mary, “thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son”. It is the same word used of her cousin: “And after those days his wife Elisabeth conceived”. What does it mean to conceive? To conceive you need seed; the man’s seed has to go in and fertilize the egg. Some might be confused, so Ruth shows how that happens.

“So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife: and when he went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception, and she bare a son.” When Boaz went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception. That is how it works: a husband goes in unto his wife, and the Lord gives the conception.

And when Luke 1:28 says the angel “came in unto her”, he came in and talked with her. He did not come in and have sex with her; he came in and talked to her, plain and simple. So when Luke 1:31 says Mary shall conceive, it is conception the way Ruth conceived, the Lord giving it when her husband came unto her. It could well have been the first time Joseph touched her that the Lord made her conceive.

Luke 1:35 says “the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee”. What does overshadow mean? Wisdom of Solomon shows it: “For the whole creature in his proper kind was fashioned again anew, serving the peculiar commandments that were given unto them, that thy children might be kept without hurt”. The whole creature is Israel, the whole nation that came out of Egypt, made new, serving the peculiar commandments.

“As namely, a cloud shadowing the camp; and where water stood before, dry land appeared; and out of the Red sea a way without impediment; and out of the violent stream a green field: Wherethrough all the people went that were defended with thy hand, seeing thy marvellous strange wonders.”

What did the cloud shadowing the camp do for us at the Red Sea? It led us. It guided us through the Red Sea, and the people went through “defended with thy hand.” That is what overshadow means: to lead, guide and defend.

So when the angel says the power of the Highest shall overshadow Mary, it is not the spirit coming into her and making her pregnant. It is the Lord guiding and defending her, leading her to where she had to go.

Matthew names Christ's family: “is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?” Mary his mother and Mary his aunt at the cross, a brother named Simon among Simons everywhere: Israel used the same names over and over, even inside one family. The Maccabees prove it.

“In those days arose Mattathias the son of John, the son of Simeon, a priest.” “And he had five sons, Joannan, called Caddis: Simon; called Thassi: Judas, who was called Maccabeus: Eleazar, called Avaran: and Jonathan, whose surname was Apphus.” Stop at Jonathan. Joannan and Jonathan are the same name: John and John, two sons of one father. Like George Foreman naming his sons George, George, George and George.

So it was a common thing for Israel to name sons the same name. You had Mary and Mary, John and John, John the Baptist too; they loved that name. You had Simon Iscariot, Simon the Canaanite, Simon Peter, and Christ's own brother Simon. That is why two Zerubbabels in the genealogies is no puzzle at all.

In Matthew his own people asked, “Is not this the carpenter's son?” John shows his own disciples said the same thing: “Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.”

The son of who? The son of Joseph. The one Moses and the prophets wrote about is called by his disciple the son of Joseph, the carpenter.

And Matthew says he had brethren, James, Joses, Simon and Judas, and sisters, more than one: a bunch of siblings. James wrote the book of James and Judas wrote Jude. So you Christians who say Mary was a virgin who never had sex read this all the time. Now some hear us teach it and act like they came up with it, saying the Roman Catholic doctrine is wrong, playing catchup. Christ had a father and a mother, brothers and sisters.

Mark gives the same account as Matthew 13. On the sabbath Christ “began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing him were astonished, saying, From whence hath this man these things?” Then: “Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him.”

They knew his family. They knew his background, his mother, his brothers by name, and his sisters. Who do he think he is? We grew up with this guy. He ain't nobody special. You're from the hood like us, from Nazareth; what you talking about, Savior? In his own home, where he was from, he got disrespected by his own neighbors and family members.

So the scripture itself shows Christ was born into a real family, the son of Mary with brothers and sisters, and that the people offended at him were the ones who knew exactly where he came from.

Matthew says Mary was espoused to Joseph, and “before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.” What does “came together” mean? Genesis 29 shows the custom. Jacob served seven years for Rachel, then said, “Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in unto her.” “And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast. And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he went in unto her.”

The feast is the coming together. Coming together was the customary wedding feast, the same custom seen with Tobit. So before Joseph and Mary came together in the wedding feast, they lay together. There was no fornication, because they were already espoused. Espousal is marriage: once the father made the promise, she could not go and marry another, and a man who lies with a betrothed woman commits adultery. That is why the angel called Mary Joseph's wife. She was his wife by espousal, not because he had lain with her; sex alone does not make a marriage.

Then “Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily.” The commentators say that means he meant to divorce her secretly, because the child was not his. But if a just man's espoused wife were pregnant by another man, the law said she must die; a just man would not hide her. Put her away privily means hide her, the way “Elisabeth conceived, and hid herself five months.” A public example means being put to death in public. Had Mary gone back to her father's house showing, they would have said she played the harlot, just as they said of Tamar at three months.

So here is the question: why would a just man hide a pregnant woman he did not impregnate? And if she had committed adultery, why would a just man hide her sin? There is no way around that question. Minded means he was thinking about it: he was going to hide her so nothing would happen to her for what the two of them had done, because the child was his.

The Lord promised David a king out of his own body: “And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.”

The seed that proceeds out of David's bowels is the promised king. So when the angel came to Joseph in the dream, he called him “Joseph, thou son of David”. The line is Joseph's, David's line.

The angel said, “fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost.” That which is conceived in her is of the prophecy of 2 Samuel: the seed promised to David, coming out of his bowels.

That is why the Nativity begins with the bloodline. The child Mary conceived is the fulfilling of the promise made to David, that God would set up his seed after him and establish his kingdom.

Peter said of David: “Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne”.

God swore to David that of the fruit of his loins he would raise up Christ, and notice the words: according to the flesh. Not according to the spirit. Christ sits on David's throne as the fruit of David's loins in the flesh.

That is why the angel spoke to “Joseph, thou son of David”, and why “that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost” means it is of the prophecy: the promise sworn to David in 2 Samuel 7 and Psalm 132 that the king would come out of his bowels, the fruit of his body.

So the child of Matthew 1 is the Christ God swore to raise up of the fruit of David's loins, according to the flesh, to sit on his throne. The bloodline is the birthright.

The promise to David was sworn: “The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.”

The Lord swore it in truth, and he will not turn from it. The king on David's throne would be the fruit of David's body. That is the same promise as 2 Samuel 7:12, the seed that shall proceed out of David's bowels.

So when the angel said to Joseph, “Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost”, that which is conceived in her is of the prophecy: the fruit of David's body that the Lord swore to set upon his throne. The line runs through Joseph, the son of David.

“And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” The son is the fruit of David's body, sworn in truth, set on David's throne.

Paul says it plainly: “Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh”. According to what? The flesh.

According to the flesh, he was made like you and I: made flesh and blood like unto his brethren, like his children. The same thing.

That is how Matthew 1 reads. Joseph was minded to put Mary away privily, “But while he thought on these things”, not did them but only thought about doing them, the angel appeared to him saying, “Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost.” That which is conceived in her is of the prophecy: the seed promised to David in 2 Samuel 7 and Psalm 132, of the fruit of his loins according to the flesh.

So Jesus Christ our Lord was made of the seed of David according to the flesh. He came into this world as a son of man, made flesh and blood like his brethren, and that is how he fulfils the promise to David.

Naomi told Ruth, “Behold, thy sister in law is gone back unto her people, and unto her gods”. Orpah went back to Moab, to her people and her gods. These were not Israelite women; this was a heathen woman of another nation. That is important, because there are doctrines out there teaching that Ruth was an Israelite. No, she was not. She was a heathen. Was it right for Boaz to deal with a heathen? No, but it happened.

Just in case there is any confusion, the last verse of Judges, right above Ruth, shows why it happened: “In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.” During the judges, we did what we wanted to do.

And Ruth opens in that very time: “Now it came to pass in the days when the judges ruled”. There was no king. It was the time when Israel did what they wanted, and that included taking heathen women.

So Ruth's story does not make her an Israelite, and it does not make it right to take a heathen wife. It shows what Israel was doing when every man did what was right in his own eyes. The scripture keeps calling her what she is: “Ruth the Moabitess”. That is clear.

Ruth said, “thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God”. She is a heathen saying, if I go with you, I will be as if I am an Israelite, and I will serve your God too. She is cleaving to an Israelite woman, that's all; there were no promises made to her. “Where thou diest, will I die, and there will I be buried”: I'm not leaving you.

The nations are going to be the same way in the kingdom. Zechariah shows it: “Thus saith the Lord of hosts; In those days it shall come to pass, that ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you.”

We will go with you, just like Ruth said. For we have heard that God is with you: your God is a real God, and ours is garbage. They are going to cleave to Israel the way Ruth cleaved to Naomi, and they will cleave as servants.

So Ruth is the picture of the nations in the kingdom: not Israelites, but holding on to Israel because the God of Israel is the true God.

“And Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed”. Boaz raised up seed in the name of Mahlon, but the record says Boaz begat Obed, not Mahlon, because Mahlon was dead. The genealogy goes under Boaz; the land falls under the dead man's line. Obed takes on the land of Elimelech even though that is not his father's line. That is the inheritance: the parcel of land, the parcel of field, the parcel of ground. You don't inherit a tribe; you inherit the land. And they were both of the same tribe anyway.

That is why the scripture says this in Jeremiah: “And it shall come to pass, after that I have plucked them out I will return, and have compassion on them, and will bring them again, every man to his heritage, and every man to his land.” It literally means what it says. In the beginning God allotted every family land.

The line of David had an inheritance given to it; the families of Judah each had land appointed to them. Guess what? Those families are here today. When the Lord returns, those that make it, that repented, are going back to that land, every man to his heritage.

That is why Boaz raised up seed for Elimelech's family: so the land would stay within that family's inheritance. That is loving your neighbor as yourself. We kept our land in house. So land is very important: if you have it, keep it and give it to your kids; don't just sell it off. A lot of Judah had millions of acres here in America, and Esau stole them, creating laws like eminent domain and finding some distant kin to pay a little money and take the land. There are beaches that belong to us. But the Lord will bring every man again to his heritage and to his land.

Judges shows how the land was first given: “And when Joshua had let the people go, the children of Israel went every man unto his inheritance to possess the land.” We all had land and an inheritance. When we came out of Egypt, every family was allotted land. Whoever of those same families is left after the destruction takes place will be given back the land and inheritance that was given to us back then.

Notice it says every man unto his inheritance. Sisters, you're divorcing us and taking half our stuff, but it says every man. Our wives benefit from our inheritance; it belongs to the men, but it is theirs too because they are married to us. According to God, the inheritance belongs to the men, just as the earth belonged to Adam, and Eve benefitted from it because she was helping him.

And the land we inherit is not an acre or something. 1 Chronicles 2 shows Jair “who had three and twenty cities in the land of Gilead”, “even threescore cities”. We owned cities. Somebody literally owned the Bronx, Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens. We had castles on those cities, winter houses and summer houses.

That is why the land in Ruth had to stay with Elimelech's family. Boaz begat Obed, and the genealogy goes through Boaz down to Jesse and David, but the inheritance, every man's portion from the time of Joshua, stayed with the dead man's line through the seed raised up to him.

Genesis 33 gives the history behind the “parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph” in John 4. “Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Padan–aram; and pitched his tent before the city. And he bought a parcel of a field, where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for an hundred pieces of money.”

Jacob bought that land from the Hamites for a hundred pieces of money, and “he erected there an altar, and called it El–elohe–Israel.” A parcel of a field is again the same thing as a parcel of land: an inheritance.

Later, as he was dying, Israel told Joseph, “Moreover I have given to thee one portion above thy brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.” His sons did take the land by the sword; Simeon and Levi went crazy and killed the men of that city. But the field was bought first, before his sons ever took it. So the inheritance at Shechem stood on a lawful purchase, the same way Boaz bought Elimelech's parcel before the elders at the gate.

Ruth 4 is a trial at the gate before ten elders over land. Elimelech had land; he died, and his two sons, Mahlon and Chilion, died too, leaving no man to take it. So the land had to be taken up by the next of kin. Boaz told the nearer kinsman that Naomi “selleth a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech’s.” A parcel of land: that phrase opens the whole chapter.

John 4 uses the same wording. Christ “must needs go through Samaria. Then cometh he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.” Jacob gave Joseph that parcel of ground; he bought his son that land.

A parcel of land, a parcel of ground, a parcel of a field: they are all the same thing, and a parcel of land and an inheritance are one and the same. So when Boaz bought the parcel that was Elimelech's, he was not making an ordinary purchase. He was taking up an inheritance in Israel, one that had to stay in the family of the dead.

“And the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem, in a parcel of ground which Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for an hundred pieces of silver: and it became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.” The parcel of ground, the parcel of land, the parcel of a field is the land of inheritance, and this one was given to Ephraim.

That is what Boaz was protecting in Ruth 4. The nearer kinsman would not redeem it, “lest I mar mine own inheritance”, and plucked off his shoe; here the shoe is passed without shame, because he is yielding the right to someone else, not refusing his brother. Boaz bought all that was Elimelech's, Chilion's and Mahlon's, and took Ruth, the wife of Mahlon, “to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren.” The son he raised up would inherit that land, because it belonged to Mahlon. Boaz is still the father; Boaz begat Obed, and the line goes through Boaz. There are no two fathers. The land falls under the dead man's line; the lineage goes back to Boaz. That is love your neighbor as yourself.

So Elimelech did not lose his land. We kept our land in house. Land is very important: if you have it, keep it and give it to your children; don't sell it off. Our people once had millions of acres in America, and Esau made laws, eminent domain among them, and found a distant kin to pay off with a little money, and so stole millions of acres, beaches included, from Judah.

The allotment still stands. When we came out of Egypt, every family was allotted land, and Judges says “the children of Israel went every man unto his inheritance to possess the land.” Those families are here today. The Lord says he “will bring them again, every man to his heritage, and every man to his land.” Whoever is left after the destruction, those who repent, will be given back the land and inheritance that was given to us back then.

Zerubbabel built the second temple, so he brought forth a literal stone with a foundation. That's the first level. But it is twofold: he also brought forth the other stone through his loins, to build up the temple which is us here in the room.

“And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”: the chief corner stone, the headstone. “In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord”: that's us. “In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit.”

So we are that holy temple that Christ builds. Zerubbabel laid the foundation of the second temple, and he brought forth the same stone and the same foundation, which is Christ, on whom we are built. Praise the Lord for that.

Zechariah says, “For behold the stone that I have laid before Joshua; upon one stone shall be seven eyes.” The Branch and the stone are Christ. Then Zerubbabel “shall bring forth the headstone thereof.”

What is the headstone? “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.” Who is the Branch, who is the stone? It's the same thing. The headstone Zerubbabel brings forth is the same stone laid before Joshua, and the same servant the Branch the Lord said he would bring forth: Christ, refused by the builders and made the head of the corner.

So when the Lord says “I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day”, he is going into Christ. The stone laid before Joshua the high priest and his fellows, men wondered at for a sign, is the Christ who would come through Zerubbabel's loins.

“for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.” Who is that? Christ. And the next chapter says who brings him forth: “Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain.” The great mountain is Babylon, made a plain, destroyed.

“and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it.” Who shall bring forth the headstone? Zerubbabel. Chapter 3 said the Lord will bring forth his servant the Branch; here Zerubbabel brings forth the headstone, which is the same as the Branch. And the headstone brings grace unto us.

How will Zerubbabel bring him forth? Through his line. And Zerubbabel comes out of Solomon's line. Matthew 1 shows it: “And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel”, born in Babylon, and from Zorobabel down to “Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” Joseph comes out of the line of kings, the kingdom of Solomon, heir to the throne, but in captivity, with Rome calling the shots and an Edomite, Herod, on the throne, until Christ returns and conquers Edom. There is no scripture that says Jeconiah's line was cursed from being kings; that doctrine was made to justify a virgin birth. The Zerubbabel of Luke 3 is a different one, of Nathan's line: Joseph is written there because he inherited Heli's inheritance as his son-in-law, Heli being Mary's father with no sons.

Christ says “joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance”, and then says it again: “Likewise, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.” The heavenly host, the angels, are happy when you change your life, when you get it together.

That is why we are weapons. “The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; and he that winneth souls is wise.” You have the potential to convert sinners, to have a brother or sister change his life, and that makes you dangerous. When one sinner repents, the angels rejoice.

How do you win a soul? Ultimately it is the word of God, but the Lord gave a secret: “By long forbearing is a prince persuaded”. We are fishers of men, on duty all day, handing out flyers even at a gas station, not waiting till Saturday or till you feel like it. But you have to be patient; you can't be brutish. Are you looking to win the argument or to win the brother or sister? Listen, study the person, wait for the moment. Don't take it personal when someone doesn't take the flyer; maybe next time. Elisha prayed, “Lord, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see”, and the young man saw “the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.” The Lord showed him something nobody could see: he opened his eyes, and he could see what was behind him. In the spiritual realm, there are angels all around us.

The Lord said it: “where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.” We don't see that. But the Lord will open up his spirit to make it evident, the way he opened the young man's eyes.

There will come a time when some of us will see things, and God will whisper in our ears, show us, direct our path and reveal things to us. That is one of the spiritual senses being activated, and part of it is having foresight.

But you have to move from milk to meat to tap into that. If you are still caught up in your old sins, you ain't going to be able to see these things. The Lord is in the midst of his people when they gather in his name; it is the ones who have come out of their sins whose eyes he opens to see it.

Moses commanded: “thou shalt read this law before all Israel in their hearing.” In their hearing. “Gather the people together, men, and women, and children, and thy stranger that is within thy gates, that they may hear, and that they may learn, and fear the Lord your God, and observe to do all the words of this law”. Faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God: in hearing we process what we heard, learn from it, and apply it to our life.

So we have to exercise these senses: in what we watch, as Job 31 was pulled up, and in our hearing, what we ingest and listen to. “Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.” What you digest in your vision and your hearing will change the way you think.

That is why the law is read in the hearing of the whole house, even “their children, which have not known any thing”, so that they may hear and learn to fear the Lord. If the ear is filled with the law, it forms the mind in the law; if it is filled with evil communications, it corrupts the manners.

We exercise the physical senses, what we see and what we hear, so we can tap into the spiritual senses we have. Going from milk to meat means training the ear on the word of God and guarding it from everything that would corrupt it.

“In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise.” Wanteth not means it does not lack: where there are many words, sin is never missing. Christ gave the rule for our speech: “But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.” Let your yea be yea and your nay be nay, and everything else is evil.

How many times do you hear it: brother, listen, stop talking. Brother, I am trying to help you, stop talking. You think you are saying something deep, and you are burying yourself. He just cannot stop talking.

Take the brother at work who handed his phone to a girl while the other brother stepped to the back. Asked why, he said it was nothing. Then it was business. What business do you have with her, when we just walked into this place? Nah, it was nothing. Now you are repeating yourself. That is the multitude of words, the over-explaining, and it gave him away. Just by seeing the phone the other brother knew something was not right, and there was more behind it.

That is the ears and the eyes being exercised. Your ears have to be tuned to the subtleties in speech, and a man's face will tell you what is really going on, not what he says. The heart takes what it has seen and heard, processes it and comes to a conclusion; to discern between good and evil you have to be spiritual. Speech reveals the thoughts formed in the heart, so the one who refrains his lips and keeps his yea to yea and his nay to nay is wise.

That is why Paul told Timothy, let no man despise your youth. God chose that man, Timothy, at that point, and he was going to be over some men older than him in age.

It doesn't make the older man less. But don't try to use your age and your worldly wisdom as though it is going to outshine God's wisdom. God is going to choose who he wants and where he wants them in his body, and that is just what it is. Be glad that you are part of this mission, and play your role.

It fits what Sirach 34 says: “The law shall be found perfect without lies: and wisdom is perfection to a faithful mouth.” Wisdom is in the law and the faithful mouth, not in the gray hair. A young man who knows God's laws, keeps them and labors in them, teaching all them that seek learning, is not to be despised because of his youth; and an older man who never learned the law is still an infant, however many years he has.

Sirach says “The law shall be found perfect without lies”, and “A man that hath travelled knoweth many things; and he that hath much experience will declare wisdom.” It is talking about the man that knows the law and travels. Some of you were in the military and traveled, and you don't know nothing. Some of you are old and traveled here and there, and you don't know nothing, only because you don't know the law. Travel and years do not make wisdom without God's laws.

That goes back to Job 32: days should speak, and the multitude of years should show wisdom, but there is a spirit in man. A lot of older brothers who lived from the time of the fifties and sixties amounted to nothing, but they want to be over men. You have to study first. You have to learn God's laws and apply God's laws. They feel because of their age they can be over younger men. No, you are not at that level yet. Spiritually you are not growing; you are still at an infant stage. We don't care if you are eighty years old: if you don't know God's laws, you are an infant, a toddler, according to the word of God.

The understanding does not come from the number of years but from the spirit God puts in a man. Military men who have been to Syria and Iraq don't know what they are looking at, because they are not studied to know what to look for. The man whose years and travels are joined to the law is the one that declares wisdom.

“But be continually with a godly man, whom thou knowest to keep the commandments of the Lord.” Your everyday life should generally be spent around godly people. We have to go out in the world and work, but outside of that, the bulk of your time is with godly men, and if the brothers around you don't have understanding, be around people with more understanding than you so you can level up. How will you know he keeps the commandments? You have to be exercised to discern between good and evil. If you are keeping the commandments, you'll be around godly men, because every beast consorteth with its own kind.

He is one whose mind is according to thy mind, “and will sorrow with thee, if thou shalt miscarry”: he's going to correct you. So how is your mind? It has to be godly. When it says “let the counsel of thine own heart stand: for there is no man more faithful unto thee than it”, that is not for the man who isn't seeking counsel, who is watching porn, whatever he's doing, and then making decisions. You're going to make a mistake. In a multitude of counsel there is safety; the counsel of your own heart stands when it's funneled through the laws of God. “For a man’s mind is sometime wont to tell him more than seven watchmen, that sit above in an high tower”: the seven watchmen are godly men, and your own godly mind can see what's best for you.

“And above all this pray to the most High, that he will direct thy way in truth.” Above the counsel of your own heart, above the counsel of a godly man, you go to God, and he directs your path. But God is not going to hear the prayer of sinners: “If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me.” Your prayer for direction is only heard if your heart is not holding on to iniquity.

“Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” So it's not telling you not to get counsel from brothers. Get counsel, balance it with what you think might be right, with a godly mind, and then go to God and ask him to direct your path.

Sirach says, “And let the counsel of thine own heart stand: for there is no man more faithful unto thee than it.” But the scripture also says, “Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.” At first that seems to be the total opposite. Should we not seek counsel?

In the multitude of counsellors there is safety means that as much counsel as you can get will help you make the right decisions and move in the right direction. That is correct. And the counsel of your own heart can stand only when it is funnelled through the laws of God, through the scriptures. Then you can make your decision and stand on it, because it is based on the laws of God.

Go up to verse 12 and it opens: “But be continually with a godly man, whom thou knowest to keep the commandments of the Lord.” Your everyday life should be spent around godly people, and if you lack understanding, around people with more understanding than you, so you can level up. You know who keeps the commandments by being exercised to discern between good and evil, and every beast consorts with its own kind. Such a man “will sorrow with thee, if thou shalt miscarry”: he will correct you.

So letting the counsel of your own heart stand is not for the man who seeks no counsel and makes his decisions while watching porn. He is going to make a mistake. It is for the man whose mind is godly, like the godly man he took counsel from. “For a man’s mind is sometime wont to tell him more than seven watchmen, that sit above in an high tower.”

“And above all this pray to the most High, that he will direct thy way in truth.” Above your own heart and above the counsel of a friend, you go to God, and God does not hear the prayer of sinners. “Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” So the two scriptures agree: get counsel from the brothers, balance it with what you think is right with a godly mind, then ask God to direct your path.

Isaiah said the people draw near with their mouth and honour God with their lips, “but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men”. The precept of men is the doctrine of men.

Christ says the same thing and names who Isaiah was speaking of: “Ye hypocrites, well did Esaias prophesy of you, saying, This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me. But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.”

The elders in Isaiah's day were teaching doctrines of men, and the Pharisees in Christ's time were doing the exact same thing. Those elders had children, and those children became the opposition of Christ in his time. The same spirit passed down.

So the doctrine of trinitarianism is exactly that: teaching for doctrines the commandments of men. It is not found plainly in the Bible; it comes from men. The priest explaining the sign of the cross as three distinct persons of one essence never opens a Bible. The one scripture he leans on is John 10:30: “I and my Father are one.” That's all he has. But Christ says it again in John 17, and there he tells you what one means.

“And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are.” These are his disciples. If one means one being, one essence, then Christ and the disciples are all one being too. That's not what it's talking about. They are one because they speak the same things, say the same things, in the same spirit.

“Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word; That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us”. “And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one”. That is why they never bring out the Bible. The trinity was argued out over centuries of councils, borrowed from Greek philosophy, confusion upon confusion, and God is not the author of confusion. The Bible is plain: “to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.” Paul warned, “Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit”.

Christ said to men, “Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” The trinity doctrine says no: only God can keep the commandments, so Christ cannot be fully a man, because a full man can't keep those laws, but a full man and a full God can. The scripture also says we are gods but shall die like men, so we are the two anyway; for not keeping the commandments we die like men.
